### R2-ENGINE-402

The item-list constructor (EN `L2.01737`, RU `L2.01738`) runs the base list
constructor, then stores +0x1c = 0x7fff and +0x20 = 0. The item-move
message's ground destination allocates 0x24 bytes and calls the same
constructor (EN `L2.01739`..`L2.01740`).

Methods, RU addresses (EN = RU − 0x9d22; EN bodies were read and found equal only for the constructor, insert, extract, merge and bag I/O; EN insert-at, find, take and list I/O were not read):

| Method | RU | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| insert | `L2.01313` | calls insert-at with index +0x1c |
| insert-at | `L2.01741` | clears item +0x4d; a stackable item (vtable +0x50) whose ID +0x40 equals a stackable entry's adds its quantity +0x42 to that entry, ORs its +0x8 into the entry and is destroyed; otherwise index ≥ count appends, a smaller index inserts before that entry; +0x20 gains +0x4a × +0x42 |
| find | `L2.01742` | first entry whose u16 +0x40 equals the argument |
| extract | `L2.00494` | find; quantity ≤ 1 unlinks the entry, else vtable +0x40 splits one unit off; +0x20 loses weight × quantity of the result |
| take | `L2.01651` | R2-ENGINE-375 pending take |
| merge | `L2.01743` | refuses when the bag count is 0x400 or more; else takes entries from the source list head and inserts each, then destroys the source list |
| I/O | `L2.01166` | R2-SESSION-165 |

Stackability (`L2.01744`, slot +0x50 of Item, Weapon and Armor): type byte
+0x44 equal to 3 or 4, or an empty effect list +0x20. Entry order is list
order. No count or weight test occurs in insert-at; the 1024 test is in
merge only. The bag has no owner field in these bodies; items carry their
owner (R2-ENGINE-403).

One linear pass over each `.text` section found 62 direct calls to seven of
these methods in each locale with equal counts per method: insert 35,
insert-at 4, merge 3, find 5, extract 4, take 8, I/O 3. The population
includes shop, ground and script lists; indirect calls are not counted.

**Confidence.** High for the RU constructor and RU method bodies read, and
for the five EN bodies read (constructor, insert, extract, merge, bag I/O),
which equal their RU bodies after address masking. Medium for EN insert-at,
find, take and list I/O: no EN window was read, and equal EN and RU
direct-call counts show equal call sites, not equal bodies. Medium for the
stackability rule of an item without effects, the 1024 test, the append
position and the saved order: they rest on helpers `L2.01745` (taken as nonzero
for a non-empty effect list), `L2.01746` (taken as the entry count) and
`L2.01747`, none of which has a listing or an earlier claim, and on `L2.01748` as
append, whose role is inferred from its use after an index-against-count
test. The type 3 or 4 stackability rule stays High. Medium that the hero's
+0x7c object is this class: every method read on [+0x7c] is a method of this
class and the bag I/O transfers +0x1c and +0x20, but the store that allocates
the hero's bag was not found. Unknown for a count or weight limit enforced by
a caller outside these bodies.

**Unknown.** The hero bag's allocation site. Searched for a store to Unit
+0x7c: the RU Unit constructor `L2.01273` and RU Humanoid constructor
`L2.01157` (committed listings, no store with displacement 0x7c) and one RU
template-load window (`R2.0089`, a navigation receipt searched with grep,
not committed). Not searched: any EN window, the template parameter routine,
and no `disp:`/`imm:` census of stores with displacement 0x7c. A census of
stores with displacement 0x7c across the Unit constructors and the template
loader in both roots would settle it. Also unknown: the third I/O caller (RU
`L2.01749`) and a limit elsewhere. A save with a nonempty bag would show the
stored +0x1c value.

**Amended.** The Unknown on the allocation site is settled by R2-ENGINE-410: Unit initialization stores +0x7c. A limit in a caller stays Unknown.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2051](../experiments/EXP-2051-rom2-inventory/)

### R2-ENGINE-403

The Item constructor (RU `L2.01750`, factory `L2.01173`, class record
`L2.01163` "Item", vtable `L2.01751`) stores +0x3c = 0, +0x40 = 0,
+0x42 = 1, +0x44..+0x46 = 0, +0xc = 0, +0x4a = 1, +0x8 = 0, +0x4c = 0,
+0x4d = 0, +0x50 = 0 and +0x54 = 0. The EN base constructor `L2.01752`
makes the same stores up to +0x50 and none at +0x54.

| Offset | Width | Use in the read bodies |
|---|---|---|
| +0x08 | u32 | flags; ORed into a merged entry; #pickup all sets 1 |
| +0x0c | u16 | row in the kind's data table; LOAD rebuilds +0x3c from it |
| +0x14 | u32 | owner Player |
| +0x1c | u32 | unit price P read by buy and sell |
| +0x20 | list | Effect objects |
| +0x3c | ptr | row descriptor, not saved |
| +0x40 | u16 | item ID (R2-ENGINE-327 armour form); bag find and stack key |
| +0x42 | u16 | quantity |
| +0x44 | u8 | type (R2-ENGINE-333); 3 and 4 always stack |
| +0x45 | u8 | class: indexes the row's mask words at descriptor +0x1c |
| +0x46 | u8 | material: the bit tested in that word |
| +0x47 | u8 | saved, not interpreted |
| +0x48 | u16 | saved; weapon level (R2-ENGINE-265) |
| +0x4a | s16 | unit weight added to bag +0x20 and to the holder's load |
| +0x4c | u8 | deal reference count (R2-ENGINE-266), not saved |
| +0x4d | u8 | shop category tag, cleared on bag insert, not saved |

Name build EN `L2.01053` parses class and material bytes, finds the row in
the armour (`L2.00808`, 0x6c bytes), weapon (`L2.00807`, 0x88), shield
(`L2.00809`, 0x6c) or magic (`L2.01753`, 0x54, kind 0xe) table and constructs
the item with (class, material, row); the armour constructor `L2.01754`
stores them at +0x45, +0x46 and +0xc. Validity `L2.01054` tests bit
material of descriptor word +0x1c + 2·class. A braced effect string goes
to `L2.01755`: parser `L2.01756` splits it at commas, `L2.01757` builds one
Effect per `name=value` token and appends it to +0x20, then item vtable
+0x4c recomputes the price.

Effect: class record RU `L2.01165` "Effect", size 0x48, factory
`L2.01758`, constructor `L2.00089`, which zeroes +0xe, +0x3c, +0x3d, +0x40,
+0xc and +0x44. +0x3c is the tag, the index of the token's name in a table
of at most 50 names; +0x3d is a flag byte; +0x40 and +0x42 are two u16
values. Tags 41 and 42 store a spell number at +0x40 from `L2.01759`; the
consumer R2-ENGINE-267 reads +0x40 of those tags as a spell key. For tag 41
the writer also stores +0x42 from `L2.01760` (a level, inferred from the
cast constructor argument only: Medium). For tag 42 the writer clears +0x42
or sets it to value<<4 by the flags, and its second word is unnamed. Tags
43..48 use `L2.01761`, `L2.01760` and `L2.01762`. The factories `L2.01173`
and `L2.01758` are navigation-only: their windows are not in the committed
listings, so the addresses and the class records named with them are
Medium.

Item use (Item slot +0x38, RU `L2.01763`): while the holder's HP word
+0x94 is positive, each effect gets +0x3d |= 8 when zero and its vtable
+0x3c with the holder, the holder's vtable +0x5c runs and the item is
destroyed; at HP ≤ 0 the item is returned unused.

**Confidence.** High for constructor stores, offsets, widths and the
effect object layout in the constructors read. Medium for the names class,
material, type, weight and price: they come from use in these bodies and
R2-ENGINE-264, R2-ENGINE-327 and R2-ENGINE-333. Medium for the factory
addresses and for +0x42 of tag 41 as a level. Unknown for the second word
of tag 42, +0x47, +0x50, RU +0x54, +0x0e on items, the tag-name table
contents and the +0x3d flag meanings.

**Unknown.** Reading the effect-name table and `L2.01761`/`L2.01760`/
`L2.01762` would name the tags and their value pairs.

**Amended.** R2-ENGINE-414 names the 50 effect tags, the slot-18 use of +0x40 and the +0x42 reads of slot 14 (duration count) and slot 19 (tag 41 price); +0x42 of tag 42 stays Unknown, as do +0x47, +0x50, RU +0x54 and +0x0e.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2051](../experiments/EXP-2051-rom2-inventory/)

### R2-ENGINE-404

Buy EN `L2.00831` / RU `L2.01764` walks the deal list +0x78 and skips an
item with an owner. For each other item it compares q·P with the money of
the customer's owner ([+0x74]+0x14, the Player of R2-SESSION-145) and
stops at the first it cannot pay. It debits q·P, removes the item from the
deal list (`L2.01765`), stores item +0x14 = the customer's +0x14, item
+0x4c = 0 and inserts the same object into the customer's bag through
`L2.01055` (R2-ENGINE-402): a stackable item can merge into an equal bag
entry and be destroyed. Buy does not equip, copy or rebuild the item and
writes no other item field. It then sends the money and unit updates
(`L2.01052`, `L2.01766`, `L2.01056` with mask 0x282000).

A hero item reaches a deal through the item-move message (R2-ENGINE-405):
source 2 takes n units from the bag at an index with `L2.01646`, the whole
object when its quantity is at most n, else a split of n; destination 4
stores item +0x14 = the unit's +0x14 and passes the item to the shop
(`L2.01767` → `L2.01768`, navigation-only: neither window is in the
committed listings). Sell (R2-ENGINE-266) credits and clears the
owner. Undo `L2.00839` returns each owned pending item to the bag through
`L2.01055` and places the rest through `L2.00804`.

**Confidence.** High for the buy, move-arm and undo bodies, equal in EN and
RU except the undo tail (R2-ENGINE-407). Medium for the hop `L2.01767` →
`L2.01768` and the shop-side accept `L2.01768`, which rest on navigation
receipts and were not read in a committed listing; R2-ENGINE-375 gives the
pending insert. Medium for the stack merge on insert (the helpers named in
R2-ENGINE-402).

**Evidence.** [EXP-2051](../experiments/EXP-2051-rom2-inventory/)

### R2-ENGINE-405

Humanoid initialization zeroes 13 slots +0x208+4i (i = 0..12); the
serializer writes slots 1..12 (R2-ENGINE-208). Worn items are referenced
from +0x74, +0x78 and these slots, not from the bag.

The item-move arm (EN from `L2.01769`, RU from `L2.01770`; equal sequences after
masking except R2-ENGINE-407) reads packet byte +0xc (source), byte +0xd
(destination), word +0xe (source index), word +0x10 (destination index)
and word +0x12 (quantity). Kinds: 1 body, 2 bag, 3 ground, 4 shop.

- Body source index i: i+1 = 1 takes +0x74, 2 takes +0x78, 3..12 takes slot
  i+1 when the unit's vtable +0x30 returns nonzero; each through Human
  vtable +0x48 (RU `L2.01771`: item vtable +0x3c, then return the item).
- Bag source: take at the index and quantity.
- Body destination: bag +0x1c = source index, then Human vtable +0x40
  (`L2.01311`); the item it returns, displaced or refused, is inserted into
  the bag at that index.
- Bag destination: insert-at the destination index. Ground: a new item
  list holding the item. Shop: R2-ENGINE-404.

Equip test `L2.01311` accepts Armor, Weapon and Shield classes when row
parameter 0xf has bit 0 for a holder where `L2.00044` is zero and bit 1 for
one where it is nonzero, then calls item vtable +0x38. Armor +0x38 RU
`L2.01315` refuses slot byte +0x58 = 0 with a message, unequips the slot's
occupant through its vtable +0x3c and returns it, stores the armour, adds
block +0x5a into +0xfe and +0xbe, adds weight +0x4a to the holder's load
and sets holder +0x150 |= 0xc000. Unequip `L2.01772` reverses these.
Weapon +0x38 follows R2-ENGINE-322. Any other class reaches Item use
(R2-ENGINE-403): an item dropped on the body is consumed.

Human vtable RU `L2.00218`: +0x40 `L2.01311`, +0x44 `L2.01310` (+0x40, then
the returned item into the bag), +0x48 `L2.01771`, +0x4c `L2.01773` (slots
1..12 into the own bag), +0x58 recompute `L2.00052`. `L2.01774` moves +0x74,
+0x78 and slots 1..12 into a given list; `L2.01775` takes each item of a
list, equips it and bags the remainder. EN `L2.01776`, `L2.01777` and
`L2.01778` apply, equip with the displaced item to the bag, and unequip,
each followed by the holder's vtable +0x5c.

The bag source arm also handles a tag-41 first effect: unit +0x68 = the
taken item and a cast object at unit +0x44; if it cannot start, the item
returns to the bag at its index and +0x68 = 0.

**Confidence.** High for the move-arm branches and the equip, unequip and
vtable bodies. Medium for the kind names, read from the targets each kind
reaches, for the +0x68 cast use, and for the binding of `L2.00044` to mages
(R2-ENGINE-322). Unknown whether the arm serves town and mission alike:
it tests no location, but its dispatch from each mode was not traced.

**Unknown.** The writer of +0x78; the ground-pickup completion after
source 3 sets bag +0x1c and unit +0x50 = 2.

**Amended.** The town-and-mission dispatch Unknown is narrowed by R2-ENGINE-413: R2-ENGINE-413 reads one dispatcher branch without a map test that reaches this arm; a second 0x22 target in the unread table of the map branch is not excluded (Medium).

**Evidence.** [EXP-2051](../experiments/EXP-2051-rom2-inventory/)

### R2-ENGINE-406

RU producer `L2.00162` tests Player +0x38. When it is set and hero byte
+0x13c is above 0, it calls `L2.01779` (each school-skill experience
×9/10, new total +0x130, skills from experience, new +0x1c0 and +0x1c4
objects, `L2.01780`), sets HP and mana to their maxima, appends the hero
to Player +0x24 and builds a group when +0x70 is null. In either case it
returns the existing hero. None of these bodies touches +0x7c, +0x74,
+0x78 or the slots. Nine callees of the path have no listing (`L2.00205`,
`L2.00349`, `L2.00361`, `L2.01781`, `L2.01782`, `L2.01783`, `L2.01784`, `L2.01785`,
`L2.01780`), so that the hero keeps its own item objects on this path is
Medium.

Map build reuses the existing Player under the conditions of
R2-ENGINE-108. In a mission, ground items reach the bag through the
item-move message and `#pickup all` merges sack lists into it
(R2-ENGINE-301, EN `L2.01064` → `L2.01786`). Victory acknowledgement calls
LeaveLocation and failure offers menu or save selection (R2-ENGINE-074).

**Confidence.** High for the reuse path's stores and calls in the two bodies
read and for the returned identity of the Unit (`L2.01787`..`L2.01788`).
Medium that the hero keeps its item objects on this path (nine callees
unread). Medium that a
mission entry reaches this path, which R2-ENGINE-105 and R2-ENGINE-108
support only conditionally. Unknown whether map unload at a mission's end
keeps or destroys the hero Unit, and whether the town is rebuilt from a
saved document.

**Unknown.** Reading the map unload and the town re-entry, or an owner
save before and after a mission with a marked bag item, would settle the
carry back.

**Amended.** R2-ENGINE-411 shows the departure path skips LOAD; R2-ENGINE-412 finds no write to the hero's bag or worn slots in the transition bodies read, with ten first-loop callees unread (Medium). Ground-item fate stays Medium.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2051](../experiments/EXP-2051-rom2-inventory/)

### R2-ENGINE-407

Eighteen EN/RU listing pairs were compared with addresses and frame
offsets masked. Equal: bag insert, extract and merge, item-list
constructor, unit bag I/O, Unit, Item, Humanoid and Effect serializers,
Effect constructor, shop buy and sell.

- RU items have a runtime dword +0x54 that EN lacks: the RU constructor
  zeroes it, and the EN builders allocate Item 0x54, Armor and Shield 0x6c
  and Weapon 0x88 bytes against RU Item 0x58, Weapon 0x8c (clone
  `L2.01789`) and Armor 0x70 (R2-ENGINE-210).
  Weapon and Armor fields shift by 4: EN slot byte +0x54, armour block
  +0x56, weapon raw blocks +0x56 and +0x6e, weapon reference +0x84; RU
  +0x58, +0x5a, +0x5a and +0x72, +0x88.
- The RU item-move arm stores item +0x54 = 0 after a bag take and after a
  body take; its body-source compare order differs with the same targets.
- RU undo apply adds a unit update (`L2.00060`, mask 0x282000, as buy
  and sell send) after the part equal to EN; the EN undo body ends
  without it.

The serializer bodies compared transfer the same fields in the same order
and widths. An item's whole stream has one layout in both roots at Medium
only: the EN insert-at, find, take, list I/O, effect-list I/O, Effect
reference reader and 38-byte base programme were not read
(R2-SESSION-165).

**Confidence.** High for these differences in the measured bodies; Medium
for the equality of the whole EN and RU stream. No
claim covers unmeasured code. Unknown for the meaning of RU +0x54 and
whether EN sends the undo update from another body.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2051](../experiments/EXP-2051-rom2-inventory/)

### R2-ENGINE-410

Unit initialization (EN `L2.01793`, RU `L2.01794`; 180 instructions,
equal after masking: instruction shape with hex values of six or more
digits masked, callee identity not compared) allocates 0x24 bytes, runs the item-list constructor
(EN `L2.01737`, RU `L2.01738`) and stores the result at +0x7c (EN
`L2.01795`, RU `L2.01796`). It also clears +0x50, +0x54, +0x58, +0x5c,
+0x64, +0x68, +0x70, +0x74, +0x78 and +0x140 and sets +0x136 = 1. The RU
Unit constructor `L2.01273` calls it at `L2.01797`. One linear pass over
each `.text` finds 9 direct calls to initialization and 18 to the item-list
constructor per root; the pattern that stores +0x1c = 0x7fff (one encoding,
`c7401cff7f0000`, register eax only; another register or encoding is
not excluded) occurs once, inside the constructor.

A direct constructor call followed within 0x60 bytes by a store with
displacement 0x7c (EN ↔ RU):

| Call | Containing body | Effect on +0x7c |
|---|---|---|
| `L2.01798` ↔ `L2.01799` | Unit initialization | first bag |
| `L2.01800` ↔ `L2.01801` | transition (R2-ENGINE-412) | a new bag when +0x7c is null, under hero +0x13c > 0 and Session +0x74 ≠ 0 |
| `L2.01802` ↔ `L2.01803` | result tick `L2.00524` ↔ `L2.00127` | a new bag when +0x7c is null, on a respawn at HP ≤ −40 |
| `L2.01804` ↔ `L2.01805` | unit death `L2.01806` ↔ `L2.01807` | old bag destroyed, new bag |
| `L2.01808` ↔ `L2.01809` | unit death | after the old bag is dropped as a ground sack (`L2.01810` ↔ `L2.01811`) |
| `L2.01812` ↔ `L2.01813` | character-file loader `L2.01814` ↔ `L2.01815` | worn items stripped, bag deleted, new bag, refill |
| `L2.01816` ↔ `L2.01817` | character-file loader `L2.01818` ↔ `L2.01819` | new bag |
| `L2.01820` ↔ `L2.01821` | script instant `L2.01822` ↔ `L2.01823` | bag dropped to the ground, new bag |
| `L2.01824` ↔ `L2.01825` | script instant `L2.01826` ↔ `L2.01827` | bag merged into another unit's bag, new bag |

The other nine calls per root have no store to +0x7c within 0x60 bytes;
that proximity rule is the only test applied. The census holds 94 EN and
98 RU stores with displacement 0x7c; nine per root were classified, and
the other 85 EN and 89 RU were not classified by receiver or source. A
store beyond 0x60 bytes or of a constructor result kept in a temporary
would not be found. Only EN `L2.01740` (the item-move ground destination
of R2-ENGINE-405) has a window; the roles of the other eight calls per
root (ground, shop, script or other) are not shown. Unit death first moves
+0x78, then +0x74 when row parameter 0xf is nonzero, then slots 1..12
(Human vtable +0x4c) into the bag. When the template name contains the
string at `L2.00405` or +0x1a0 is set, the bag is destroyed and replaced;
otherwise a nonempty bag goes to the ground sack and a new empty bag
replaces it. LOAD fills the existing +0x7c object (R2-SESSION-165).

**Confidence.** High for the census, the initialization store and the
listed bodies, read in both roots (`unit-init`, `unit-death`, `drop-bag`,
`result-tick`, `script-drop`, `script-merge` and `charfile-server` equal
after masking; `charfile-client` and `transition` differ in local
branches). Medium for the nine role names death, respawn, character file and
script instant, taken from what each body does, and for the 9 of 18
split, which is a proximity-rule result. Unknown for a count or weight
bound in a caller of the bag methods: no census of direct calls to bag
insert and merge was run and no caller was searched; none occurs in these
bodies. That census and a read of each caller would settle it.

**Unknown.** The string at `L2.00405` and the meaning of Unit +0x1a0.

**Amended.** R2-ENGINE-535 states what Unit +0x1a0 does: set, the bag is replaced and no gold or item is rolled (High); the human attacker's experience skips the victim (Medium); the writers are type-6 0x10 bit 8, two unique-spell arms and the map build, and the unit copy omits it (Medium). The grades above stay.

### R2-ENGINE-411

Mission entry (EN `R2.0026`, RU `R2.0023`), called with argument 0 by
the 0x42f, 0x457 and 0x468 message arms, tests app +0x5d4; when it is
set it stores Session +0x1ac = 0 and calls the map caller (EN
`L2.00222`, RU `L2.00112`). The map caller's only LOAD call (EN
`L2.01828` to `L2.00289`) runs when Session +0x1ac is nonzero. Map build
reuses the existing owner under R2-ENGINE-108's conditions and the
producer returns the existing hero (R2-ENGINE-406). After the map loads,
mission entry posts 0x442 with wParam 0, the autosave. The 0x468 arm
calls mission entry on its first branch, after `L2.00175` and `L2.00466`
when a location list is built.

The load entry (EN `L2.00826`, RU `L2.00119`) calls LOAD (`L2.00289`,
RU `R2.0121`) on the save named at app +0x248; it then posts 0x421 when
`L2.01829` returns 0, calls mission entry with argument 1 when `L2.01830`
returns nonzero, and otherwise posts 0x42e (town). Among the bodies read,
LOAD is called only there and in the map caller.

The saved hero address 262270312 is equal in all four frozen saves A to D
(R2-SESSION-169); it does not discriminate between the same object and a
rebuilt one.

**Confidence.** High for the cleared flag, the gated LOAD and the
absence of a LOAD call in mission entry and the 0x42f, 0x457 and 0x468
arms, read in both roots (map caller equal after masking: shape only, callee identity not compared). Medium that
the hero's item objects survive the unread callees of map build and the
producer (R2-ENGINE-406). The saved address gives no support for object
identity; that the hero is the same object rests on the code reading alone
(Medium).

**Evidence.** [EXP-2052](../experiments/EXP-2052-rom2-inventory-mission/)

### R2-ENGINE-412

The 0x41d arm (EN `L2.01831`, RU `L2.01832`) branches on app mode
+0x5d8. Modes 1 and 3 call the transition (EN `L2.01664`, RU `L2.01833`)
and post 0x459. In EN mode 0 posts 0x452 without it; RU mode 0 first tests +0x3f4, +0x3bc
and +0x3c8 (`L2.01834..L2.01835`) and can call `L2.01836` (unread),
skipping the 0x452 post, a branch EN lacks. Other modes call it when
the Session exists and the win flag (EN app +0x3e4, RU +0x3fc) is set,
then post 0x428 or 0x468 or call `L2.00876`. The transition, read in
both roots (RU pushes one more argument before its last call):

1. expires unit effects (+0x42 = 1, vtable +0x38, remove);
2. calls world-clear (EN `L2.01837`, RU `L2.01838`) on Session +0x7c;
3. deletes the map `L2.01066` and the global ground list `L2.01839` and
   zeroes both pointers;
4. removes owners with +0x2c ≠ 0 or a matching name;
5. for each unit of class +0x0e in 0x21..0x3f: HP and mana to maximum,
   +0x13c = 0, reset (EN `L2.01668`, RU `L2.01840`), and +0x5c, +0x64,
   +0x44, +0x68, +0x40 = 0; other units are detached through EN
   `L2.01669` (RU `L2.01841`).

Reset calls `L2.01842` (RU `L2.01843`), which returns an in-progress tag-41
scroll at +0x68 to the bag, destroys a +0x68 item of kind 0xe when +0x136
is 0 and the cast object +0x64, then sets +0x136 = 1 and clears +0x50,
+0x54, +0x58 and +0x64. Steps 1 to 5 and the reset bodies read write none
of +0x7c, +0x74, +0x78 or the slots. The transition's first loop (EN
`L2.01844..L2.01845`), which runs for every owner whose +0x38 unit exists,
is not among the five steps: it calls ten unread functions (EN `L2.01846`,
`L2.01847`, `L2.00830`, `L2.01848`, `L2.01849`, `L2.01850`, `L2.01001`,
`L2.00160`, `L2.01851`, `L2.01852`) with the hero or its owner, and it
stores +0x7c at EN `L2.01853` after the null test of the R2-ENGINE-410
table row. That store creates a bag for a null pointer and does not
replace an existing one, which agrees with that row. No LOAD call occurs
in the bodies read; the 0x41d arm also calls `L2.01424` (0xa5 bytes below
the load entry `L2.00826`), `L2.00876`, `L2.01854`, `L2.00875` and
`L2.01855`, none read, and the delete callees `L2.01856` and `L2.01857`
were not read.

Without the win flag the arm calls fail-cleanup (EN `L2.01858`, RU
`L2.01859`) and posts 0x421. The 0x41e arm does the same. Fail-cleanup
calls the transition only when the mode is 1 or 2, the Session exists
and app +0x404 bit 0 is set. The 0x418 arm builds the save-slot page
(`L2.01860`, mode 1).

**Confidence.** High for the arm structure and steps 1 to 5 as read in both
roots (the arms, fail-cleanup, transition, reset, reset helper, detach and
world-clear read; `arm-418`, `arm-41e`, `reset-callee`, `reset-helper`,
`owner-detach` and `world-clear` equal after masking: instruction shape
with hex values of six or more digits masked, callee identity not
compared; `arm-41d` is not in that statement, RU has a mode-0 branch EN
lacks). Medium that the hero keeps its bag and worn items across the
victory transition and that no LOAD follows: both negatives are bounded
to the bodies read. Medium that ground items are destroyed:
world-clear's list callees and the deletes were not followed. Medium that
the save-slot page restores a hero only through LOAD (R2-ENGINE-074).
Unknown for the meaning of app +0x404 bit 0.

**Unknown.** Reading world-clear's callees (`L2.01861`, `L2.01862`,
`L2.01863`, `L2.01864`, `L2.01865`, `L2.01866`, `L2.01867`) and the writers of app
+0x404 would settle ground-item fate and the defeat gate. Reading the ten
first-loop callees, the delete callees, the 0x41d arm's callees listed
above and RU `L2.01836` would settle whether the hero's items and the
absence of a LOAD hold beyond the bodies read.

**Amended.** R2-ENGINE-529 reads one of the ten first-loop callees listed as unread: `L2.01851`, the party placement routine (R2-ENGINE-529 to R2-ENGINE-531). Nine remain unread. Whether that routine runs in the first loop depends on the +0x74 gate, which R2-SESSION-198 finds 0 in a campaign (Medium).

### R2-ENGINE-413

The server dispatcher (EN `L2.00171`, RU `R2.0119`) has two branches on
packet byte +4. For byte +4 < 1 it indexes opcode byte +9 − 2 through a
byte table (EN `L2.01868`, RU `L2.01869`) into a dword table (EN
`L2.01870`, 32 entries; RU `L2.01871`, 31). Opcode 0x22 reaches the
item-move arm (EN `L2.01769`, RU `L2.01770`; R2-ENGINE-405); opcodes
0x32..0x35 reach shop enter, buy, sell and undo (R2-ENGINE-404). This
branch tests no map pointer. The other branch (byte +4 at least 1) exits
when `L2.01066` is null, otherwise takes opcode byte +9 − 0x12, bounds it
at 0x14 and jumps through a table at EN `L2.01872` (`L2.01873..L2.01874`);
that range includes opcode 0x22. The table was not read and its RU
counterpart was not located. The arm's ground source uses the global list
`L2.01839`.

One client builder (EN `L2.01875`, RU `L2.01876`; equal after masking)
fills record `L2.01877`: +9 = 0x22, +5 owner, +0xa unit [app +0x138] +4,
+0xc source kind, +0xe source index, +0xd destination kind, +0x10
destination index, +0x12 quantity, and sends it through `L2.00871` on
`L2.00872`. A linear `.text` pass finds seven direct calls per root:

| EN call | EN body | RU call | RU body |
|---|---|---|---|
| `L2.01878` | `L2.01879` | `L2.01880` | `L2.01881` |
| `L2.01882` | `L2.01883` | `L2.01884` | `L2.01885` |
| `L2.01886` | `L2.01887` | `L2.01888` | `L2.01889` |
| `L2.01890` | `L2.01887` | `L2.01891` | `L2.01889` |
| `L2.01892` | `L2.01893` | `L2.01894` | `L2.01895` |
| `L2.01896` | `L2.01897` | `L2.01898` | `L2.01899` |
| `L2.01900` | `L2.01901` | `L2.01902` | `L2.01903` |

**Confidence.** High for the dispatch in the byte +4 < 1 branch, the arm
address, the builder record and the direct-call census in both roots
(builder equal after masking: shape only, callee identity not compared).
Medium that this is the only server arm for opcode 0x22: a mission-only
0x22 arm may sit in the unread table of the other branch. Medium that
the town and the mission both reach this arm: no location test occurs in
the dispatcher branch, the arm or the builder, but no runtime was
observed. Indirect calls to the builder are outside the census.

**Unknown.** The entry for opcode 0x22 (and the entries up to 0x12 + 0x14)
in the table at EN `L2.01872` and its RU counterpart; reading the table
and its targets would settle whether a second 0x22 arm exists.

Effect vtable RU `L2.01905`, 20 slots. Slot 18 (`L2.00054`) computes a
value as its argument times s16 +0x40 when flags +0x3d share a bit with

### R2-ENGINE-420

A linear EN `.text` scan for E8 calls (`out/code/en-dll-text-census.tsv`)
lists every direct call of the availability writers:

| Writer | Callers |
|---|---|
| add-mission `D2.00014` | departure IDs 10, 20 (slot 772), 31, 40 (two), 60; TalkTo kind 3 `D2.00138`; Load `D2.00257` |
| add-town `D2.00031` | departure IDs 20 and 50; Load `D2.00258` |
| append `D2.00033` on `D2.00105` | the two add helpers; NewGame `D2.00259` (town 1); the restoration (46 sites: 42 unconditional, four arm alternatives); ID 50 slot 780 (`D2.00256`) |
| clear `D2.00034` on `D2.00105` | NewGame `D2.00260`; restoration `D2.00210`; Load `D2.00261`; the remove helper `D2.00262` when the count reaches zero; the destructor `D2.00263` |
| remove `D2.00022` | type-2 departure (ID 1); ordinary departure (current) |

The other append calls target the catalog in the rebuild, which NewGame
and Load call. EnterLocation stores current only. The exports 14, 16, 17
and 19 return the list, test for an available type-2 record (argument 0:
any town), test for an available type-1 ID, and return the catalog head.
The stage switch `D2.00027..D2.00030` holds no writer call.

The method `D2.00254` appends items read through two unread archive calls
and has no E8 caller; its address occurs once outside `.text`, at `.rdata`
`D2.00255`. Indirect calls were not censused.

**Confidence.** High for the EN direct-call census (one linear `.text` pass,
every hit read in the listed bodies). Medium for the RU census: it is the
navigation receipt `evidence/navigation/nav1-ru-dll-text-census.tsv`,
identical to the EN file after the locale field but not regenerated, and a
navigation receipt carries no High. The pass lists `E8 rel32` calls and

inside another instruction are outside what it classifies. Medium that no
other writer exists: the `.rdata` method and indirect calls remain open.

GetAvailableLocations and GetAllLocations sites walk the lists with the

when GetVar(768) is at least 120 (`L2.01921`); otherwise it builds the
victory dialog with main row 140. The 0x41d arm in campaign mode with the
win flag set (EN `L2.01922..L2.01923`, RU `L2.01924..L2.01925`):

1. runs the transition (R2-ENGINE-412) and calls LeaveLocation with a
   local output;
2. reads slot 773 (`L2.00173`, GetVar(0x305)) and, when nonzero, passes it
   and stage768 to the addition producer (R2-ENGINE-106);
3. calls the movie dispatcher with the output when it is 0 or more;
4. if GetVar(768) is at least 120, posts 0x428 (credits);
5. otherwise, if IsTownAvailable(0) returns 0, calls EnterLocation on the
   first available record and posts 0x468, which enters it;
6. otherwise clears the map route flag and opens the global map
   (`L2.00876`); its selection path calls EnterLocation on the available
   record that passes the map's position test (`L2.01926`).

DLL export 16 returns 1 for argument 0 when any available record has
type 2. In the bodies read, a defeat does not reach LeaveLocation: the 0x41d arm
with the win flag clear (EN `L2.01858` fail-cleanup, then 0x421), the 0x41e
arm and the failure-report close branches of R2-ENGINE-074 (see also
R2-ENGINE-412, R2-ENGINE-421). The mission keeps its place in the list and its completion
slot stays zero. Leaving a town (0x42d) calls LeaveLocation and opens the
map (R2-ENGINE-272).

**Confidence.** High for steps 1..6 in both roots and the export body; the
EN and RU arms differ only in application offsets and RU's mode-0 branch.
EN only for the 0x430 arm. Medium that no other path calls LeaveLocation
after a mission, and Medium for the defeat negative: it covers the three
bodies named above and the call sites of the cell census (R2-ENGINE-421).

**Unknown.** The live dialog, the map's presentation and the 0x430 arm in
RU.

**Amended.** R2-ENGINE-428..R2-ENGINE-434 give the map's presentation,
selection and travel; the position test is point equality with the
target nearest the pointer (R2-ENGINE-431).

**Evidence.** [EXP-2053](../experiments/EXP-2053-rom2-campaign-graph/)

### R2-ENGINE-428

A direct `call rel32` census of each client `.text` lists the open body's
callers: EN `L2.01930` (0x41d arm) and `L2.01931` (0x42d arm), RU
`L2.01932` and `L2.01933`. The open body pushes the map view app+0xf0 on
room stack app+0xcc and calls its slot +0x80, the map enter (EN
`L2.00880`, RU `L2.01934`), which has no direct caller. The map vtable (EN
`L2.01935`, RU `L2.01936`, 34 slots) holds both roots' bodies at the same
slots.

Map+0x1b0 is the mode: the 0x42d arm sets it to 1 for town ID 1
(R2-ENGINE-272) and the 0x41d arm stores 0 before the open
(R2-ENGINE-422). Nonzero is route mode, zero select mode.

The window message body EN `L2.00913` sends 0x200 to slot +0x4c, 0x400 to
+0x50, 0x201..0x206 through the jump table `L2.01937` to +0x54, +0x58,
+0x5c, +0x60, +0x64 and +0x68, 0x100 to +0x6c, 0x101 to +0x70 and 0x102 to
+0x74. The map overrides these input slots:

| Slot | Message | Map body (EN / RU) | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| +0x4c | pointer move | `L2.01938` / `L2.01939` | target the nearest record (R2-ENGINE-431) unless travelling, then set cursor `L2.01940` |
| +0x54 | left down | `L2.01941` / `L2.01942` | start the travel, or skip it when one runs |
| +0x58 | left up | `L2.01943` (EN) | returns 0 |
| +0x60 | right down | `L2.01944` / `L2.01945` | inside the Hero.bmp rectangle at map+0xfc, store a rectangle at map+0x114 |
| +0x64 | right up | `L2.01946` / `L2.01947` | clear map+0x114 |
| +0x6c | key down | `L2.01948` / `L2.01949` | skip a running travel |
| +0x74 | character | `L2.01950` / `L2.01951` | skip a running travel |

No map slot closes the map or returns to a town. The map closes when a travel
ends: EN `L2.01952` sends 0x445 to the map's own slot +0x48, which hands it
to `L2.00782`; that body calls leave slot +0x84 (EN `L2.01953`: map+0x194
= 0, art, sounds and route graph released) and posts 0x44c with the map
pointer. The dispatcher `L2.00782` closes the view on message 0x446 as
on 0x445 when `[this+0x5c]` is nonzero. The EN 0x42d arm window holds an
application arm (`L2.01954..L2.01955`) that sends 0x446 or 0x445 to
app+0xcc by the flag bits of app+0x404; its senders were not read, nor
whether the room-stack top is the map when it runs. Init slot +0x78 (EN `L2.01956`) adds one child, button class
`L2.00901` with ID 4, a zero-size rectangle at (540,450), a caption
shorter than two printable characters, message 0x7fff and no hotkey.

**Confidence.** High for the direct callers, the vtable, the EN message
mapping and every map slot body with an RU listing (slot +0x58 is EN
only). Medium that no other path opens the map: indirect calls were not
censused. Medium that no key, control or message closes it: the
application's own key handling, the senders of 0x446 and 0x445 in the
application arm at `L2.01954` and the zero-size button's paint were not
read, and the RU jump table was not read (the RU dispatcher body is
equal after masking).

**Unknown.** Base bodies EN `L2.01957` (+0x5c, left double click),
`L2.01958` (+0x68) and `L2.01959` (+0x70); what map+0x114 is used for,
since no read paint draws it.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2054](../experiments/EXP-2054-rom2-global-map/)

### R2-ENGINE-429

Map enter calls EN `L2.01960`, which releases old art and loads by
direct path string:

| Field | Resource | Loader | Use in the paint body |
|---|---|---|---|
| +0x68 | `main\graphics\Global.Map\Umoir.bmp` (route) or `GMap.bmp` (select) | BMP `L2.00573` | background at the view origin |
| +0x70 | `graphics\Global.Map\BallMap.bmp` | BMP | route dots |
| +0x74 | `...\Flag1\sprites.16a` | 16a `L2.00639` | frame count for map+0x128; its draw sits in the record loop, which route mode does not reach (R2-ENGINE-430) |
| +0x78 | `...\Flag\sprites.16a` | 16a | party marker, route mode |
| +0x7c | `...\Cross\sprites.16a` | 16a | travel target |
| +0x80 | `...\MissionFlag\sprites.16a` | 16a | pointed record, select mode, no travel |
| +0x84 | `...\FlagOnMap\sprites.16a` | 16a | other records, select mode, no travel |
| +0x88 | `...\YourFlag\sprites.16a` | 16a | party marker, select mode |
| +0x6c | `...\Hero.bmp` | BMP | not drawn; its size sets the right-button rectangle |
| +0x8c..+0xa0 | `Scroll01..03.bmp`, `ScrollP1..3.bmp` | BMP | not drawn by the paint body |

Each .16a load is followed by `L2.00644(16,4,0)`. EN `L2.01961` loads
`SFX\ScrollUp.wav`, `SFX\ScrollDn.wav`, `SFX\Point1.wav` and
`SFX\Point2.wav` into +0x180..+0x18c. The enter also loads
`main\text\globalmap.txt` into the shared text buffer (R2-ENGINE-344) and
builds the route graph (R2-ENGINE-433).

Paint EN `L2.00881` returns until the enter has set map+0x194. It draws
the background, the route dots, the record markers (R2-ENGINE-430), the
travel figure (R2-ENGINE-432), the party marker and, in select mode, the
text block (R2-ENGINE-434), all at the view origin from map+8 plus fixed
offsets. Scroll pieces are drawn only by EN `L2.01962`, called only from
`L2.01963`, which has no direct caller in either `.text`; ScrollUp and
ScrollDn have no use in the bodies read.

**Confidence.** High for the paths, loaders, fields and the paint's draw
calls in both roots. Unknown for palette, transparency and blending: the
BMP and .16a loaders and the sprite draw slot +0x18 were not read.

**Unknown.** Whether Hero.bmp, the scroll pieces or ScrollUp/ScrollDn are
reached by an indirect call; the view origin's value. The backgrounds'
size is R2-ASSET-093.

**Amended.** R2-ENGINE-465 reads the BMP and .16a draw slots, the
shade table and the paint's lock order, settling palette, transparency

### R2-ENGINE-430

The paint body walks the list returned by GetAvailableLocations (client
cell EN `L2.01964`, R2-ENGINE-421, R2-ENGINE-422) and reads each record's
point at record+8 (`L2.01965`). It never reads the catalog list. Offsets
are from the record point; frames advance one per paint.

The record loop (EN `L2.01966..L2.01967`) runs behind the test
`map+0x12c != 0` at `L2.01968`, which jumps past it. Map+0x12c is a
travel's progress (R2-ENGINE-432). In route mode (map+0x1b0 nonzero) the
code at `L2.01969` raises it to 8 unless it is already 8 or more, so it
is nonzero on every paint and the loop, with its Flag1 draw at (x-4,
y-32), is not reached. In select mode the loop runs only while no travel
runs; a travel draws the route dots, Cross and the party marker and no
record marker.

| Mode | Drawn | Sprite and offset | Frame |
|---|---|---|---|
| route | records | nothing (record loop not reached) | |
| select, no travel | record whose point equals the target | MissionFlag at (x-5, y-41) | map+0x128 |
| select, no travel | other records not at the party position | FlagOnMap at (x-5, y-37) | map+0x128 |
| select, no travel | record at the party position | nothing | |
| select, travel | records | nothing | |
| route | party | Flag at (px-10, py-24) | map+0x130 |
| select | party | YourFlag at (px-20, py-44) | map+0x130 |

The party point is map+0x104/+0x108. Map+0x128 cycles modulo the frame
count of Flag1, map+0x130 modulo that of Flag. A record's point is its
catalog x and y (R2-ENGINE-418); each lies on a node of the mode's path
image (R2-ENGINE-433).

**Confidence.** High: the paint body is read whole in both roots (equal
after masking); it holds no other record loop, and the test at
`L2.01968` is the only path to the loop. A completed or not-yet-available record is not
drawn, because only the available list is walked.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2054](../experiments/EXP-2054-rom2-global-map/)

### R2-ENGINE-431

Target body EN `L2.01970` runs on pointer move and on every paint while
no travel runs and no route is held. It converts the pointer to
view-relative coordinates and walks the available list for the least
(dx*dx + dy*dy); a tie keeps the earlier record. There is no distance
limit and no rectangle. The winner's point becomes the target
map+0x10c/+0x110. When the new target differs from the previous target the body
recomputes the route from the party point (R2-ENGINE-433); a target equal
to the party point gives a two-point route. The paint draws the route as
BallMap dots on every eighth route point. It then fetches the record's name and
description (R2-ENGINE-434).

A left-button press with no travel running sets map+0x12c = 8, which
starts the travel to the current target (R2-ENGINE-432). Nothing else
gates it: no confirmation, and a single press suffices (the base
double-click body is unread, R2-ENGINE-428). The pointer body also sets
the cursor object EN `L2.01940`. During a travel the pointer move does
not retarget.

**Confidence.** High for the selection rule, the click and the cursor
call in both roots.

**Unknown.** The cursor image `L2.01940` holds.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2054](../experiments/EXP-2054-rom2-global-map/)

### R2-ENGINE-432

A travel runs while map+0x12c is nonzero. Each paint draws the route dots
up to map+0x12c, draws Cross at (tx-10, ty-12) with frame map+0x134
(held at its last frame), then adds 1 to map+0x134 and 8 to map+0x12c.
While map+0x12c is below the route length the body plays SFX Point1 and
Point2 alternately, starting the other one when the current one is
silent (`L2.01971`, `L2.00941`). The travel ends when map+0x12c exceeds
the route length and map+0x134 exceeds the Cross frame count plus 1.

At the end the party point becomes the target, map+0x12c = 0 and the
route is cleared. The map then closes (R2-ENGINE-428), posts 0x468 to the
application and calls EnterLocation (client cell EN `L2.01972`): in
route mode on the first available record, in select mode on the first
available record whose point equals the target (`L2.01926`). The 0x468
arm enters the location (R2-ENGINE-272). In route mode the paint starts
the travel itself, with the first available record as target.

Skip EN `L2.01973` sets map+0x12c to the route length plus 1 and
map+0x134 to the Cross frame count plus 1, so the next paint ends the
travel. It is called from left down, key down and character. The map
plays no movie.

**Confidence.** High for the sequence in both roots. Medium for the
alternation reading: `L2.01971` and `L2.00941` were not read.

**Unknown.** The paint rate, so the travel's duration; message 0x402
calls slot +0x34 at most once per 100 ms (slot +0x48, EN `L2.01974`), and
whether that drives the paint was not read.

**Amended.** R2-ENGINE-463 reads `L2.01971` and `L2.00941`: the
alternation stands and Point2 sounds first. R2-ENGINE-464 settles the
paint rate and the travel's paint count.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2054](../experiments/EXP-2054-rom2-global-map/)

### R2-ENGINE-433

EN `L2.01975` loads `graphics\Global.Map\UmoirPath.bmp` in route mode and
`PathMap.bmp` in select mode through the 8-bit loader `L2.00583`, whose
picture index is top-origin (R2-ENGINE-233). The graph builder EN
`L2.01976` scans 640x480 pixels at x + 640*y and makes every pixel of
value 2 a node; `L2.01977` traces each node's road from the node and
stores a point list per connected node pair, both directions. Route EN
`L2.01978` finds the nodes equal to the start and end points; equal points
give a two-point route. Search `L2.01979` is a depth-first search over
nodes not yet on the path that keeps the path of least summed list
length. The route is the concatenation of the pair lists.

Node pixels counted in the installed images (`out/map/node-counts.tsv`):
PathMap.bmp 100 (EN and RU, equal SHA256), UmoirPath.bmp 81 (EN). Of the
49 catalog records (R2-ENGINE-418), 47 lie on PathMap nodes in both roots;
town 1 (215,234) and mission 10 (302,158) lie only on UmoirPath nodes (EN
image). Route mode starts at town 1 (R2-ENGINE-272), so its route runs on
UmoirPath. A select-mode start is the party point (R2-SESSION-177); a
start or target at mission 10's point matches no PathMap node.

**Confidence.** High for the loaders, the node rule, the search and the
node match (UmoirPath: EN image only). Medium for the road rule: tracer `L2.01980` was not read, so
which pixel values carry a road (2552 pixels of value 1 in PathMap) is
inferred.

**Unknown.** The search result for a start or target that matches no node:
the read body of `L2.01978` leaves its start index unset in that case
(`L2.01981..L2.01982`), and the party point after a victory is Unknown
(R2-SESSION-177), so whether a select-mode start can be such a point
is not settled.

**Amended.** R2-SESSION-185 settles the party point after a victory:
after mission 20's it is mission 20's point, a PathMap node. The search
result for a point that matches no node stays Unknown.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2054](../experiments/EXP-2054-rom2-global-map/)

### R2-ENGINE-434

Name body EN `L2.01983` formats `#title%d` for record type 1 and
`#town%d` otherwise with the record ID; description body `L2.01984`
formats `#briefing%d` and `#description%d`. Each finds the key in the
loaded `globalmap.txt` and returns the text from two bytes past the key
to the next `#`, or an empty string when the key is absent. The target
body trims two characters from the name and wraps the description with
font `L2.01249` into rectangle (70,48)-(390,200) (`L2.01257`). In select
mode, when the name is not empty, the paint draws the name with font
`L2.01985` at (230,27) and each description line with font `L2.01249` at
(230, 48+10i), the last line less two characters.

The EN and RU files hold the same 92 keys: #title and #briefing for
missions 21, 30..32, 40..43, 50..53, 60..63, 70..77, 80..87, 90..96,
100..103 and 110, and #town and #description for towns 2 and 3
(`out/map/record-nodes.tsv`). Town 1 and missions 10 and 20 have no key
of their own; for town 1 and mission 20 no key begins with theirs, so the
lookup is empty and the paint skips the text block (`L2.01986` tests the
length).

**Confidence.** High for the EN key formats, the lookup and the draw
positions, and for the key sets. Medium for RU key formats: the RU format
strings (`L2.01987`..) were not read; the RU bodies are equal after
masking. Medium for the wrap: `L2.01257` was not read.

**Unknown.** Whether the find `L2.00997` matches a prefix: if it does,
`#title10` finds `#title100`. Mission 10 is drawn only in route mode,
which draws no text.

**Amended.** R2-ENGINE-462 reads the find, settles the prefix Unknown
(a substring search, so `#title10` finds `#title100`) and reads the RU
key formats; the wrap `L2.01257` stays unread.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2054](../experiments/EXP-2054-rom2-global-map/)

### R2-ENGINE-435

`out/code/pairs.tsv` compares 39 EN/RU body pairs with addresses of six or
more hex digits and frame offsets masked: 38 are equal instruction for
instruction; the map open differs in three instructions, the application
flag field +0x404 (RU +0x41c, R2-ENGINE-272). The RU vtable holds the RU
bodies at the EN slots. The 23 resource and text path strings are equal.
`graphics.res` lists the same 17 `global.map/` members at the same offsets
and sizes in both roots, and PathMap.bmp is byte-equal. `main.res`
`gmap.bmp` is 921654 bytes in both, `umoir.bmp` 921656 EN and 921654 RU,
not compared by hash. `globalmap.txt` is 5179 bytes EN and 5403 RU, with
the same keys.

**Confidence.** High for the body pairs, the path strings, the PathMap
hash and the text keys. Medium for the EN `graphics.res` registry
equality and the background sizes: they rest on the EN registry listing, a
navigation receipt (R2-ASSET-093).

**Unknown.** The RU UmoirPath.bmp node set (not read) and the pixel
equality of the backgrounds.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2054](../experiments/EXP-2054-rom2-global-map/)

### R2-ENGINE-462

Name body EN `L2.01983` (RU `L2.02241`) empties its output string
(`L2.02242`, RU `L2.02243`), formats `#title%d` for record type 1 and
`#town%d` otherwise, and calls Find EN `L2.00997` (RU `L2.01289`) on the
loaded text. Find calls EN `L2.01457` (RU `L2.02244`). With the multibyte
flag EN `L2.02245` zero it calls `strstr` EN `L2.01080` (RU `L2.01081`);
otherwise it compares the key at each character position, advancing one
multibyte character at a time (`L2.02246`). Both branches return the
first occurrence of the key as a substring, in buffer order. On a hit the
name runs from the hit + key length + 2 to the next `#`; on a miss the
name stays empty, and the paint skips the text block (`L2.01986` tests
the length, R2-ENGINE-434). The description body uses the same Find
(R2-ENGINE-434). The format strings read are:

| Root | Strings | Values |
|---|---|---|
| EN | `L2.02247`..`L2.02248` | `#title%d`, `#town%d`, `#briefing%d`, `#description%d` |
| RU | `L2.01987`..`L2.02249` | `#title%d`, `#town%d`, `#briefing%d`, `#description%d` |

Over the 92 keys of both files (R2-ENGINE-434), `#title10` and
`#briefing10` occur first inside `#title100` and `#briefing100`, so a
mission 10 name and description would begin inside mission 100's section;
mission 10 is shown only in route mode, which draws no text. `#title20`, `#briefing20`,
`#town1` and `#description1` occur in no key, so town 1 and mission 20
show no text.

**Confidence.** High for the bodies, the formats in both roots and the
first-occurrence rule. Medium for the key consequences: the key lists
count `#` at line starts, and whether a key string also occurs inside a
text line was not searched.

**Unknown.** The wrap `L2.01257`.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2058](../experiments/EXP-2058-rom2-map-presentation/RESULTS.md)

### R2-ENGINE-463

Bind EN `L2.01961` (RU `L2.02250`) loads `SFX\ScrollUp.wav`,
`SFX\ScrollDn.wav`, `SFX\Point1.wav` and `SFX\Point2.wav` into map+0x180,
+0x184, +0x188 and +0x18c through `L2.00980`; the names are equal in both
roots. The enter sets map+0x190 to 0.

After a travel's step (R2-ENGINE-464) the paint, while map+0x12c is below
the count `L2.02240` of the route list at map+0xe0, tests the slot at
map+0x188 + 4*map+0x190 with `L2.01971`, which returns whether
`L2.00976` gives a channel for it. With none, it toggles map+0x190 between
0 and 1 and calls `L2.00941` on the new slot. `L2.00941` starts the sound
through `L2.02166` with the global `L2.02251` only when `L2.00976` gives no
channel. So Point2 starts first, and each later start is the other sound
after the current one has no channel.

No other body read starts a map sound. Pointer move EN `L2.01938` and
hover `L2.02252` set the cursor `L2.01940` through `L2.00587`; the target
body `L2.01970`, left down `L2.01941` (map+0x12c = 8 or nothing) and the
travel end start none. Not read here: the route builder EN `L2.01978`
(called from `L2.01970` at `L2.02253` and from the paint at `L2.02254`),
the arrival EN `L2.01952` (called from the paint at `L2.02255`) and the
skip EN `L2.01973` (called from `L2.02256`); EXP-2054 listings read them
as navigation only. The leave EN `L2.01953` calls `L2.02257`, which
releases all four slots through `L2.00981`: it calls `L2.00982` on a
channel `L2.00976` returns, clears the channel's +8 and deletes the sound.
No dword reference to the scroll draw EN `L2.01962` or its caller
`L2.01963` exists in EN `.text` and `.rdata`, nor to RU `L2.02258` or
`L2.02259` in RU `.text`, and no read body uses +0x180 or +0x184 except
bind and release.

Map music is R2-ENGINE-335, R2-ENGINE-337 and R2-ENGINE-338: the map open
EN `L2.00876` (RU `L2.00877`), when the music word EN `L2.00878` is set,
sets a one-entry list of `music\map.wav` (EN `L2.02260`, RU `L2.02261`)
and starts it, and the mission end EN `L2.01424` (RU `L2.02262`) stops
music; both bodies were read whole in both roots.

**Confidence.** High for the slots, the toggle, the call order and the
absence of a start in the bodies listed, in both roots. Medium that no
other body starts a sound (the word "only"), for the arrival, the
retarget and the skip: their bodies and the scroll draw are unread, and
the dword census cannot see a `call rel32`. Medium that a
sound plays once: `L2.02166` and `L2.00976` were not read, so play-once
and channel-playing are inferred from the toggle. Medium that the leave
silences a playing sound: `L2.00982` was not read.

**Unknown.** Starts in the unread bodies `L2.01978`, `L2.01952`,
`L2.01973`, the scroll draw `L2.01962` and its caller `L2.01963`, and
starts reached through a call outside the bodies read. One window per
root for each body and one `.text` rel32 `call` scan per root for
`L2.00941`, `L2.02166` and `L2.00980` would settle them. The audible
overlap at a toggle needs the play body `L2.02166` (one window per root).

**Evidence.** [EXP-2058](../experiments/EXP-2058-rom2-map-presentation/RESULTS.md)

### R2-ENGINE-464

The application idle body EN `L2.01222` (RU `L2.01223`; its address is a
`.rdata` dword at EN `L2.02263`) returns 1. Unless application+0x5d8 (RU +0x63c) is 3 with the static EN `L2.00805`
(RU `L2.01317`) nonzero, which skips the rest (EN `L2.02264..L2.02265`,
to `L2.02266`), and when application+0x404 bit 0
(RU +0x41c) is clear and application+0xbc is nonzero, it sends 0x402 to
the view stack application+0xcc through slot +0x48; the stack offers it
to its children in order and stops at the first child that returns
nonzero (EN `L2.00915`, RU `L2.02267`). Map slot +0x48 EN
`L2.01974` (RU `L2.02268`) sets a static stamp EN `L2.02269` to
timeGetTime − 100 on its first call. On 0x402, when the unsigned
difference timeGetTime − stamp is at least 100, it calls slot +0x34 and
then stores a fresh timeGetTime in the stamp. Missed intervals are not
repeated. timeGetTime is the WINMM import at EN `L2.02270`, RU
`L2.02271`. Slot +0x34 EN `L2.02272` (RU `L2.02273`) calls the paint
+0x2c and the present +0x38 unless its own test of flag 0x20 is set or
EN `L2.00624` (RU `L2.02274`) is nonzero.

Each paint draws the route to map+0x12c and Cross with frame
min(map+0x134, frames − 1), then adds 1 to map+0x134 and 8 to map+0x12c
(R2-ENGINE-432). The enter sets map+0x134 to 0; left down sets map+0x12c
to 8. The travel ends on the paint where map+0x12c exceeds the value of
`L2.02239` on the route list at map+0xe0 and map+0x134 exceeds the Cross
frame count plus 1, 14 (R2-ASSET-109). After paint n, map+0x12c = 8 + 8n
and map+0x134 = n, so, if `L2.02239` and `L2.02240` both return the
point count L, the end is paint max(15, floor((L − 8)/8) + 1). Paints 13
onward show frame 12. The EXP-2054 skip listing sets map+0x12c = L + 1
and map+0x134 = 14; this experiment holds no window of it.

**Confidence.** High for the idle send with its early exit, the 100 ms
gate, the stamp rule and the paint's counters, in both roots. Medium for
the paint-count formula: `L2.02239` and `L2.02240` are unread and may
differ by one. Medium for the wall-clock rate: seven other `push 0x402` sites per root (EN `L2.02275`,
`L2.02276`, `L2.02277`, `L2.02278`, `L2.02279`, `L2.02280`, `L2.02281`)
were not read, and a parent's child paint (EN `L2.00579`) also calls the
map's +0x2c; another paint source would shorten the travel.

**Unknown.** The bodies `L2.02239` and `L2.02240` (one window per root
each), which settle the paint count; the time a paint takes, which adds
to each interval (a timed run); the lengths of the routes the shipped
records produce (one read of the route builder `L2.01978` per root and
the records).

**Evidence.** [EXP-2058](../experiments/EXP-2058-rom2-map-presentation/RESULTS.md)

### R2-ENGINE-465

Paint EN `L2.00881` (RU `L2.00882`) locks the surface with `L2.02282`,
draws, unlocks with `L2.02283` and then calls the child paint `L2.00579`.
The draw slots, read in both roots through the class tables:

| Object | Class table EN / RU | Slot | Wrapper EN / RU | Body EN / RU | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| background +0x68 | `L2.00574` / `L2.02284` | +0x18 | `L2.00575` / `L2.02285` | `L2.00576` / `L2.02286` | opaque copy of the converted 16-bit picture |
| BallMap +0x70 | `L2.00574` / `L2.02284` | +0x38 | `L2.00704` / `L2.02287` | `L2.00705` / `L2.02288` | copy that skips converted word 0 |
| .16a sprites | `L2.00640` / `L2.02289` | +0x18 | `L2.00641` / `L2.02290` | `L2.00642` / `L2.02291` | word-run painter |

The BMP loader `L2.00573` converts the 24-bit picture to the device
format when it loads. The sprite wrapper passes palette row 0
(`L2.02292(0)`, the table base; row n is base + 512n). The table is built

(R2-ENGINE-429): 16 rows of mode 4, whose per-pixel blend R2-ASSET-059
and R2-ASSET-066 give.

Draw order: background; in select mode with no travel the route preview
dots and the record flags (R2-ENGINE-430); during a travel the route dots
and Cross (R2-ENGINE-432); the party flag, Flag in route mode and YourFlag
in select mode; the text block in select mode (R2-ENGINE-434); unlock;
child paint.

**Confidence.** High: every slot, wrapper and body in the table is read in
both roots and equal after masking.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2058](../experiments/EXP-2058-rom2-map-presentation/RESULTS.md)

### R2-ENGINE-436

The main menu is the view the 0x421 arm shows (EN `L2.01994`, RU
`L2.01995`) when application flags +0x404 (RU +0x41c) are zero. Its
mouse body EN `L2.01996` reads the MenuMask.bmp pixel at x + 640*y
(R2-ASSET-097), subtracts 0x80 and maps the result through the byte
table EN `L2.01997` (113 cells, `out/code/tables.tsv`): cells 0x00,
0x10 .. 0x70 give buttons 0..7 and every other cell gives 8, no button.
The result is the hover index +0xec. A press stores the hover index in
+0xf4; the release stores it in +0xf0 only when the release lands on
the pressed button. The mouse body clears the drawn image +0xd8 when
the hovered button's bit in byte +0xf8 is set.

The release body EN `L2.01097` / RU `L2.01998` dispatches +0xf0
through the 8-entry jump table EN `L2.01999` and skips index i when bit
(1 << i) of +0xf8 is set. R2-ENGINE-437 names the posted messages. The
two release bodies are equal instruction for instruction (110 of 110,
`out/code/pairs.tsv`).

**Confidence.** High for the mask rule, the press and release match and
the disable test (EN). Medium for the RU index order: the RU jump table
was not read; the RU body is equal to EN. Medium for the screen
position of a mask box: the hit test reads x + 640*y, and the row order
of the loaded surface is unread (R2-ASSET-097).

**Unknown.** Which keys act on the main menu: the read windows hold no
key handler, and the menu vtable slot that would receive keys (the
release is reached from slot `L2.02000`) was not read.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2055](../experiments/EXP-2055-rom2-menu-load/)

| 1 | 0x426 | sets mode +0x5d8 to 0 and shows view app+0x370 (EN `L2.02001`, RU `L2.02002`) | no name (Unknown) |

| 7 | 0x10 | WM_CLOSE | Exit |

### R2-ENGINE-439

Load Ok with a selection copies the row label to app+0x148 and the file
name to app+0x248 and closes the page with 0x445; Ok with no selection
and Cancel close it with 0x446. The view-close body (EN `L2.00787`,
page branch EN `L2.02033` / RU `L2.02034`) posts 0x419 on 0x445.
Otherwise it posts 0x421, the main menu, when no session exists
([EN `L2.00805`] zero), and 0x41e when app+0x43c (RU +0x454) is 0xff.

Arm 0x419 (EN `L2.02035`) leads to the load entry EN `L2.00826` / RU
`L2.00119`: it sets mode 2 and loads app+0x248 through the session
object [EN `L2.00805`] (EN `L2.00289`). When EN `L2.01829` returns 0 it
posts 0x421; for a mission it calls EN `R2.0026(1)`; otherwise it posts
0x42e, the town entry.

A save without `Bsg&` at offset 0 never reaches the load path: the page
does not list it (R2-ENGINE-438). A listed file whose blob is unreadable
is handled by the session load and EN `L2.01829`, not by the page.

**Confidence.** High for the Ok and Cancel routing and the 0x419 entry
(EN). Medium for the RU page-close routing: the pair compared 121 RU
instructions against a differently cut 129-instruction EN window
(R2-ENGINE-443). Medium for the failure branch: what EN `L2.01829` tests was not read,
read here as the load result.

**Unknown.** The page close in a session when app+0x43c is not 0xff.
What a listed file with a valid magic and a damaged body shows.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2055](../experiments/EXP-2055-rom2-menu-load/)

### R2-ENGINE-440

Arm 0x41a (EN `L2.02036`, RU `L2.02037`) acts only when app+0x404 is 0
or 1. It creates a 0x9c-byte page, constructor EN `L2.02038` / RU
`L2.02039` (called only from this arm in EN), with the load page's
geometry, vtable EN `L2.02040` / RU `L2.02041`, +0x98 = dialogs row 28
`<<< Empty Slot >>>`, stored at app+0x140.

The init (slot 30, EN `L2.02042` / RU `R2.0165`) draws row 29 at
(40,32), a name box (EN `L2.02043`, id 1) at (40,68) with prompt row
30, row 144 at (40,104) and a list (id 3) at (40,128) with 10 rows and
header row 31. Row 0 is the Empty Slot; the other rows come from the
enumerator in mode 0 with the load page's Bsg& rule and order.

The init converts four characters of each listed file's name, read as
name characters 4..7 (offsets 0..3 of the pointer plus 4 that call EN
`L2.02044` returns; the callee is unread), with inline arithmetic
`(c - 0x30) * weight`, weights 1000, 100, 10 and 1 (EN `L2.02045`
.. `L2.02046`). It sorts the numbers with qsort and comparator EN
`L2.02047` (unread) and picks the smallest unused number from 0, or 0
with no file. It formats the Empty Slot's name with
`game000%ld.sav`, `game00%ld.sav`, `game0%ld.sav` or `game%ld.sav`, a
four-digit `gameNNNN.sav` for numbers below 10000. Buttons: Ok (id 4,
0x479, tip row 32), Delete (id 6, 0x475, tip row 158), Cancel (id 5,
0x47a, tip row 33).

The command body (slot 18, EN `L2.02048` / RU `L2.02049`): selecting a
row puts its label in the name box (row 0 gives an empty box). Ok, when
id 4 is enabled, copies the box text to the label app+0x148; when a
compare (call EN `L2.02024`, unread, so its case rule is Unknown) finds
the text equal to the label of a row i >= 1 it selects row i; it copies that row's file name to app+0x248 and closes with 0x445.
No confirmation precedes an overwrite in the read body. Delete acts on
rows i >= 1 with the load page's confirmation. On 0x445 the page close
(EN `L2.02033`) calls the save driver EN `L2.00860` / RU `R2.0166`.
By R2-ENGINE-271 the driver appends the 256-byte label to app+0x248
only when app+0x5d8 is 2 (Medium there) and otherwise sends the name in
a type-7 record without a label. The driver was not read here, and the
save page runs for app+0x404 of 0 or 1 in any mode.

**Confidence.** High for the layout rows, the file name format and the
absence of an overwrite confirmation in the read command body. Medium
for the selection rule (compare unread), the exclusion of game9998 and
game9999 (compare unread), the number sort (comparator unread), the
bindings of 0x479, 0x475 and 0x47a to Ok, Delete and Cancel (the EN
tables `L2.02050` and `L2.02051` and the RU tables are unread; read
from the arm contents) and the label write (mode 2). The enable rule
of Ok (EN `L2.02052`) was not read.

**Unknown.** When Ok is disabled (for example an empty name). Sounds.
Reads that would settle the Medium clauses: EN `L2.02024`, `L2.02047`,
`L2.02044`, `L2.02014`, `L2.02015`, the command tables, driver
`L2.00860`.
Where a mission save reaches this page: the 0x41f menu posts 0x41a
(R2-ENGINE-441), and the 0x404 values a mission sets were not read.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2055](../experiments/EXP-2055-rom2-menu-load/)

### R2-ENGINE-444

Item description EN `L2.02139` (RU `L2.02140`), the tag 41 and 42 arms of
R2-ENGINE-267, formats `spell.txt` line value-1 between `main.txt` lines
0x5a/0x5b (cast spell) or 0x5c/0x5d (taught spell) with `" %s %s%s"` or
`"#%s %s%s"`. The spell list EN `L2.02141` (RU near `L2.02142`, approximate) walks
bits 0..31 of a mask at object +0x1c and appends `spell.txt` line b-1 for
each set bit b, separated by `", "` with `",#"` as a periodic line break;
`main.txt` line 192 is `Spells: ` (R2-ASSET-103). Spell row r and mask bit
r therefore show line r-1.

The spellbook (EN class at `L2.02143`, RU `L2.02144`) has 24 slots drawn as
a 12 by 2 grid at a 38-pixel pitch from slot mod 12 and slot div 12; a slot
whose bit is clear in the hero masks +0x148 or +0x150 gets a cover sprite.
The hover EN `L2.02145` (RU `L2.02146`, approximate) takes slot s from the cursor
(`L2.02147`), requires bit s of +0x148 and a per-slot mana cost +0x2d4
below 0xffff, and formats `"%s#%s: %d"` from `spells.txt` line s,
`main.txt` 117 and that cost. Further `"#%s: ..."` lines use `main.txt`
118 (damage from +0x154/+0x1b4), 123, 124, 182..187 and 217 with further
per-slot arrays.

The 24 dwords at EN `L2.02137` (RU `L2.02148`) are, for slots 0..23: 1, 2,
3, 4, 24, 20, 21, 26, 13, 12, 11, 10, 5, 6, 7, 8, 25, 22, 23, 27, 19, 18,
17, 16. The values are read from the binary. That each value is the
data.bin row whose name matches the slot's `spells.txt` line is Medium: it
rests on the `spells.txt` name order, which is not committed, and on the
fit that the 24 values are distinct and equal rows 1..29 without 9, 14, 15,
28 and 29. Rows 9 (Acid Stream), 14 (Darkness), 15 (Light), 28
(Curse) and 29 (Slow) have no slot and no hover line. The 'A' key handler
EN `L2.02149` reads this table when the per-slot flag table EN `L2.02150`
admits the slot. A slot click calls EN `L2.02151` with slot+1 when the flag
table EN `L2.02152` admits it.

**Confidence.** High for the item and list text selections, the grid, the
hover text lines and the table values, in both roots. Medium that the table
entries are spell rows (the slot-to-row binding), which rests on the
uncommitted `spells.txt` name order (R2-ASSET-103) and on the unread
consumer EN `L2.02136` of the 'A' key handler. Medium that the hover's
per-slot arrays are filled through this table: their filler was not read.

**Unknown.** The writer of the hover's per-slot arrays, the text of
`main.txt` line 217 in the hover, the order of the `spells.txt` names as a
committed list and the consumer EN `L2.02136` of the 'A' key handler.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2056](../experiments/EXP-2056-rom2-spell-presentation/)

Server senders EN `L2.02153`/`L2.02154` (RU `L2.02155`/`L2.02156`) write

+0xa/+0xb when the caster word +0xe is zero; +0xc = 2*row+8
(`lea ecx,[eax+eax+8]`), +0xd the target key or cell, +0xf the argument.

non-unit caster) with a target list.

type count with a type in the map EN `L2.02134` creates a 0x158-byte effect
object at the cell centre (cell*256+128), with lifetime +0xa8 = argument.
Any other identifier reaches the caster arm: an idle caster whose unit type
has +0x1c set enters state 8 for unit-type +0x68 updates and stores the
identifier at +0xac; its target is its own position without a type, the
target key with Homing, else the cell centre. The chain arm stores 30 at

| 2 Fire Ball | 12 fireball | 13 fireexpl |

### R2-ENGINE-447

The effect update EN `L2.02165` (RU `L2.02167`) increments counter +0x9c,
switches on ID-13 (byte table EN `L2.02168`, jump table `L2.02169`), then
decrements lifetime +0xa8; at lifetime 0 the effect ends. Frame +0x74:

| IDs | Update arm |
|---|---|
| default | moves toward the target, frame (counter/2) mod Phases |
| 13 | default frame; at counter 4 adds the 3x3 cells around it to a world list, at counter 8 sets tile bit 0x2000 on them |
| 23 | frame = counter |
| 28, 30 | for counter 1..13 frame 4, 3, 2, 1, 0, 1, 2, 1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 |
| 54 | frame = counter-1 |
| 16, 20, 24, 34, 44, 46, 48, 50, 62, 64, 66 | follows the target unit; frame = counter; adds mark (ID<<16) or 0xffff to unit +0x130 |
| 56, 60 | follows the target unit; sets or adds mark (ID<<16) or 0x20 |

The draw EN `L2.02170` centres the sprite by Width/2 and Height/2 and
switches on ID-7 (byte table `L2.02171`, jump table `L2.02172`). Default:
direction = (facing-8) and 15; Flip mirrors directions above 8 as 16-d;
frame index = Phases*direction + frame, or frame when RotationPhases is 1.
A type with Palette draws through the sprite's own palette path plus a
second draw from `L2.02173`; without Palette it uses palette object EN
`L2.02174`. The lazy loader EN `L2.02175` prepares a palette type's sprite
palette through EN `L2.00644` with (16, 4, 0) for `.16a` and (16, 2, 1)
for both `.256` sprites; the two projectile palettes get (16, 2, 0) through
EN `L2.00645`. IDs 10 and 12 keep their last six positions and draw trail
sprite 0 or 1 of the array EN `L2.02176` at each, with frame = position
index; the array is filled by a two-pass loop formatting the unread key
string EN `L2.02177`. ID 23 draws frame 8 lifted 28-4*frame pixels while
frame < 8, then frame-8. IDs 28 and 30 draw type 28 or 30 sprites at each
point of list +0x11c, chains adding 5 times the point's byte 6 to the
frame. ID 54 draws its frame directly. ID 56 draws nothing itself. Units
draw overlays from projectile types listed at unit +0x11c (EN `L2.02178`).

For row 7 the cell effect lives 16 updates (argument 16): a falling piece
for 8 updates, then shatter frames 0..7 (R2-ENGINE-394).

**Confidence.** High for the switch tables, counter arithmetic, frame
sequences, direction and Flip rule in both roots. Medium for the tile-mark
and unit-mark meanings and for the trail sprite keys (`smoke0` and `smoke1`
match the two passes and six frames, R2-ASSET-101). Unknown for the update
period in seconds and the link from unit marks +0x130 to overlays +0x11c.

**Unknown.** The update rate; the trail key string; the overlay list filler;
what the palette preparation arguments select, including any translucency.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2056](../experiments/EXP-2056-rom2-spell-presentation/)

### R2-ENGINE-448

The effect method EN `L2.02138` (RU `L2.02179`) switches on ID-10 (byte
table EN `L2.02180`, jump table `L2.02181`). Writer EN `L2.02182` (RU
`L2.02183`) stores a byte value into the world byte map at world +0xa8
(row width map width + 7) and counts the writes at +0x108. R is an
argument of the call. A cell is admitted when a word of the table EN
`L2.02184` (stride 0x52, row dy+0x14) is below R*(R+1), or below 1 for
R 0; that table is unread, and the committed listing ends at `L2.02185`
while the function runs to `L2.02186`, so the footprint shape is not
known. Only the writer tests flag EN `L2.02187` (at `L2.02188`); the
lightning and chain arm `L2.02189..L2.02190` stores its bytes inline
without that test. When flag EN `L2.02191` is clear the writer also
invalidates the area.

| ID | Radius R | Value |
|---|---|---|
| 10, 18, 40 | 0 | 16 |
| 12 | 1 | 16 |
| 13, frame 0 | 1 | 16 |
| 13, frame 1 | 2 | 8 |
| 13, frames 2, 3 and above 10 | 3 | 0 |
| 13, frames 4..10 (table `L2.02192`) | 3 | 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 46, 46 |
| 28, 30 | 2 by 2 cells at each list point | frame*10 |

Every other identifier only invalidates a 5 by 5 cell area when
`L2.02191` is clear. Rows: 1 (10),
2 (12, 13), 5 (18), 10 (28), 11 (30), 16 (40). Light (row 15) and Darkness
(row 14) have no effect type; their effect is the sight change of

**Confidence.** High for the arms, the radius arguments and the values in

site writes the map: no census of the callers of `L2.02182` or of the
stores to world +0xa8 was made, and the navigation scans that located the
code exceeded their budget. Medium that the map is the ground light map and that a lower value is brighter:
the Fire Ball blast grows from 16 to 0 and fades to 46, and lightning
reaches 0 at its middle frame, and structure registries carry
`LightRadius` and `LightPulse` keys. Unknown for the map's reader, the
flag's setting and durations in seconds.

**Unknown.** The light-map reader and blend, the option behind `L2.02187`,
and whether unit marks light units. The cell footprint of the writer: the
contents of the table `L2.02184` and the tail of `L2.02182` after
`L2.02185`. The other callers of `L2.02182` and the other stores to the

### R2-ENGINE-449

Byte-equal in EN and RU: `projectiles.reg`, `sfx.reg`, the 29 projectile
`.16a` payloads, the 33 magic WAV payloads, the client `data.bin` payload
(SHA256 `aa9952354f1cbc4329528dff49ed4a6d9c875877b3ce22fe2a1c48b12d3b84d6`),
the slot-to-row table and four of the five per-slot flag tables. The eight
effect switch tables have equal index bytes in both roots; RU jump targets
are the EN targets plus 0x5473. The read senders, client arms, item
description, spell list, hover and effect methods match in structure,
constants and offsets.

Different: `spell.txt`, `spells.txt` and `main.txt` text bytes
(R2-ASSET-103), and the per-slot flag table EN `L2.02150`, RU `L2.02196`,
whose slots 16 (Summon) and 22 (Wall of Earth) are 1 in EN and 0 in RU. That
table gates the 'A' key handler of R2-ENGINE-444.

**Confidence.** High for data equality and the table values. Medium for
code parity: the routines were compared by structure, constants and
offsets, not as equal bytes.

**Unknown.** The player-visible effect of the flag-table difference.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2056](../experiments/EXP-2056-rom2-spell-presentation/)

### R2-ENGINE-452

Client data.bin rows 5 and 16 equal row 1 in every stored value except Sphere
(R2-ASSET-107). Their apply-table cells (`L2.00069` + 4*id) name the blank
default `L2.00085`, which positive cached damage bypasses for the common suffix
`L2.01690` (R2-ENGINE-390). The apply head `L2.00034` builds a 0x60-byte damage
object (`L2.02071`) when base + spread > 0 and the id is not 24 or 26. The
sphere switch maps Sphere 2 to setter `L2.00096` (damage kind 2) and Sphere 4
to `L2.00098` (kind 4); the resolver's kind switch at `L2.01701` reads
resistance word +0xc6 for kind 2 and +0xca for kind 4 (R2-ENGINE-028).

Distribution 1 builds the single-target object `L2.02072` (vtable `L2.02073`;
+0x48 target unit, +0x4c payload), which applies its payload once through
payload vtable+0x3c and runs the hostility bookkeeping `L2.02074`. Delivery 2
wraps it in the projectile `L2.02075` (vtable `L2.02076`); +0x50 is a countdown
of distance over Effect Speed, and the tick `L2.02077` registers the carried
object at zero. Only ids 10 and 11 set their own countdown (10) and a cast
delay of 5. Rows 1, 5, 10 and 16 therefore share one route, and the hit lands
on the bound target unit only. The Effects strings of rows 5 and 16 are empty,
so no effect is attached.

**Confidence.** High for the dispatch cells (both roots) and for the damage
kinds, single-target and projectile route in RU: committed reproduced listings
of this experiment and EXP-2049. Medium for the absence of a row-5 or row-16
test elsewhere: the search covers the apply head, unique arms, delivery
objects, spell object and cast routine read here and the resolver, which tests
only ids 20 and 28 through the mask routines `L2.00042`/`L2.00043`
(navigation; id 12 is tested in other routines, R2-ENGINE-454).

**Unknown.** The EN damage-kind setters, delivery objects and resolver were
not read; reading the EN counterparts of `L2.00096`, `L2.00098`, `L2.02072`
and `L2.02075` would settle EN parity. The presentation of the two projectiles:
the projectile tick `L2.02077` and the Effect Speed fields were read; no
sprite, sound or animation consumer of the projectile object was searched, and
reading the projectile's draw method (vtable `L2.02076`) would settle it.

### R2-ENGINE-453

Arm `L2.00076` allocates a 0x48-byte effect and builds it with
`L2.00086(row Effects string)`, then ORs the timed flag byte `[L2.01906]` into

2*18+8 = 44 to +0xe, and continues at the common suffix `L2.01690` as a

The build `L2.00087` finds the first `=` (0x3d; `L2.02078..L2.02079`) and takes
the text before it as the key, trims the key with `L2.02080` and `L2.02081`,

in the 50-name table of R2-ENGINE-414. The stored row-18 key is `"absorbtion`
with a leading quote byte 0x22; no name carries that byte, the lookup returns
no tag, and the build leaves the effect blank (tag 0, magnitude 0). The value
piece is searched for a comma only later (`L2.02083`) and is not reached. Tag-switch cell 0 at `L2.01909` jumps to
`L2.02084`.

**Confidence.** High for the arm, the flags, the id stamp and the stored key:
committed reproduced listings and data rows. Medium for the blank outcome: the
comparator chain and trims are navigation listings, the final compare
`L2.02085` was not read, `L2.02086` is presumed a whitespace test, and
`L2.02084` was not read.

**Unknown.** Whether tag 0 runs any code after `L2.02084`. Searched: the
tag-switch cell 0 and its target address only; the body at `L2.02084` was not
read. A 0x40-byte window at `L2.02084` in the RU image would settle it.

### R2-ENGINE-454

Attach (effect vtable `L2.01905` slot 15, `L2.00480`): when the target already
holds an effect with the same spell id, the existing object is kept (`L2.02087..L2.02088`):
it runs its slot 17, takes the larger magnitude and the larger duration, and
runs slot 16 again; the new object is not joined. Otherwise the copy runs
slot 16, joins the unit's list +0x20 and sets bit id of the actor mask +0x144. Timer (slot 14, `L2.00482`): a duration above 0x2580 never counts down;
otherwise each tick decrements it and at zero runs slot 17, removes the effect
and clears the bit.

The actor dispatcher `L2.00506` installs primary command 4 when mask & 0x40000
is set and primary +9 is zero; its primary-4 arm sets actor state 27 and keeps
command 4 while the bit stays set (R2-ENGINE-399). While a primary command is
nonzero the dispatcher skips its move, attack and cast switch, so the target
stops acting until the timer clears bit 18. An already active primary command
is not replaced. State 27 also has five other writers.

The RU `.text` holds 31 dword immediates 0x00040000 and no 0xfffbffff (the EN
`.text` holds 30, R2-ENGINE-459). Of the 31, 15 were read in a committed
window: the dispatcher (2), the effect core (5), the computer Stone Curse
choice `L2.02089`, which skips a victim with the bit, target scoring
`L2.02090`, which adds 0x7f to a victim with the bit, and six in the
mask-read windows; ORs into +0x150 are presentation dirty flags. Sixteen were
not classified: `L2.02091`, `L2.02092`, `L2.02093`, `L2.02094`, `L2.02095`,
`L2.02096` and ten `mov [reg+disp], 0x40000` stores. The mask-test calls
`L2.00042`/`L2.00043` have six call sites in three routines with literal ids
12 (`L2.02097`, `L2.02098`), 20 (`L2.02099`, `L2.02100`) and 28 (`L2.02101`,
`L2.02102`); the hit resolver `L2.00101` tests 20 and 28 only. "Damage taken
is unchanged" is the result of those three routines and the 15 read
immediates; it does not cover the 16 unclassified ones.

**Confidence.** Medium, all in RU. The effect core and the computer choice are
committed reproduced listings; the dispatcher is an EXP-2050 listing; the
dword scans, mask reads, call sites and target score are navigation listings.
The EN effect core, dispatcher and readers were not read (Unknown).
Unknown for appearance.

**Unknown.** The EN effect core and dispatcher: the EN counterparts of
`L2.00480`, `L2.00482` and `L2.00506`, located from the EN bit-18 hits
(R2-ENGINE-459), would settle it. The 16 unclassified immediates: a window
around each would settle whether any reads the bit as damage input. The
petrified appearance and any presentation message: searched only the mask
readers above; the presentation dirty flags at +0x150 were not followed to a
draw routine, and reading that routine would settle it. The seconds per timer
tick: the timer decrements per call; the caller of slot 14 and the game clock
rate were not read, and reading that caller, or an owner run of the original
