### R2-ENGINE-455

Arm `L2.00082` (RU): the owner is the caster's Player (+0x14). The arm first
walks the global unit list `[L2.02103]+4` (`L2.02104..L2.02105`) for a dead
unit (kind byte +0x13c >= 5); RU also requires that unit's vtable+0x30 to
return zero (R2-ENGINE-459). Without one it builds a 0x208-byte unit
(`L2.01273`); the unit is given the Player afterwards. A roll `L2.00092(3)` picks Squirrel,
Turtle or Foot_Animated (1, 2, 3); the level of R2-ENGINE-026 above 1 appends
`.` and the digit, so `.5` is never produced although Units holds it
(R2-ASSET-107). The built name is passed to `L2.01794`; its window (0xff bytes)
only zeroes and allocates unit fields and never reads its stack argument, so
that the name selects a Units row is inferred from the call signature and is not
read. +0x1a0 is set to 1 and +0x148 to the caster's +4.

Placement `L2.00313(x, y, 6)` takes the caster's cell: 20 random tries at
offsets -3..3 (the bound is 19 and the counter runs from 0 while it is at most
19), then a scan of the 7 by 7 square; a candidate must pass the cell tests
`L2.01700` and `L2.02106`, which were not read. Both loops also reject a
candidate whose byte value is below 12 while the flag `[[L2.01317]+0x74]` is
nonzero (`L2.02107..L2.02108`, `L2.02109..L2.02110`); what the value and the
flag mean was not read (Unknown). Failure aborts the cast. The unit joins a new group under the caster's Player.

**Confidence.** High for the roll, names, level suffix, owner, reuse loop and
placement call: committed reproduced listings in both roots. Medium for the
binding of the built name to a Units row and for the search order, from the
placement listing and the template window (navigation). Unknown for leaving.

**Unknown.** When or whether the creature leaves: searched the RU `.text` for
the dword `0x1a0`, 68 hits, none classified, and no timer or death rule was
found. Classifying the 68 hits, or reading the group-removal routine, would
settle it; so would an owner run of the original that casts Summon and waits
for the creature to go. The binding of the name to a Units row and the template
statistics: reading `L2.01794` past its 0xff-byte window would settle
them.

**Amended.** R2-ENGINE-535 states what +0x1a0 does: no bag or gold drop at death, no experience to a human attacker (Medium), and the unit copy omits it (Medium). When the creature leaves stays Unknown. The grades above stay.

**Unknown.** The EN table and callers: the EN counterpart of `L2.02111`, found

### R2-ENGINE-470

The refill message is built by EN `L2.02197` / RU `L2.02198`: kind byte
0x3f at +9, the two arguments at +0xa and +0xe and the client's word at +5,
sent through EN `L2.00871` / RU `L2.00459`. A pattern pass over each
`.text` for `c6 ?? 09 3f` finds that store once per root, inside the
builder. A call-target pass finds two callers per root:

| Site | EN | RU | Branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x468 arm | `L2.02199` | `L2.02200` | current location type not 1, before the town dispatcher |
| load entry | `L2.02201` | `L2.02202` | `L2.01830` zero (not a mission), before posting 0x42e |

New Game's campaign start EN `L2.01084` creates the server in mode 2 and
calls neither the builder nor the fill. Server case 0x3f (EN `L2.00824`,
RU `L2.02203`) leaves when server +0x74 is nonzero, else calls owner
refill EN `L2.00825` / RU `L2.02204` on the static owner EN `L2.00822` / RU
`L2.02205`. The EN `.text` holds no dword equal to the builder, owner
refill, fill, shop entry or owner entry address.

The 0x468 arm is the travel-end handler (R2-ENGINE-432). The mission-end
arm 0x41d calls EnterLocation and posts 0x468 directly only when
IsTownAvailable(0) returns 0; otherwise it opens the map, whose travel ends
in 0x468 (R2-ENGINE-422, R2-ENGINE-473). The arm sends no refill itself;
the 0x468 it posts or the map's travel end does. A 0x468 arrival at a
mission (type 1) takes the mission entry and sends no refill.
The load entry is R2-ENGINE-439's path for a load from the load page.

**Confidence.** High for the builder, both callers, the 0x3f case and the
New Game body: committed listings in EN (this experiment, EXP-2032,
EXP-2052) and RU (this experiment, EXP-2052). Medium for the sender set:
the passes see direct `E8` calls and one store encoding; a call through a
register or a table (no RU pointer pass, no `.rdata` pass) or a kind byte
written another way would escape them. Medium that a campaign keeps +0x74
zero (R2-ENGINE-334).

**Unknown.** Senders of 0x3f outside the direct-call census. Pointer scans
of `.rdata` and `.data` for the builder address in both roots, and an
immediate scan of each `.text` for `3f` stored at `+9` including SIB
encodings, would settle it; none was run.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2059](../experiments/EXP-2059-rom2-shop-stock/)

### R2-ENGINE-471

Fill EN `L2.00803` / RU `L2.01640` returns without change while the
open-deal count shop+4 is above 0. Otherwise it empties the four category
lists (`L2.02206`), takes the record from ordinal 15 (R2-ENGINE-263), which
indexes the record by the ID of Scenario's current location `D2.00007` at
that moment, and draws each of the four categories (R2-ENGINE-265). It
draws no category alone and adds nothing to a kept list.

The call-target pass finds three fill callers per root: owner refill
(message 0x3f, R2-ENGINE-470), shop entry EN `L2.00823` (call `L2.02207`,
RU call `L2.02208`) when category 0's list is empty, and pending refill EN
`L2.00829` (call `L2.02209`, RU call `L2.02210`) when counter shop+8 is
above 0. The tick EN `L2.00828` raises shop+8, every 180 ticks, and only
while server +0x74 is nonzero; other writers of shop+8 were not enumerated.
Shop leave calls the pending refill.

In a single-player campaign the draws therefore happen at a town arrival
through 0x468, at a load in a town, and at a shop entry with category 0
empty. A mission's end, an arrival at a mission, time spent in the shop and
a shop leave draw nothing.

**Confidence.** High for the EN fill, entry, pending-refill and tick bodies
(EXP-2032 listings) and the three callers in both roots (call-target
scans); the RU fill is equal after normalization. RU entry, leave, tick and
pending-refill bodies were not read: Unknown. Medium for the campaign event
list: it composes the sender set of R2-ENGINE-470 and +0x74 = 0 of
R2-ENGINE-334, and the shop+8 writers were not enumerated beyond these
bodies.

**Unknown.** Other writers of shop+8. A scan of each `.text` for stores at
displacement `+8` on the shop object would settle it; none was run.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2059](../experiments/EXP-2059-rom2-shop-stock/)

### R2-ENGINE-472

Owner lookup EN `L2.01846` / RU `L2.02211`, which server case 0x32 uses to
find the shop owner for a customer, returns the static owner (EN
`L2.00822`, RU `L2.02205`) whenever server +0x1a4 is nonzero; otherwise it
searches the server's owner list by ID and type. The server constructor
stores +0x1a4 = 1 (EN `L2.02212`); the routine ending at EN `L2.02213`
stores +0x1a4 = (+0x74 == 0) (EN `L2.02214`). With +0x74 zero both give 1,
so shop entry and refill 0x3f act on one shop object. The static
initializer builds the static owner once (EN `L2.02215` calls `L2.01632`;
RU `L2.02216`) and a registered exit routine destroys it.

The shop object holds no town: its constructors (EN `L2.01636`,
`L2.02217`) store the open-deal count, the pending counter, the category
tags 1..4, +0x90 = 1000 and +0x94, and the fill writes only the lists and
item tags. Arriving in a town redraws all four categories from that town's
record (R2-ENGINE-471). Returning to the first town redraws it again; the
stock seen there before does not come back.

**Confidence.** High for the lookup in both roots, the EN constructor and
setter stores and the shop constructors. Medium for the composed campaign
result: two pattern passes over EN `.text` for stores at displacement
0x1a4 found these two server stores and 23 other hits (7 frame stores that
only match the bytes, 6 word stores, 10 dword stores on other bases, not
read); RU writers of +0x1a4 were not read.

**Unknown.** The ten EN dword stores to displacement 0x1a4 on other bases,
at `L2.02218`, `L2.02219`, `L2.02220`, `L2.02221`, `L2.02222`,
`L2.02223`, `L2.02224`, `L2.02225`, `L2.02226` and `L2.02227`
(listed in `evidence/navigation/nav3/scans/en-store-imm-1a4.tsv` and
`en-store-reg-1a4.tsv`). A disassembly window at each, naming the base
object, would settle whether any writes the server's `+0x1a4`.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2059](../experiments/EXP-2059-rom2-shop-stock/)

### R2-ENGINE-473

Departure writes (R2-ENGINE-330), the stage maxima included, run inside
LeaveLocation, which the mission-end arm 0x41d calls (EN `L2.01911`)
before it calls EnterLocation and posts 0x468 (EN `L2.01920`,
`L2.02228`), or before it opens the map, whose travel ends in 0x468
(R2-ENGINE-432). The direct EnterLocation and 0x468 post run only when
IsTownAvailable(0) returns 0 (R2-ENGINE-422); otherwise the map opens and
the travel's end posts 0x468. Either way the arrival's refill reads the
written record, as it runs after LeaveLocation; an arrival at a mission
draws nothing, and the change waits for the next town arrival.

The druid inn TalkTo write (R2-ENGINE-331) happens in town 3 after the
arrival's draw. It reaches the shelves at the next fill while town 3 is
current: the next arrival in town 3, a load of a save made in town 3 (the
record is saved, R2-SESSION-156), or a shop entry with category 0 empty.
It does not reach them at once.

**Confidence.** High for the order inside the 0x41d arm (EXP-2052 listing).
Medium for the result: it composes R2-ENGINE-470 and R2-ENGINE-471, and the
map path depends on 0x468 being handled after EnterLocation returns.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2059](../experiments/EXP-2059-rom2-shop-stock/)

### R2-ENGINE-474

A sold item enters a category list through `L2.00804` (R2-ENGINE-333).
Shop entry keeps the lists while category 0 is not empty, and leave
removes only quantity-0 entries with no deal reference (R2-ENGINE-266),
so the sold item stays through entries and leaves. The next fill empties
all four lists, so the item is gone after the next town arrival, the next
load in a town, or an entry with category 0 empty. When the player buys
every category-0 entry, leave removes the quantity-0 placeholders and the
next entry draws all four categories again.

**Confidence.** High for the EN bodies (sell, buy, entry, leave). RU
bodies were not read: Unknown. Medium for the event set, which is
R2-ENGINE-471's.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2059](../experiments/EXP-2059-rom2-shop-stock/)

### R2-ENGINE-475

With absolute addresses masked, these pairs read in both roots are equal
instruction for instruction: the refill builder (27), the owner lookup (37)
and the static owner wrappers (19). The server 0x3f case (9) and 0x32 case
(42, to the owner entry call) differ only in the frame offset of the server
pointer (EN -0xd1c, RU -0xd00). Of the EXP-2052 listings, the 0x468 arm (64)
differs only in frame offsets and the load entry (94) only in
application-field offsets (+0x3ec/+0x5d8/+0x460 in EN, +0x404/+0x63c/+0x478
in RU). The 0x41d arm differs in register allocation and length (191 EN, 207

EnterLocation (`L2.02229`), post 0x468 (`L2.02230`), else map open. The fill
is equal after normalization (EXP-2032). The call-target and pattern passes
give the same two builder callers and one kind store per root.

The mask rule is every address at or above 0x400000; the one differing
constant outside frame and field offsets is an exception-state value in the
0x468 arm (0x22 EN, 0x23 RU).

**Confidence.** High for the bodies named, by the masked comparison of
committed listings. Unknown for the RU +0x1a4 writers, the RU New Game
start, the RU shop constructors, the RU shop vtable and the RU shop entry,
leave, 180-tick, pending-refill and sell bodies, which were read in EN
only; reading them in RU would settle it.

### R2-ENGINE-477

The resolver `L2.00101` is virtual +0x54 of the Human table `L2.00218` and
of the table `L2.02314`, whose +0x30 cell returns 0 and whose +0x64 cell is
the creature award of R2-ENGINE-480; it runs on the target. It takes a 0x18-byte
attack block and the attacker. It returns 0 for a null block or a target
whose byte +0x4c has bit 8. Block word +0 is the attack value A. The roll is
r = U[0,200] - 100, where U[0,n] is `(rand15 x (n+1)) >> 15` from
`R2.0021`, 0 for n = 0, and rand15 is the 15-bit output of the linear
generator `L2.01699` (multiplier 214013, increment 2531011, bits 16..30).
With d the target's word +0xbe (defence, R2-ENGINE-321):

- A + r > d, or the attacker's byte +0x4c has bit 0x10: the physical part
  hits;
- otherwise r >= 90 hits (11 of the 201 values of r);
- every other blow misses and the physical part is 0.

The strike dispatcher `L2.02315` sends a target whose virtual +0x2c is
nonzero to the unit strike `L2.02313` and else one whose +0x34 is nonzero to
the structure strike `L2.02316`. The structure strike requires an attacker
with an owner and health above 0 within range, then calls `L2.01703` on the
structure with the attacker's block. That resolver returns 0 unless the
block is not null and the structure's word +0x44 is nonzero; it computes
v = block +0x13 + U[0,+0x14] when +0x14 > 0, else 0, then v - 5, and returns
0 when that is not positive. It takes no roll and reads no physical byte of
the block. The strike subtracts the result from the structure's word +0x42
(R2-ENGINE-393) and pays no experience. A weapon's block bytes +0x13/+0x14
come from the weapon's bytes copied at equip (R2-ENGINE-479), so a weapon
whose copied bytes are zero deals a structure 0.

**Confidence.** High for the roll, the comparison and the three hit cases,
and for the structure route, in both roots: committed listings reproduced
from the Git blobs, RU read in full and EN equal after address masking with
the immediates 0xc8, 0x64, 0x5a and 5 compared (R2-ENGINE-482). The
generator body was read in RU only: Medium for its EN arithmetic. The state
address `L2.02317` returns was not read.

**Unknown.** Whether another routine damages a structure by a weapon blow:
no census of +0x42 writers was run.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2060](../experiments/EXP-2060-rom2-physical-combat/)

### R2-ENGINE-478

The resolver reads block bytes +0xe (base B) and +0xf (spread S):

1. When B has bit 7 and the attacker's virtual +0x30 returns 0 (the
   creature table's `L2.02318`; the Human table's `L2.02319` returns 1),
   B = (B & 0x7f) x 15 and S = S x 15 (R2-ENGINE-483).
2. Bless (effect 20) and Curse (effect 28) on the attacker follow
   R2-ENGINE-028: when the effect's magnitude exceeds U[0,100], Bless makes
   v = B + S and Curse v = B without a draw. Otherwise v = B + U[0,S].
3. On a hit (R2-ENGINE-477): v minus the target's absorption word +0xc0,
   skipped when the attacker has flag 0x10, floored at 0. Then, when the
   target's byte at +0xce + block byte +0x10 (the attack type) is a nonzero
   a, v = trunc(v(100-a)/100 + 0.75), with no floor after the cut.
4. Block bytes +0x11 (base) and +0x12 (spread) add B2 + U[0,S2] on every
   call, with no hit test, cut by word +0xc6 in the same form when it is
   nonzero and floored at 0.
5. The magic part, bytes +0x13/+0x14/+0x15 (R2-ENGINE-028), is admitted
   only when A + r > d or block bytes +0xe and +0xf are both 0; a hit by
   r >= 90 or by flag 0x10 does not admit it.
6. A sum at or below 0 returns 0.

The unit strike and the damage object (`L2.01702`) subtract the result from
health word +0x94 with no clamp. The truncation helper `L2.01309` stores
with rounding set to chop. RU constants: 100.0 at `L2.01307`, 0.75 at
`L2.02320`. After the parts, when the attacker's +0x3c is nonzero, the
target stores the attacker at +0x40 (0 when the attacker has no owner) and
the block's kind byte at +0x48 when the predicate `L2.00044` holds, else 0;
the hostility bookkeeping of R2-ENGINE-482 follows.

**Confidence.** High for steps 1 to 6 in RU and for the arithmetic shape in
EN (R2-ENGINE-482). Medium in EN for the constant values, which were read in
RU only.

**Unknown.** Which bytes fill a creature's +0xce array and its attack type
+0x10 (R2-ENGINE-483), and what the human +0xce array holds; reading the
writers of +0xce..+0xd3 would settle it.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2060](../experiments/EXP-2060-rom2-physical-combat/)

### R2-ENGINE-479

Recompute (`L2.00052`, R2-ENGINE-321) writes the human's attack block at
+0xa6, with Body +0x84 and Reaction +0x86 (R2-ENGINE-021):

- spread +0xb5 = trunc(1.1^Body / 20), and base +0xb4 = the same value;
- attack value +0xa6 = trunc((1.1^Body + 1.1^Reaction) / 5);
- the school skills are restored, clamped to 0..100 and given their +0xe8
  modifiers (R2-ENGINE-320);
- when the attack type t = byte +0xb6 is above 0: +0xa6 += 3 x skill[t] and
  +0xb4 += skill[t] / 5 (integer), skill[t] being word +0xa8 + 2t;
- bytes +0xb7..+0xba are zeroed. The fold `L2.00102` of R2-ENGINE-321 then
  adds the record block +0xe6 into +0xa6 through `L2.02321`, which adds word
  +0 and bytes +0xe, +0xf, +0x11, +0x12, +0x13 and +0x14 (the rest of
  `L2.02321` was not read).

`1.1^x` is `L2.00109`, which pushes 1.1 and calls the library power routine
`L2.02322` (not read). Divisors: 5.0 at `L2.02323`, 20.0 at `L2.02324`.

Weapon equip `L2.01314` (R2-ENGINE-322) reads weapon parameter 5 as t. For t
below 10 it adds the weapon's toHit word +0x5a to +0xe6, base byte +0x68 and
spread byte +0x69 to +0xf4/+0xf5 (block +0xe/+0xf) and defence word +0x72 to
+0xfe, stores the weapon's bytes +0x6d..+0x6f into +0xf9..+0xfb (block
+0x13..+0x15) and writes +0xb6 = t. For t 11 or 12 it adds base and spread
to +0xf9/+0xfa with kind 1 or 2 into +0xfb; for every t of 10 or more it
writes +0xe6 = word +0xa8 and +0xb6 = 0. Then recompute runs. The weapon
fill `L2.02311` derives these from the Weapons row (R2-ASSET-111) and two
class records chosen by item bytes +0x45 and +0x46: base =
trunc(physicalMin x f + 0.5), spread = trunc(physicalMax x f - base + 0.5),
with f the product of the records' doubles at +0x40; toHit with +0x48,
defence with +0x50 and parameter 3 (weight) with +0x38, each + 0.5; range
byte +0x58 = the row's range, 1 when -1. 0.5 is the double at `L2.02325`.

**Confidence.** High in RU for the stores, operands and constants listed.
Medium for every term containing 1.1^x: R2-ENGINE-290 and R2-ENGINE-320 give
E(s) = trunc((1.1^s - 1) x 1000) and R2-ENGINE-321 the recompute arithmetic
by instruction shape with its helpers (`L2.00109`, `L2.01309`) unread, so none
of them establishes `L2.02322` as pow(1.1, x) in RU. Medium for every term
that passes through the fold tail of `L2.02321` past `L2.02326` (unread),
where the magic kind byte would be carried. Medium in EN for the recompute
section, equal after masking with its constants unread. Unknown in EN for the
weapon fill, equip and fold, which were not located.

**Unknown.** The body of `L2.02322`; the fold tail of `L2.02321`; the
class-record doubles per item byte value; the binding of BareHands (Weapons
row 1, attack type 3) to an unarmed human; the EN fill, equip and fold.
Reading `L2.02322` and the fold tail would settle the RU terms; reading the
EN counterparts of `L2.02311` and `L2.01314` would settle EN.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2060](../experiments/EXP-2060-rom2-physical-combat/)

### R2-ENGINE-480

The unit strike calls the attacker's virtual +0x6c (`L2.02327`) with the
target, the damage D and spell 0 when D > 0, the target had health above 0
before the blow and has health above -10 after it. A blow that takes the
target to -10 or lower pays nothing. `L2.02327` requires the victim's owner
+0x14 to have +0x2c nonzero and calls the award (+0x64, `L2.00055`) with
X = trunc(V x 0.5 x D / H + 1.0), V the victim's dword +0x1c, H its HPmax
word +0x96. With a nonzero spell it returns unless the predicate `L2.00044`
holds, and then passes parameter 2 of the spell's row as the skill. The
damage object `L2.01702` calls the same +0x6c with its spell id when that id
and its source are nonzero. The virtual +0x68 (`L2.02328`) awards
trunc(V x 0.5) and counts the victim's kind word +0x14c in the attacker's
list +0x1a8: a found kind adds 0x10000 to its entry, a new kind is
appended, and at five entries the first is removed before appending.

The award, for attacker type word +0xe in 0x21..0x3f and a victim without
+0x1a0:

1. X = trunc(X x (Mind/30 + 0.25)), Mind word +0x88 (R2-ENGINE-021).
2. If the victim's kind is in the list with count n (high word):
   X = 10X / (n + 10).
3. Unless the victim's health is below 0: no award when the victim's owner
   is the attacker's, the attacker has no owner, or the diplomacy byte of
   the two owners has bit value 2 set.
4. School skills are reset to their base words +0x116 + 2i.
5. When `L2.00044` holds, the skill s is the passed spell skill and must be
   above 0; otherwise the passed skill must be 0 and s = attack type +0xb6,
   above 0. Skill s must be below 100.
6. If s is neither the main skill +0x23c nor 5: X = ceil(X / 8).
7. With L the base level of s: X = min(X, T(L+1) - T(L)) (`L2.02329`; the
   difference is divided by 5 when global +0x74 is nonzero), T the dword
   table at `L2.02330`, index capped at 149.
8. E(s) at +0x23c + 4s and the sum +0x130 grow by X (R2-ENGINE-320). When
   E(s) reaches T(L+1), s rises by 1 and recompute (virtual +0x58) runs;
   otherwise the skills are restored as recompute restores them.

A creature attacker's +0x64 (`L2.02331`) adds X to its +0x130 and, when the
victim's health is below 0, adds 1 to its owner's +0xa48. A human victim's V
is trunc(0.01 x the sum of its skill experience) (R2-ENGINE-320).

**Confidence.** High for the arithmetic, gates and stores of the bodies read
in RU, except the repeated-victim list; RU constants 0.5 at `L2.02325`, 1.0
at `L2.00067`, 30.0 at `L2.00066` and 0.25 at `L2.02332`. EN bodies are
equal after masking: Medium in EN for the constants. Medium for the
repeated-victim list (count, index, remove and append): its roles are
inferred from the call shape of `L2.02333`, `L2.02334`, `L2.02335` and
`L2.01545`, none read. The predicate `L2.00044` returns actor byte +0x4c & 4
(read in RU, High, R2-ENGINE-362); that this byte is the mage class is
Medium (R2-ENGINE-362; R2-ENGINE-021 and R2-ENGINE-322 name it), so the
headline clause "a mage's weapon hit pays none" is Medium and rests on
R2-ENGINE-362. Medium for +0x68 as the kill award: two byte-pattern scans
over RU `.text` for calls through virtual slot +0x68 (`ff 52 68` 85 matches,
`ff 50 68` 189 matches; receipts under `evidence/navigation/scans/`) were
read but no match was classified. Medium for T: the table lies in
uninitialized `.data` and its writer was not read.

**Unknown.** The callers of +0x68: the two scans returned 274 matches in
all (many are slot-0x68 calls of other classes and `push eax; push 0x68`
sequences), none classified; a call-target pass keyed on the Human class slot
or a triage of the 274 matches would settle it. The roles of `L2.02333`,
`L2.02334`, `L2.02335` and `L2.01545`; the creature V; a creature
attacker's +0x6c; the writer of `L2.02330`; spell row parameter 2's title.
Reading those four routines, the writer of `L2.02330` and the creature row
reader past `L2.02336` would settle these.

**Amended.** R2-ENGINE-485 reads the writer of T: `L2.02342` fills `L2.02330` with
trunc((1.1^L - 1) x 1000) for L 0..149. R2-ENGINE-487 identifies spell row
parameter 2 as the Sphere (Medium; R2-ENGINE-019 gives the column order and
R2-ENGINE-028 ties the damage kind to the Sphere column). The other clauses and grades stand.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2060](../experiments/EXP-2060-rom2-physical-combat/)

### R2-ENGINE-481

In the actor update (RU `L2.02337`), state 3 calls the strike
`L2.02315(attacker, attacker +0x5c)`, except that an attacker whose weapon
+0x74 has a cast object (+0x88 nonzero, `L2.02338`) and for which
`L2.00044` holds stores the object at +0x64, the weapon at +0x68 and enters
state 13.

The unit strike requires the target and its owner, the attacker and its
owner, attacker health above 0, and range byte +0x12c at least the distance
`L2.02339`. The distance is the larger absolute axis difference of the two
positions minus ((size1 + size2) x 128 - 256); at or below 0x180 it is 1,
else (d + 0x40) >> 8. The strike then calls the target's virtual +0x54
(R2-ENGINE-477, R2-ENGINE-478) with block +0xa6 and subtracts the result
from health +0x94 in the same call. Its body calls no object constructor:
melee and ranged weapons share it, and the damage lands when the strike
runs. When the attacker's weapon has a cast object and the predicate
`L2.01517` (not read) admits the attacker, the object is cast through
`L2.00035` on a blow with damage above 0 that leaves the target above 0
health, and on any blow
when the object's byte +8 is 2. `L2.00035` passes the object to the apply
head `L2.00034` (R2-ENGINE-452) unless its byte +8 is 11. Weapon equip adds
range - 1 to +0x12c (R2-ENGINE-322); R2-ASSET-111 gives the ranges.

**Confidence.** High for the bodies read in RU, which show that the strike
body `L2.02313` calls no object constructor and subtracts the damage in the
same call. Medium that a ranged blow creates no projectile object: the body
also calls the notification `L2.02340` with the target and the damage (not
read), the actor update before `L2.02337` (what runs on entering state 3) was
not read, and pointer tables were not searched for callers of `L2.02315`.
Medium for the cast-object clause: the predicate `L2.01517` was not read.
Medium that this strike is the only weapon-damage route: a call-target pass
over RU `.text` found one call of `L2.02315` (navigation), and pointer-table
routes were not searched. Medium for the distance units: the position,
absolute-value and size helpers were not read.

**Unknown.** Whether a ranged blow creates a projectile object, picture or
sound, which may come from the notification `L2.02340` (not read) or from the
actor update before `L2.02337`; what counts the attack time before state 3
strikes; the predicate `L2.01517`; the EN caller. Reading `L2.02340`, the
actor update before `L2.02337` and a pointer-table search for callers of
`L2.02315` would settle these.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2060](../experiments/EXP-2060-rom2-physical-combat/)

### R2-ENGINE-482

With absolute addresses masked, the committed EN and RU listings are equal
instruction for instruction for the strike dispatcher (70), the structure
strike (70), the structure resolver (81), the award (464), the threshold
(9), the cap (50), the +0x68 route (105), the +0x6c route (65), the damage
object constructor (26) and apply (103), the random range (16) and the
recompute attack section (160). The resolver (449 EN, 460 RU) and the unit
strike (138 EN, 159 RU) differ in two RU-only tests:

- the RU unit strike returns without a blow when the attacker's virtual
  +0x30 is nonzero, `L2.00044` does not hold, the attack type is not 5 and
  the target's byte +0x4a is 3; EN strikes;
- the RU resolver skips the hostility bookkeeping `L2.02074` when global
  +0x74 is nonzero, the attacker's owner has +0x2c nonzero and the target's
  owner has +0x2c zero; EN always calls it.

The unit strike reads the weapon's cast object at +0x84 in EN and +0x88 in
RU, the item shift of R2-ENGINE-407. The EN +0x70 window is shorter than the
RU one; that pair is not compared.

**Confidence.** High for the pairs named. The meaning of target byte +0x4a
is not established here: the only ROM2 statement names MovementType at
+0x49, +0x4a in the template-load field list. The masked comparison does not
compare the values behind masked constant addresses.

**Unknown.** The value table of MovementType and the writers of +0x4a; EN constants, the EN generator, weapon fill, equip, fold,
creature row reader, actor update and distance. Reading them in EN would
settle EN parity.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2060](../experiments/EXP-2060-rom2-physical-combat/)

### R2-ENGINE-483

The RU creature row reader `L2.02341` reads one value per field from a
stream and stores, in this order: Body, Reaction, Mind, Spirit (+0x84..+0x8a),
HPmax +0x96 and health +0x94, +0x98, mana +0x9c (copied to +0x9a and +0xa0),
+0x9e, speed +0x8c, a byte at [+0x1c0]+0xa, byte +0xa5, then min, max and
kind as dwords, toHit into +0xa6 (copied to +0xa8), defence +0xbe,
absorption +0xc0, bytes +0x134 and +0x135, and five words +0xc4..+0xcc. The
order equals the Units column titles 1 to 24 (healthMax to prot Astral).

With spread = max - min, kind decides the attack bytes:

- kind 0 or below: when min < 128 and spread <= min + 255, base +0xb4 = min
  and spread +0xb5 = spread; otherwise +0xb4 = min(min/15, 127) | 0x80 and
  +0xb5 = min(spread/15, 255), the encoding R2-ENGINE-478 step 1 undoes;
- kind 1: min and spread into +0xb7/+0xb8 (block +0x11/+0x12);
- kind 2: their negated bytes into +0xb9/+0xba (the magic part
  +0x13/+0x14);
- kind 3: unit flag 0x10 and min and spread into +0xb4/+0xb5 unencoded;
- any other kind stores no attack byte.

In the RU client Units table, 180 of the 241 rows carry values; 165 carry
attackKind -1 and 15 carry 3 (the five levels of Bat_Sonic, Bee and
Spider). No named row carries kind 1 or 2.

**Confidence.** High for the stores and their order in RU. Medium that the
stream is the unit's Units row: the order matches the titles and the stream
source was not traced. Medium for the meaning of kinds 1 and 2: no client
row uses them. EN: not read.

**Unknown.** The rest of the reader past `L2.02336`, which would show the
res.Blade..res.Shooting bytes, typeID and XPvalue; the creature's attack
type +0xb6. Reading the reader to its end and its EN counterpart would
settle these.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2060](../experiments/EXP-2060-rom2-physical-combat/)

### R2-ENGINE-493

TalkTo `D2.00137` is 61 instructions with one range hash in EN and RU. It
takes NPC from bits 0..15, topic from bits 16..27 and kind from bits
28..30; bit 31 is not read. Kind 0 runs two tests in order:

1. `CMP NPC,5` at `D2.00266`. Equal stores 1 at `D2.00267` (bank 536), 3 at
   `D2.00268` (bank 556) and 2 at `D2.00269` (bank 774). The topic is not
   tested.
2. `CMP NPC,0x2a3` at `D2.00270` and `CMP topic,0x4e` at `D2.00271`. Both
   equal store 2 at `D2.00215` (bank 770) and OR `0x80000` into
   `D2.00240` (R2-ENGINE-331).

Bank N is the dword at `D2.00003+4N` (R2-ENGINE-367). The kind 0 path
calls nothing and tests no stage, bank or current record. Kind 1 stores
`bank[511+NPC]==0` into bank 511+NPC. Kind 2 and kinds 4..7 return at
`D2.00272` without a store. Kind 3 is R2-ENGINE-219 and R2-ENGINE-229.

**Confidence.** High: the complete body, decoded in both roots from one
committed and reproduced listing; its two arm tests have no other entry.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2062](../experiments/EXP-2062-rom2-inn-talk/)

two store the tail word of R2-ENGINE-221 (`D2.00273` kind 1, `D2.00274`

| `D2.00099` | 5 / 79 | NPC 5 |

### R2-ENGINE-485

The writer `L2.02342` (EN `L2.02344`) loops L = 0..149 (`cmp 0x96`) and
stores `ftol((pow(1.1, L) - 1.0) x 1000.0)` at `L2.02330 + 4L`. The power
helper `L2.00109` pushes the double 1.1 (`0x3ff199999999999a`) and calls the
library routine `L2.02322`. Constants: 1.0 at `L2.00067`, 1000.0 at
`L2.02345` (RU; the EN table at `L2.01124` holds the same 40 dwords).
`ftol` (`L2.01309`) truncates (R2-ENGINE-478). The one direct call of the
writer in RU `.text` is at `L2.02346` (EN `L2.02347`), next to a block of
startup stores; the containing routine was not read further.

Three routines read the table among the bodies read (Medium, below):

- the threshold `L2.02348` returns T(min(L, 149));
- skill-from-experience `L2.01782` returns the first i from 0 with
  T(i+1) > E; past i = 149 it returns the dword at `L2.02349` (T(149)),
  a value, not an index, and the comparison at i = 149 reads `L2.02343`,
  one dword past the table. Its result is the largest L with T(L) <= E for
  E below the dword at `L2.02343`, which was not read;
- experience-from-skill `L2.01285`, through the threshold, writes E(s) = T(skill s) for s = 1..5,
  their sum to +0x130 and copies each skill to its base word +0x116+2s

A RU `.text` dword pass for L2.02330, L2.02350, L2.02351 and L2.02343
finds four sites: the writer store, the two readers and an immediate
L2.02343 at `L2.02352`, which lies in no window read here and may read or
write the table. The pass searches four values and cannot enumerate the
readers of the table.

T(20) = 5,727, T(50) = 116,390, T(99) = 12,526,829, T(100) = 13,779,612,

11,739 at 50 and 1,378,061 at 100.

### R2-ENGINE-486

The award `L2.00055` (Human slot +0x64) takes X, the victim and a skill
(R2-ENGINE-480 gives its gates and scaling). It first restores the five
skill words from their base words +0x116+2i, so L is the base level of s.
It pays nothing when L is 100 or more. After the off-main cut, the cap
`L2.02329` sets X = min(X, T(L+1) - T(L)); when global +0x74 at
`[L2.01317]` is nonzero the difference is divided by 5 first. E(s) and the
sum +0x130 grow by X. Then:

- E(s) >= T(L+1): skill s and its base rise by one. When the owner's +0x2c
  is zero, message `L2.02354(2, s | kind << 16, owner)` is sent; a mage's
  spell book (+0x140) is refreshed through `L2.00041`; recompute (slot
  +0x58, `L2.00052`) runs; notification `L2.00060` carries
  `(0x100 << (s-1)) | 0x3000c`.
- otherwise: notification `L2.00060` with `0x100 << (s-1)` when X is
  nonzero, and each skill word becomes min(base, 100) + its modifier
  +0xe8+2i, without recompute.

When X is nonzero and global +0x74 is set, the award calls `L2.00059` if
more than 15,000 ms (tick source `[L2.02355]`) passed since owner
+0xa74. One award raises a skill by at most one level, and no award lifts
a base level above 100.

**Confidence.** High for the stores, branches and order, read in RU and EN
and equal after masking. Medium for the names of the message, the
notification and `L2.00041`, which were not read; their arguments are as
listed.

**Unknown.** The meaning of global +0x74 and the body of `L2.00059`.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2061](../experiments/EXP-2061-rom2-hero-growth/)

### R2-ENGINE-487

A caster whose `+0x4c` has bits 2 and 4 (template load sets both when
ManaMax is positive, R2-ENGINE-319) and who casts without an item offers
trunc(row parameter 1 x 0.5 + 0.5) to the award, which scales it by Mind,
cuts it off the main skill and caps it. The credit is the award's result,
below the offered amount; a cost of 10 at Mind 24 offers 5 and credits 1 on
an off-main Sphere.

The apply head `L2.00034` (R2-ENGINE-024) sets a flag from `L2.02356`
(caster byte +0x4c & 2), computes P (R2-ENGINE-020) from the skill named
by row parameter 2, runs the fill, and then, when that byte bit is set and
the caster's +0x68 (item cast, R2-ENGINE-020) is zero, calls the caster's
slot +0x70 with the target and the spell id before any per-spell arm.
Slot +0x70 (`L2.02357`) returns unless `L2.00044` holds (byte +0x4c & 4,
the mage test of R2-ENGINE-362). It then reads the spell row through
`L2.02358` (row = table +4 + 32 x id) and `L2.02312` (dword i of the row's
parameter array at row +8, `L2.02359`): s = parameter 2, and when s is
nonzero it calls the award with X = trunc(parameter 1 x 0.5 + 0.5), no
victim and skill s. With no victim the award skips the repeated-victim
cut and the owner gates, keeps the Mind scaling, the off-main cut (ceil
X/8 unless s is the main skill or 5) and the cap (R2-ENGINE-486). The
call is made only when bit 2 is set and +0x68 is zero.

Parameter 2 is the Sphere: the apply head reads the power skill through
the same accessor and index, and R2-ENGINE-020 names that skill
caster +0xa8 + 2 x Sphere. Parameter 1 is the Mana Cost under the column
numbering of R2-ENGINE-018 (column 1); costs run 3 to 100, so the offered amount
before scaling runs 2 to 50. The Heal arm (`L2.00081`) calls no award
slot in its own instructions; its callees `L2.00092`, `L2.02360` and
`L2.00060` were not read, so a Heal pays the cast payment only as far as
those bodies are not paying (Medium). R2-ENGINE-027 applies the head
once per Prismatic Spray victim, so that spell pays once per victim. A
non-mage caster reaches +0x70 and is paid nothing.

**Confidence.** High for the call, its gates and the arithmetic, read in
RU and EN and equal after masking. Medium for the Heal clause and for the
statement that an item cast pays no cast payment beyond the gate read
(the callees above are unread). Medium for the column names: the spell
loader was not read, and the Mana Cost binding rests on R2-ENGINE-018.
Medium for the meaning of +0x4c bit 2, which is read but not named.

**Unknown.** Whether the arms of Summon, the protections and the other

### R2-ENGINE-488

Slot +0x6c (`L2.02327`, R2-ENGINE-480) with a nonzero spell id returns
unless `L2.00044` holds; for a mage it passes s = row parameter 2 (the
Sphere, R2-ENGINE-487). It pays only when the victim has an owner whose
+0x2c is nonzero, with X = trunc(V x 0.5 x D / HPmax + 1), V the victim's
+0x1c and HPmax its +0x96. Three callers found in the bodies read pass a
spell (Medium: no call census of slots +0x6c and +0x70 was made):

- the damage object `L2.01702` with its spell id when the id and its
  source are nonzero (R2-ENGINE-480);
- the Drain Life arm (`L2.00083`): v = (base + U[1, spread]) x (100 - word
  +0xcc) / 100, capped at target health + 10 (R2-ENGINE-026); when v > 0
  the caster's +0x6c runs with v and the spell id before the target's
  health falls by v;
- the effect tick `L2.02361` for effect kind 6: d = -magnitude, cut when
  the target's word +0xc6 is nonzero to trunc(d(100 - p)/100 + 0.5); when d
  is nonzero health +0x94 falls by d, and the effect's source +0x44, unless
  `L2.02362` holds for it, receives +0x6c with d and spell id 6.

The Heal arm calls no slot in its own instructions; its callees
`L2.00092`, `L2.02360` and `L2.00060` were not read. A non-mage source with a spell id is paid
nothing.

**Confidence.** High for the RU bodies (Drain Life and Heal also in EN,
equal after masking). Medium for the three-caller statement and for the
Heal clause: the callees named above are unread and no census of the calls
through slots +0x6c and +0x70 was made. Medium in EN for the effect tick, which was read in
RU only. Medium that kind 6 is the Poison Cloud health effect: the tick
passes 6 whatever spell created the effect.

**Unknown.** The callers of the kill slot +0x68 (R2-ENGINE-480), so
whether a spell kill pays its trunc(V x 0.5) is not established; the
meaning of `L2.02362`; the callers of slots +0x6c and +0x70 beyond the
three above (the census and its byte patterns are in R2-ENGINE-487); the

### R2-ENGINE-489

Bodies that write E(s) (+0x23c + 4s) besides the award, all read in RU.
"Level from E" below is bounded as in R2-ENGINE-485: for E below the dword
at `L2.02343`, which was not read.

- reuse `L2.01779` (R2-ENGINE-406, which grades Medium that a mission entry
  reaches the reuse path, so how often the cut applies is open):
  E(s) = trunc(9 E(s) / 10), the sum
  recomputed, skill s = level from E (R2-ENGINE-485), bases copied; it
  calls no recompute itself (`L2.01780` unread);
- the character-file loaders (R2-ENGINE-410; client `L2.02363`, server
  `L2.02364`): E(1..5) from record dwords +0x20..+0x30, skill s = level
  from E, and the sum rebuilt from E; the server loader takes the main
  skill from byte +0x2e of a second record;
- an experience-from-skill producer, whose window at `L2.02365` starts
  inside its function (the function entry was not read), stores +0x14c (replaced by (value / 10) mod
  1000 when above 10,000), sets +0x4b bit 0x80 when the unit's row
  parameter 0x12 is nonzero, then runs experience-from-skill and
  recompute;
- item routine `L2.02366`, item class word +0x40: 0xfffe gives
  A = 250 x word +0x42 and walks s = 1..5 with a carry c: c += A/5 for the
  main skill or 5, else c = (c >> 3) + A/40; E(s) is capped at T(100) and
  the excess carries to the next skill; when the level from E exceeds the
  base, message `L2.02354(2, s, owner)` is sent, the base takes it and the
  skill word becomes min(base, 100) + modifier. This case writes neither
  the sum +0x130 nor runs recompute. Class 0xffff adds 250 x word +0x42 to
  the owner's +0x3c through `L2.02367`;
- raise-one `L2.02368`: skill s + 1, E(s) = T(new level) + 1, the sum
  grows by the difference, recompute runs. A RU `.text` call-target pass
  and a `.rdata` dword pass find no reference to it.

A RU `.text` pattern pass for the bytes of displacement 0x23c finds 56
sites. Ten are indexed stores into E: the award (2), reuse,
experience-from-skill, raise-one, the item case (3), an immediate store at
`L2.02369` and a copy at `L2.02370` (bytes only, bodies unread). The
character-file loaders store E(1..5) with the displacements 0x240..0x250,
which this pass does not see; no pass searched those displacements
elsewhere.

**Confidence.** High for the arithmetic of the bodies read (reuse, raise
and the item cases also in EN). Medium for the roles: "character-file
loader" follows R2-ENGINE-410; what places an item of class 0xfffe and
what runs the item routine (pickup or use) was not read. Medium for the
population: the 46 other 0x23c sites and the direct 0x240..0x250 stores
were not classified.

**Unknown.** The join of the loaders' records (dwords +0x20..+0x30, byte
+0x2e of the second record) to a section of the `.a2c` page is Unknown.
Script and `scenario.dll` sources: neither was searched.
Mission-end awards: no census of award-slot callers was run. The caller of
`L2.02368`.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2061](../experiments/EXP-2061-rom2-hero-growth/)

## Computer-unit target choice, pursuit and flight

Shared terms. Addresses are RU `allods2.exe`; the EN body sits at RU -
0x9ff0 below `L2.01527` and at RU - 0xa039 from `L2.02401` upward
(R2-ENGINE-508). The actor's command object is actor +0x1c4 ("cmd"), its
movement block actor +0x1c0 ("block"). The order is actor +0x50
(R2-ENGINE-398); the activity is cmd byte +8, run by the unit tick
`L2.00506` through the 15 dwords at `L2.01571`. Owner +0x2c is the Player
kind, nonzero for computer-owned units (R2-ENGINE-457). Attack range is
`L2.01728`: the range byte +9 of the spell in cmd byte +0x78 when the
spellbook +0x140 holds it and mana +0x9a covers its cost word +0xc, else
the weapon range byte +0x12c. "Kind" is the byte `L2.02402` returns; that
it is byte +0x4a (R2-ENGINE-482) rests on navigation reads only. The cards
state executable behaviour and no stored-file layout.

| ID | Public functional claim | Confidence | Status | Evidence |

| R2-ENGINE-503 | ROM2 group members take the enemy with the least score (cells x 256 + turn), scaled by a 16-byte kind table whose 0 excludes. | High / Medium | ● active | [EXP-2063](../experiments/EXP-2063-rom2-enemy-targets/) |
| R2-ENGINE-504 | A ROM2 unit holds a target for one activity, then re-picks, from units each nearer than those kept before, the hostile of least turn, or stands or looks around. | High / Medium / Unknown | ● active | [EXP-2063](../experiments/EXP-2063-rom2-enemy-targets/) |

### R2-ENGINE-501

The idle planner `L2.01731` (order 12, and every order the table does not
name, through `L2.01733`) runs the list builder `L2.02404` (R2-ENGINE-502)
and walks session list +0xa64. A candidate whose score `L2.00057`
(R2-ENGINE-503) is 0xffffff is skipped. For the rest, d is `L2.01588`, plus
1 when the candidate's kind is 3 and the actor's is not, and t is the turn
`L2.02405` from block byte +0 (facing) to the direction `L2.02113`. The
best starts at d = range + 1, t = 0xff. A smaller d replaces it; an equal d
not above range with t not above the best t replaces it, so the later
candidate wins a full tie. With live candidates but no result, and a
nonempty list +0xa88 (R2-ENGINE-502), list +0xa84 is walked the same way
without the score filter or the kind adjustment. A result above range is dropped.

`L2.01588` is an edge-to-edge distance: per axis |a - b| in position units
minus (size a + size b) x 128, floored at 0; the larger axis divided by 256,
plus 1. Size is virtual slot +0x1c, and each coordinate is offset by
(size - 1) x 128.

A found target goes to `L2.01525`: a player-owned mage first tries
`L2.01527`; otherwise activity 6 with cmd +0xc = target and cmd byte +0x14
= range. Activity 6 (`L2.02406`) strikes through `L2.02407` when `L2.01574`
admits the target at that range; otherwise `L2.02408` passes the
direction to the target to `L2.02409`, the call the look-around uses to
turn (R2-ENGINE-504), and sets state +0x54 to 1 when the facing changed.
Activity 6 makes no call to the step routine `L2.01577` of activity 5.
A player-owned mage with range below 2 drops the activity there. With no
target the idle planner calls support `L2.01531`. It then sends a unit
standing centred in its cell (`L2.00490`) whose block word +0x80 is nonzero
and differs from its cell back to that cell through `L2.02410`.

**Confidence.** High for the choice rule and the activity-6 body in RU, and
for the choice rule in EN (equal masked bodies, reproduced listings).
Medium: `L2.01525` was read in navigation only; the position units behind
`L2.02411` and `L2.02412`, and the bodies of `L2.01574` and `L2.02409`,
were not read, so "without stepping" rests on activity 6 calling no step
routine; EN activity 6 is generation only (R2-ENGINE-508).

**Evidence.** [EXP-2063](../experiments/EXP-2063-rom2-enemy-targets/)

### R2-ENGINE-502

The list builder `L2.02404` clears and fills the sight grid at map
+0x58ec0 through `L2.02413` and `L2.01586`. `L2.01586` calls `L2.01587`:
the budget is (ScanRange byte +0xa5 << s) + (1 << (s - 1)), s the map dword
+0x2a004. Byte +0xa5 is the ScanRange copied by the hero template load for
Humans (R2-ENGINE-319); for creatures it is the byte the creature row
reader stores in the Units column position (R2-ENGINE-483). It marks the actor's cell, then walks square rings 1 to 19 and
stops after a ring in which every in-bounds cell (`L2.02414`) is marked.
Cell test `L2.02415` steps toward the actor through the direction table
+0x22000 and sets the cell's remaining budget to the previous cell's minus
(terrain height byte at +0x944f4 minus the actor's height, plus the cost
word at +0x28000); it marks the cell when the remainder is above 0.

For a computer-owned actor with a remembered cell in cmd word +0x58, the
builder marks that cell too, increments cmd byte +0x5a and clears +0x58
when the count passes 20: builder runs 1 to 21 mark the cell, run 21
clears it after marking. World units on marked cells form list +0xa64.
Filter `L2.02119` removes units whose owner relation mask 1 (`L2.01589`
returns byte & 1, the predicate R2-ENGINE-364 calls the hostility bit)
does not mark hostility, and units with effect 0x1000 that no member of the
actor's +0x70 list sees within its cmd byte +0x71 (R2-ENGINE-364). Then
`L2.02416` moves units with health +0x94 below 1 to lists +0xa84 and
+0xa88. When no live candidate remains, the builder moves list +0xa84 into
+0xa64 and clears +0xa88 (`L2.02417`..`L2.02418`).

Being hit sets the memory: `L2.02074` (attacker, victim) writes the
victim's cmd +0x54 = 1, +0x58 = attacker cell and +0x5a = 0, runs relation
`L2.02419`, posts event 1, stores the attacker at cmd +0x94 and the time
`[L2.01317]+4` at +0x98, and stores at word +0x9c the cell a fixed distance
(the double at `L2.02420`) from the victim directly away from the attacker.

**Confidence.** High for the ring walk, the cell-test arithmetic, the
remembered cell, the filter and the hit memory in RU, and all but the hit
memory in EN. Medium for the ScanRange of a creature (R2-ENGINE-483 grades
its stream source Medium) and for the jitter draw `L2.02421`. Medium: the contents and writers of the direction, height and
cost tables, `L2.02413`, the world list, and the value 10.0 at `L2.02420`
(navigation read) were not read in generation; EN `L2.02074` is generation
only.

**Unknown.** The bodies of `L2.02402` (kind; navigation window
`L2.02422` only) and `L2.02421`; whether the creature +0xa5 equals the
title ScanRange of its Units row.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2063](../experiments/EXP-2063-rom2-enemy-targets/)

### R2-ENGINE-503

Score `L2.00057` (actor, candidate): d is the Chebyshev cell distance
`L2.01522`. The candidate kind k becomes 0 when it is 1 and the candidate's
own range exceeds 1. A ranged actor (range above 1) reads preference
p = T[k] and uses d - range + 1 beyond range, else 1; a melee actor reads
p = T[k + 4 x its own kind] and keeps d. The score is d x 256 plus the turn
to the candidate. p = 0 returns 0xffffff (excluded); p = 1 adds half the
score and p = 4 subtracts a quarter, both only when the actor's size slot
+0x1c is below 2 and its Mind word +0x88 is at least 15. A candidate with
effect bit 0x40000 adds 0x7f (floor 1).

The session constructor writes T at session +0xa54 (`L2.02423`): 2, 1, 2,
4 / 4, 2, 1, 0 / 2, 1, 4, 0 / 2, 1, 2, 4. Group assignment `L2.02424` gives
each member cmd +0x20 = the enemy of list +0xa68 with the strictly least
score (first on a tie), or 0, and posts event 4 when enemies exist, for active groups only (R2-ENGINE-057;
R2-ENGINE-507). The
idle planner uses the score only to exclude (R2-ENGINE-501).

**Confidence.** High for the arithmetic and the table values in RU and EN.
Medium for what the kind values name.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2063](../experiments/EXP-2063-rom2-enemy-targets/)

### R2-ENGINE-504

When block dword +0x98 is set at the end of an activity, the unit tick
clears it and, unless the order is 1, 10 or 24, sets activity 0 and runs
`L2.02425`. That routine walks the world unit list and keeps a unit only when its
distance d (`L2.02426`) is at most the range and at most a running
minimum seeded at 0xff and lowered to d after each kept unit
(`L2.02427`, `L2.02428`, `L2.02429`), so a unit later in list order than a
nearer one is dropped, a nearer non-hostile unit included. It then
filters list +0xa64 with `L2.02119` and `L2.02416`, falls back to list +0xa84 as the idle planner does, and takes the unit
needing the least turn (the later one on a tie). A result becomes activity
6 on that target (R2-ENGINE-501). With none, a computer-owned unit takes
activity 11, the look-around `L2.02430`, and a player-owned unit activity
0.

The look-around turns toward block byte +1 while it differs from the
facing; otherwise, when cmd +0x54 is set or `L2.02431` returns below 0xcd,
it sets a new heading facing + 0x21 + `L2.01532`(0xbe) and clears +0x54.
The order dispatch `L2.01725` resets through `L2.01576` an attack whose
target has state +0x54 = 0x10, and a follow order whose leader has. A group
member's target is reassigned on every tick of an active group
(R2-ENGINE-503, R2-ENGINE-057).

**Confidence.** High for the bodies in RU. Medium in EN (generation only)
and for the random helpers `L2.02431` and `L2.01532`, which were not read.

**Unknown.** When block +0x98 is set: its three writers (`L2.02432`,
`L2.02433`, `L2.02434`) lie in unread movement code. Reading them would
settle how long one activity holds a target.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2063](../experiments/EXP-2063-rom2-enemy-targets/)

### R2-ENGINE-505

The attack planner `L2.01530` sends a target with byte +0x4c bit 8 to the
default route. It casts the last of the three template spell entries cmd
+0x7c..+0x84, in index order, for which `L2.02431` returns less than the
entry's dword at +0x88 + 4i (nonzero entries only; the loop has no exit on
a hit, `L2.02435`..`L2.02436`; spell 23 only beyond 2 cells). With no target, or itself as target, it takes the first unit of
`L2.02117` around itself. It then sets activity 5 with cmd +0xc and range
+0x14; a computer mage first tries `L2.00056` (R2-ENGINE-457). Activity 5
(`L2.02437`) strikes when `L2.01574` admits the target at range, else steps
toward it through `L2.01577` (`L2.01578`); the activity-5 body itself has
no distance bound. Whether the step helper or the movement code gives up
is open.

Order 11 reaches `L2.02438` through `L2.02439`, and order 4 reaches the
planner through `L2.02440`; neither is in a committed listing, and the
link rests on the scan receipt `planner-calls` (`L2.02441`). The guard
(`L2.02438`) keeps a post in cmd word +0, set to the current cell when 0.
At a distance `L2.02442` (`L2.02443`) of at least ScanRange from the post
the unit walks back (`L2.02401`, activity 1). When `L2.02117` finds a
hostile within block byte +8 of the post (R2-ENGINE-457), `L2.01530` sets
activity 5 and replaces the walk, so the effective bound is the picker
radius around the post; with none the unit walks to the post, or stands
there. ScanRange is R2-ENGINE-319 for Humans and R2-ENGINE-483 for
creatures.

**Confidence.** High for the bodies in RU. Medium in EN for activity 5 (the
EN tail was generated once and not reproduced) and for the order mapping.
Medium for the order 4 and 11 identification, for `L2.02442` (navigation
only; Chebyshev by reading), for the creature ScanRange and for the
clause that activity 5 has no distance bound. Medium for what
`L2.01574` and `L2.01578` test. Medium for what `L2.02431` is: a random
draw by comparison with 0xcd in R2-ENGINE-504, not read; not established
as a time.

**Unknown.** Whether an unordered computer unit enters activity 5 other
than through orders 3, 4 and 11 and the group handlers; the writers of
activity 5 were not censused. The bodies of `L2.01574`, `L2.01578`,
`L2.02431`, `L2.02442`, `L2.01576` and the three block +0x98 writers
(`L2.02432`, `L2.02433`, `L2.02434`) were not read.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2063](../experiments/EXP-2063-rom2-enemy-targets/)

### R2-ENGINE-506

`L2.02444` sets class byte cmd +0x4c and two health thresholds when virtual
slot +0x30 returns nonzero, which R2-ENGINE-477 and R2-ENGINE-478 give as
the Human table (the creature table returns 0, and then `L2.02444` stores
nothing, so +0x40 and +0x44 keep their constructor values and the
predicates have no threshold from this routine): with a spellbook, class 2, +0x40 = HPmax +0x96
and +0x44 = HPmax/4; else with range above 1 and kind not 3, class 1,
HPmax/2 and 0; else class 0, 0 and 0. `L2.02445`(a, b, c, 0) rewrites +0x40
for player-owned units as HPmax x {a, b, c}[class] / 100. The group
post-step `L2.02446` calls `L2.02447` per member: when health +0x94 <= +0x44
and `L2.02448` finds a hostile within block byte +8 + 5, flee `L2.02449`;
else when health <= +0x40 and `L2.02450` finds a hostile within 2,
`L2.02451`. Flee casts spell 23 through `L2.02452` when `L2.01518` admits
it; else it walks 3 cells away from the hostiles' centre (`L2.02453`,
`L2.02454`); with no living hostile it takes the default route. Order 22
also reaches `L2.02449`.

**Confidence.** High for the thresholds, the two predicates and the flee
body in RU and EN. Medium: the direct-call scan over RU `.text` finds
`L2.02448`, `L2.02450` and `L2.02451` called only from `L2.02447`, with
virtual dispatch not searched; the centre and away helpers and
`L2.02451`'s destination rest on navigation reads.

**Unknown.** Whether units outside a group run `L2.02447`; its callers
beyond `L2.02446` were not scanned. Whether creature-table members have

| R2-ENGINE-510 | The ROM2 type-10 pass builds a 0xcc object with defaults for each group that passes the owner +0x2c test and a L2.02502 guard, then applies matching entries; the object re-creates the group's members after a countdown. | High / Medium | ✔ promoted (amended, branch candidate) | [EXP-2064](../experiments/EXP-2064-rom2-map-records/) |

| R2-ENGINE-512 | The ROM2 type-4 pass gives three object classes their type-11 fields by kind: 0xec objects from every matching 11a, 0xc4 objects from the first matching 11b, 0x70 objects from every nonzero 11c. | High / Unknown | ✔ promoted (amended, branch candidate) | [EXP-2064](../experiments/EXP-2064-rom2-map-records/) |

### R2-ENGINE-509

In the map build (RU `L2.00113`, EN `L2.00186`; R2-ENGINE-108) the
instruction at RU `L2.02503` compares map+0xd8 with 1 and stores the
result of `> 1` in Session(`[L2.01317]`)+0x74; Session+0x178 receives its
negation and Session+0x1cc receives map+0xdc. The dispatcher fills
map+0xd8 and map+0xdc from type-0 payload dwords 0x84 and 0x88. After the
owner, type-4, actor and two further builders, RU `L2.02504` calls the
type-10 pass `L2.00118` only when Session+0x74 is not 0. The actor builder
scales actor word +0x96 by difficulty constants in its Units arm only
when Session+0x74 is 0.

Over the census of R2-ASSET-122, the 46 `scenario.res` campaign maps per
root, type-0 dword 0x84 is 1 in every map, so the store at `L2.02503`
leaves the gate closed on them and their type-10 entries would have no
effect if present. Session+0x74 has other writers: R2-ENGINE-334 gives
the server init store +0x74 = (mode < 2) and leaves 119 EN and 121 RU
other dword `[reg+0x74]` stores unclassified, and R2-ENGINE-125 states
all other writers and the persistence of the gate across the call as
Unknown. So "no campaign map runs the pass" is Medium.

**Confidence.** High for the gate: the store at `L2.02503` and the test at
`L2.02504` are in `out/listings/ru-world-build.txt` and equal in EN; the
map build, dispatcher and actor builder bodies were read in both roots and
match after address masking; the census is reproduced from Git blobs.
Medium for "only" and for "no campaign map runs the pass": that `L2.00118`
has one caller rests on a RU call-target scan (a navigation receipt, hit
`L2.02505`); no EN call-target scan and no dword scan of `.rdata` for the
address ran, so a pointer-table call is not excluded; the other writers
of Session+0x74 are open (above); and the two further builders between the
store and the test (RU `L2.00116`, `L2.00117`) were not read for stores
to +0x74.

**Unknown.** Which code writes Session+0x74 besides the store at
`L2.02503` and the init of R2-ENGINE-334. What a value above 1 in dword
0x84 means beyond these two uses. What type-0 dword 0x88 means; it is
stored in map+0xdc and Session+0x1cc (`L2.02506`..`L2.02507`). Whether any
of the 13 EN and 37 RU root `.alm` maps has dword 0x84 above 1
(R2-ASSET-122). An EN call-target scan of the pass, a dword scan of
`.rdata` for its address, and reading the two further builders and the
other `[reg+0x74]` stores would settle the gate.

**Amended.** R2-ASSET-130 reads the root `.alm` maps: type-0 dword 0x84 is 4..16, above 1, in all 13 EN and 37 RU of them; the gate opens if the root maps are built by this routine, which was not read (Medium). The loader of a root map is Unknown; reading the callers of the build RU `L2.00113` settles it. Dword 0x88 is 1..4 there.

### R2-ENGINE-510

For every owner (global RU `L2.00293`) whose +0x2c is not 0 (`L2.02508`..
`L2.02509` skips an owner with 0) and every group in owner+0x28, the pass
calls the group function (RU `L2.02493`, EN `L2.02494`). The function
calls `L2.02502(group)` at `L2.02510` and returns when the result is 0
(`L2.02511`..`L2.02512`), before any object exists; the helper is unread.
Otherwise it computes the members' centroid and spread through member+0x10
(`L2.00486`, `L2.00487`), allocates a 0xcc object (ctor RU `L2.02513`, EN
`L2.02514`; vtable RU `L2.02515`) at the centroid and sets:

| Object field | Value |
|---:|---|
| +0x14 | group +0x44 |
| +0xac | group +0x1c, the group number from unit row +0x40 |
| +0xb0, +0xb4 | 120 * S / 100 |
| +0xb8 | -1 (init) |
| +0xbc | see R2-ENGINE-511 |
| +0xc0, +0xc4, +0xc8 | 0 (init) |

The ctor's init (RU `L2.02516`) also sets +0x68 = 0, and `L2.02517`
stores a copy of each member as a template. The type-10 entries then
apply as in R2-ASSET-120. The object is registered (`L2.02518`), the
group gets `L2.02519(group, 0)`, and `L2.02490(+0xb8)` runs when +0xb8 is
at least 0. `L2.02519` sets byte +0x20 of the group's programme ([group+0x3c]) to
0x12 (R2-ENGINE-507 route 18), raises its bytes +0x2d and +0x38 to a
floor and clears +0x39. `L2.02490(i)` is read to its dispatch table, with
i the +0xb8 value; the lookup helper `L2.02520` and the iterator helpers
`L2.02497` and `L2.02498` are unread, so what i selects is not
established.

Vtable slot 5 (RU `L2.02521`) sets +0xc0 = 1 once every member in +0x6c
has byte +0x13c of at least 3, and decrements +0xb4 once per call. At 0 or
below it looks up the group with number +0xac; when `L2.02502` of that
group is above 0 (`L2.02522`..`L2.02523`) the call ends. Otherwise it
re-creates each member from its template, places it at object+0x10 with
+0xbc as the third argument of `L2.00313`, resets +0xb4 to +0xb0,
re-forms the group with number +0xac, sets group +0x48 and +0x4c from
+0xc4 and +0xc8, and repeats the two calls above. The member loop at
`L2.02524` also calls `L2.02525` on members with byte +0x13c below 5 and
stores 0xfda7 at object +0x42.

S is the first dword of RU `L2.02526` and EN `L2.02527`. In RU the only
absolute store found by the writer scan is at `L2.02528`, by a key/value
parser (key string `L2.02529`, unread) that clamps the value to 20..500;
the ctor RU `L2.02530` writes 100 to this+0.

**Confidence.** High for the build: the group function, ctor, init and
template copy were read in both roots (the group function differs only as
R2-ENGINE-511 states), and the owner and `L2.02502` guards are read in RU
listings; the EN slot-5 body equals the RU body after masking (152 of 152
instructions), and the EN group function head was not compared by hand.
Medium for the slot-5 behaviour: the body was read in both roots, but the
caller of slot 5 and the helpers `L2.02502`, `L2.00313`, `L2.02525`,
`L2.02520`, `L2.02497`, `L2.02498` and the tail of `L2.02490` were not,
so when it runs, when members are re-created and what the third argument
does rest on unread code. Medium for S = 100 by default in RU: that the
ctor `L2.02530` runs on `L2.02526` was not read. The RU writer census of
`L2.02526` is a navigation scan.

**Unknown.** What `L2.02502` tests, and so which groups get an object and
which skip re-creation; the caller and call rate of slot 5; the units of
+0xb0 (ticks or another clock); the EN writer of `L2.02527` and its
default; the key string at `L2.02529`. Reading `L2.02502` and the slot-5
caller would settle the first two; the EN store would settle the last.

**Amended.** R2-ENGINE-538 reads `L2.02502`: it returns dword +0xc of its receiver (High); that the value is a member count is Medium. The third argument of `L2.00313` is the positioning radius of R2-ENGINE-531.

### R2-ENGINE-511

At RU `L2.02531` the group function stores the spread it computed (the
larger of the x and y extents of the members) in object +0xbc. The EN body
`L2.02494` stores +0xb4 at `L2.02532` and calls the template copy
`L2.02533` next, with no +0xbc store; its only +0xbc store is the bit-2
clear at `L2.02534`, which writes 0. The EN init `L2.02535` sets +0xbc to
0. So in EN a type-10 object always has +0xbc = 0, and in RU it has the
spread unless a matching entry with bit 2 clear sets it to 0. The only
content difference found in the EN lines read (`L2.02536`..`L2.02537`) is
this one store of three instructions; the masked comparison of the two
bodies (330 EN and 333 RU instructions) counts 139 differing instructions
after it by alignment.

**Confidence.** High for the stores: both bodies were read. Medium for the
player effect: +0xbc reaches `L2.00313` as its third argument when slot 5
re-creates members (R2-ENGINE-510), and that helper was not read. Under
R2-ENGINE-509 the pass is not run on the 46 campaign maps per root unless
another writer opens the gate (Medium), so the difference is not reached
there.

**Amended.** R2-ENGINE-538 states the player effect through R2-ENGINE-531: RU re-creates members over the spread, EN tests the centre cell at radius 0 (Medium).

### R2-ENGINE-512

The type-4 pass (RU `L2.00114`, EN `L2.00189`) runs only when global
`L2.02538` is not 0 (`L2.02539`..`L2.02540`, `cmp`, `jne`; otherwise it
ends), then calls `L2.02541` (`L2.02542`). The same global is passed to
the constructors as an argument; its meaning is Unknown. The pass builds
an object per type-4 element by kind (element word +4):

| Kinds | Object | Type-11 source | Fields |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x43..0x45, 0x63..0x65, 0x6f..0x71 | 0xec, ctor RU `L2.02543`, vtable `L2.02544` | every 11a entry with e0 = element +0x10; the last wins | word +0xd4 = low word of e2 when e1 & 2, else 0; +0xc4 = e1 & 0x10; +0xc8 = e1 & 0x20; +0xcc = e1 & 0x40; +0xd0 = e1 & 4 |
| 0x22, 0x23, 0x5d..0x5f, 0x69..0x6b | 0xc4, ctor RU `L2.02545`, vtable `L2.02546`; +0xc0 = 10000000, +0x6c = a 0x98 helper (`L2.02547`) | the first 11b entry with e0 = element +0x10 | for i in 0..3: +0x80+0x14i = e[0x04+4i], +0x70+0x14i = e[0x14+4i], +0x74+0x14i = e[0x24+4i], +0x78+0x14i = e[0x34+4i], +0x7c+0x14i = e[0x44+4i] |
| 0x46..0x4b | 0x70, ctor RU `L2.02548`, vtable `L2.02549`; +0x6c = -1 | every 11c entry with e0 = element +0x10 and e1 not 0; the last wins | +0x6c = count of the first e2 type-7 first-array nodes with dword +0x40 below 0x10002 |
| other | 0x6c (`L2.02550`) | none | none from type 11 |

The 11a loop applies its stores four times per entry with the same
values. Every byte of a matching 11b entry is read. Slot 2 of the 0xc4
class (`L2.02551`) serializes only the base and +0xc0.

**Confidence.** High for the kind split and the stores: the pass and the
three ctors were read in both roots. Unknown for the consumers of 0xc4
+0x70..+0xbc, 0xec +0xc4..+0xd4 and 0x70 +0x6c: those methods were not
read. The listing of the 0x98 helper's methods is in the evidence but was
not interpreted, and the 0xec and 0x70 vtables were not walked.

**Unknown.** What the three classes do with these fields during a
mission, and what global `L2.02538` is. Interpreting the 0x98 helper
listing and reading the methods of vtables `L2.02544` and `L2.02549` that
touch these offsets would settle the first.

**Amended.** R2-ENGINE-536 reads a reader of 0xec +0xc4, +0xc8, +0xcc, +0xd0 and word +0xd4 (the Inn offer generator; that its receiver is the Inn is Medium, inferred from addresses), and R2-ENGINE-539 a reader of 0xc4 +0x70..+0xbf (the Shop fill, as its stock record when Session+0x74 is set; R2-ASSET-131). Other readers of Inn +0xc4..+0xd4 and Shop +0x70..+0xbf are Unknown: no displacement scan ran for those offsets, and one `.text` displacement scan over both roots, classified against the class bodies, settles it. 11a flag 1 is stored by no field and occurs in the root maps (R2-ASSET-132).

### R2-ENGINE-513

Two bodies take rows from map+0x3a4 through the getters `L2.02552` and
`L2.02553`: the actor builder (RU `L2.00115`, EN `L2.00192`) and the
mission-load row loop (RU `L2.02554`, EN `L2.02555`).

| Row slot | Actor builder | Mission-load loop |
|---:|---|---|
| +0x00, +0x04 | shifted right by 8, placement `L2.00313` | read |
| +0x08 | not read | pushed to `L2.02556` on `L2.02501`; a nonzero +0x124 in the result builds a 0x1e4 object with `L2.02557`, zero builds a 0x1e4 object with `R2.0068` (`L2.02558`..`L2.02559`) |
| +0x10 | definition id (R2-ENGINE-038) | read, passed to `L2.02560` on `L2.02561` |
| +0x14 | owner lookup; a miss logs text `L2.02562` | read |
| +0x20, +0x22 | person arm: equal and not -1 makes both -1; +0x22 not -1 to actor word +0x96, +0x20 not -1 to word +0x94, else +0x94 = +0x96 | read |
| +0x3c | word, sign-extended, to actor dword +8 | word + 0x6000 |
| +0x40 | matched against group +0x1c | read |
| +0x48 | bit 0x10 selects the person arm (0x254) or the Units arm (0x208) | bit 0x10 arm |
| +0x50 | bits 1, 2, 4, 8 to actor +0x194, +0x19c, +0x198, +0x1a0 | not read |

In ROM2 row +0x08 indexes the `L2.02501` collection, and the +0x124 of
the record found chooses which constructor builds the 0x1e4 object; what
the collection and the class are stays Unknown. R2-ENGINE-040 reads the
same field as a unit class value under a ROM1 reading.

Neither body reads row +0x0c, +0x1c or +0x44; the loader uses +0x44 for
the type-8 join (R2-ASSET-119). The two mission-load bodies differ in four
constants only, none a row offset. The other callers of the getters are the
teardown (RU `L2.02563`, `L2.02564`).

**Confidence.** High for the reads listed: both bodies were read in both
roots and match after masking (the loop with four differing constants).
Medium for the absence of +0x0c and +0x1c readers and for "+0x08 is read
only by the loop": the census lists every use of the row local in the two
bodies, and the caller census is an RU call-target scan of the two getters
plus `add ecx, 0x3a4` sites (a navigation receipt); a row passed whole to
a helper, or a copy of the row, would escape it.

**Unknown.** What the collection at `L2.02501` and the 0x1e4 object are;
an EN call-target scan of the getters would bound the EN readers.

**Amended.** R2-ENGINE-535 states the effect of +0x1a0 (bit 8) and R2-ENGINE-537 the Inn offer reads of +0x194, +0x19c and +0x198 (bits 1, 2 and 4). The bound on row +0x0c and +0x1c readers is unchanged (the two bodies of this card; EXP-2068 ran no displacement scan for those row offsets, and one over `.text` classified against the row consumers settles it): a displacement scan for +0x3a4 finds 21 sites per root, and only the dispatcher and teardown sites lie in windows read for it.
