### R2-ENGINE-517

The 0x70 objects of R2-ENGINE-512 belong to the class whose record is RU
`L2.02568` and EN `L2.02569`: name "Pointer" (RU `L2.02570`, EN
`L2.02571`), size 0x70, base record RU `L2.02572` and EN `L2.02573`, named
"Building", size 0x6c. The ctor (RU `L2.02548`, EN `L2.02574`) calls the
Building ctor (RU `L2.02550`, EN `L2.02575`, which stores the Building
vtable RU `L2.02576`, EN `L2.02577`), stores the Pointer vtable (RU
`L2.02549`, EN `L2.02578`) and sets +0x6c to -1.

The two vtables have 15 slots each and differ in three: slot 0 returns the
class record (RU `L2.02579`), slot 1 (RU `L2.02580`) is called the
destructor on a navigation window only, with no committed listing of its
body, and slot 2 is Serialize (RU `L2.02581`). Serialize calls the
Building Serialize (`L2.02582`), then, when `R2.0017` on the archive
returns nonzero, passes dword +0x6c to `L2.00354`, else passes the address
of +0x6c to `L2.02583`. Every other slot, slot 5 included, is the Building
method. The Shop record (RU `L2.02584`, size 0xc4, name "Shop") and the
Inn record (RU `L2.02585`, size 0xec, name "Inn") have the same base record.

**Confidence.** High for the class identity, the slot comparison and the
ctor and Serialize bodies: the ctor (22 instructions), Building ctor (39),
slot 0 (8) and Serialize (26) are equal in EN and RU after address
masking, and both vtables and both records were read in each root. Medium
that Serialize writes +0x6c to a save and reads it back: the archive
helpers `R2.0017`, `L2.00354` and `L2.02583` were not read here.

**Unknown.** Which save sections carry these objects; reading `R2.0017`,
`L2.00354` and `L2.02583` and the caller of the collection's Serialize
slot would settle it. The body of slot 1 is unread in a committed
listing.

### R2-ENGINE-518

The actor step (RU `L2.00028`, EN `L2.00263`, both 0xaeb bytes; R2-ENGINE-030
and R2-ENGINE-399 call the same function the actor tick or step) returns at
once in state 0x10. It reaches the switch only when signed word unit +0x94
is above 0 (RU `L2.02586`..`L2.02587`: `movsx`, `jg L2.02588`); otherwise
the path at `L2.02589` writes unit +0x54 = 0, the same gate R2-ENGINE-399
reads. The switch is on unit +0x54 minus 1 through the byte
table RU `L2.02590` and jump table RU `L2.02591` (EN `L2.02592`,
`L2.02593`, equal in content). State 15 reaches the arm RU `L2.02594`
(EN `L2.02595`):

1. The building lookup (RU `L2.02596`, EN `L2.02597`) on the collection
   at [[[`L2.01317`]+0x7c]] forms a point from the position at unit +0x10
   minus 1 in x and y (getters `L2.00486`, `L2.00487`; point helpers
   `L2.02598` and `L2.02599`, unread) and calls `L2.02600`, which returns the first object in the
   collection (the iterator helpers `L2.02601`, `L2.02602` and `L2.02603`
   are unread) whose position gives `L2.02426` at or below 2, with no class
   test. The arm then tests Shop, Inn and Pointer in that order
   (`L2.02604`, `L2.02605`, `L2.02606`); an object of another class found
   first ends the Pointer path, which continues at `L2.02607`. `L2.02426`
   is the larger of the absolute x and y differences of two byte
   coordinates (`L2.01523` is absolute value).
2. A Shop (record `L2.02584`) calls `L2.02566` (unread; "packet" is the
   first argument's name here, and R2-ENGINE-058 and R2-ENGINE-047 name
   the different functions `L2.00512` and `L2.00457` as packet producers)
   on `L2.02608` with 0x83,
   byte +0x40, 0 and unit +0x14. An Inn (`L2.02585`) calls it with 0x84,
   byte +0x40, dword +4 and unit +0x14.
3. A Pointer (`L2.02568`) with signed +0x6c above 0 (`cmp`, `jle` skips
   0 and -1) passes +0x6c to the action executor `L2.02490` on
   [`L2.02609`]. The executor copies compiled slot +0x6c (R2-ENGINE-520)
   and runs its operation through the table of R2-ENGINE-058.

The arm stores nothing to the building and does not change the unit state;
the step returns after it. So each actor step in state 15 that reaches a
Pointer calls the executor; nothing in the arm limits the call to once.
The executor head (151 instructions, ending at the jump into the
operation table) and the operation arms are not read here; a latch inside
an operation is excluded only for operation 2, by R2-ENGINE-047 (no latch
seen at the event producer).

Readers of Pointer +0x6c: a navigation dword scan of RU `.text`, `.rdata`
and `.data` for the record `L2.02568` has four hits, all in `.text`: the
arm's class test at `L2.02610`, slot 0 at `L2.02611` and two short
functions at `L2.02612` and `L2.02613` whose bodies were not read. The ctor,
Serialize and the type-4 pass store are the other reads and writes found. The executor has
four direct callers in each root (RU `L2.02614` this arm, `L2.02615` and
`L2.02616` of the type-10 object, R2-ENGINE-510, and `L2.02617` of the
trigger runner; EN `L2.02618`, `L2.02619`, `L2.02620`, `L2.02621`).

**Confidence.** High for the arm's tests, branches and its call of the
executor with +0x6c, and for the lookup and the executor head: the
actor step is 818 instructions in both roots and equal after masking except
two reads of +0x84 (EN) against +0x88 (RU) before the switch (RU `L2.02622`,
`L2.02623`) and two `push 0x54` (EN `L2.02624`, `L2.02625`) against `push
0x58` (RU `L2.02626`, `L2.02627`). The two pushes lie inside the arm, in
the non-Pointer branches for building byte +0x40 = 0xf and 0x10 after the
second lookup, and size an object those branches build. The Shop, Inn and
Pointer paths (`L2.02604`..`L2.02628`) are equal. The lookups (31 and 27 instructions) and
the executor head (151) are equal; the switch tables are equal. Medium that
the arm is the only reader of +0x6c: the record scan ran in RU only, and a
Pointer reached through a Building field or a virtual slot would escape it.
Medium for the class tests and the distance origin (x-1, y-1): `L2.02629`,
`L2.02598`, `L2.02599`, `L2.00486` and `L2.00487` were not read. Medium for
"first" in the lookup (`L2.02601`, `L2.02602`, `L2.02603` unread) and for
the packet meaning of 0x83 and 0x84 (`L2.02566` unread). The step function
has no direct RU caller (a call-target scan found none), so it is reached
through a pointer.

**Unknown.** Which units run this step and how often: a dword scan of RU
and EN `.rdata` and `.data` for `L2.00028` and for the vtable that holds it,
then the caller of that slot, would settle it. What `L2.02566` does with 0x83
and 0x84 and what their receivers open: a read of `L2.02566` in both roots.

### R2-ENGINE-519

A pattern scan for `mov dword [reg+0x54], 15` with an 8-bit displacement
(`c7 ?? 54 0f 00 00 00`) over `.text` finds one site per root: RU
`L2.02630`, EN `L2.02631`. It is in the order handler RU `L2.02632`, EN
`L2.02633` (47 instructions, equal after masking). With the order record
r = [unit+0x1c4] the handler calls `L2.02567(unit, word r+0xa, byte r+0x14)`
on [this+0xa50]:

- nonzero: state 15 when the unit is not in state 15; when it is,
  `L2.01576(unit)`;
- zero: `L2.02634(unit, r+0xa, r+0x14)` and state 1.

`L2.02567` returns 1 when the first byte of the record at [unit+0x1c0]
equals the low byte of `L2.02635(unit, word)` and the low byte of
`L2.01522` applied to `L2.01521(word)` on the unit's position object is at
or below the byte argument; it returns 0 otherwise. It calls `L2.00490`
first and ignores its result. Its helpers `L2.00490`, `L2.02635`,
`L2.01521` and `L2.01522` are unread, so "arrival" and "range" are names
for this comparison, not read facts. `L2.01576` calls `L2.01585`
and `L2.02636`, which calls `L2.01584` (clears r+0x50) and the unread
`L2.02637`, then stores r+0x50 = 1. It does not store to unit +0x54, and
nothing read shows that the order ends. R2-ENGINE-363 calls `L2.01576`
"reset/replan" and R2-ENGINE-504 says the order dispatch `L2.01725` resets
through it; this claim reads the same function and adds the store of 1. The handler's one direct caller
is the arm `L2.02638`..`L2.02639` of an order dispatch, which passes r+0x68
as the second argument. A dword scan of RU `.rdata` for the handler finds
no table entry and a call-target scan finds one direct caller; both scans
are generation-1 receipts that were not reproduced, and `.data` was not
scanned for the handler.

So a unit in state 15 reaches the Pointer lookup of R2-ENGINE-518 on the
actor steps between the handler call that sets state 15 and the next
handler call.

**Confidence.** High for the handler body, read in both roots. Medium that
it is the only producer of state 15: the pattern covers one encoding; a
store from a register or with a 32-bit displacement is outside it. Medium
for "arrives" and "range" (the helpers of `L2.02567` are unread), for the
scan results above and for the reading of the `L2.01576` call as an order
finish (R2-ENGINE-363 and R2-ENGINE-504 read it as reset or replan). The
handler's order code, the dispatch head and the helpers `L2.02634` and
`L2.02637` were not read; the dispatch window and the helpers are RU only.

**Unknown.** Which order code reaches this handler and which producer
issues it (a player command, computer play or a script): a window over
the dispatch head (RU `L2.02640`) and a call-target scan of its function
would settle it. Whether the actor step runs once or more between two
handler calls: the callers of the step (R2-ENGINE-518 Unknown). What
`L2.02567` tests: reading `L2.00490`, `L2.02635`, `L2.01521`, `L2.01522`.

**Amended.** R2-ENGINE-607 names the order: unit order 0xf, whose planner
stores prepared byte 0xf; index 14 of the prepared table reaches the arm
`L2.02638` (EN `L2.02984`) and this handler. Order 0xf is set from message
type 0x24, which the client's structure click sends (R2-ENGINE-606); other
producers of order 0xf were not searched. `L2.01521` returns word +2 of
its object (R2-ENGINE-607).

### R2-ENGINE-520

The compiler (RU `L2.00116`, EN `L2.00201`) counts the action nodes of
map+0x40 whose signed dword +0x40 is below 0x10002 (`cmp`, `jge` at RU
`L2.02641`) and sizes the compiled array [[`L2.02609`]+0xeab0] to that
count (through `L2.02642`, unread). Its compile loop skips nodes at or above 0x10002
(0x10002 goes to the u16 collection of R2-ENGINE-042) and fills slot s.
After the parameter loop, when the compile flag is 1 it maps node ID +0x44
to s, stores the operation at slot+4 and s at slot+0, and adds 1 to s (RU
`L2.02643`..`L2.02644`). A failed reference clears the flag (R2-ENGINE-044).
The increment at `L2.02645` follows `cmp [ebp-0x11c], 1; jne L2.02646`
(`L2.02643`); the target `L2.02646`, the compile loop between `L2.02647`
and `L2.02648` and the log path are in navigation windows only, so that
the flag test is the only increment and that a failed node keeps s are
Medium. The executor's copy `L2.02520` takes slot i at array +4 + 0x74*i
with no bound test; the slot accessor `L2.02565` that the compiler uses
against it is unread.

The type-4 pass counts the first e2 nodes with the same signed test
(R2-ENGINE-512). Pointer +0x6c therefore equals the slot of node e2 when
every earlier node below 0x10002 compiled; with f earlier failures, slot
+0x6c holds a later node, or a slot no node filled (Medium, as above).
That the slot "names node e2" rests on `L2.02565` against `L2.02520`. The pass walks the
nodes with `L2.02498` without a null test, so an e2 above the node count
has no defined result in the bodies read.

**Confidence.** High for the count loop (70 instructions), the commit
(41) and `L2.02520` (20), which are equal in EN and RU after masking.
Medium for the compile-slot rule (only a successful compile advances s;
a failed node keeps s) and for a campaign entry's node: whether earlier
nodes compile depends on the references each resolves at mission start.

**Unknown.** Whether another store to the slot counter exists and what the
failure branch does: a generation window over `L2.02647`..`L2.02649` in
both roots with a census of the stores to `[ebp-0x9c]` would settle it.

### R2-ENGINE-521

The Shop vtable (RU `L2.02546`) differs from the Building vtable in slots
0, 1, 2 and 5; the Inn vtable (RU `L2.02544`) in slots 0, 1 and 5. Shop
slot 2 (`L2.02551`) transfers only +0xc0 after the Building Serialize
(R2-ENGINE-512). Shop slot 5 (`L2.02650`) calls method `L2.02651` (unread) of the
0x98 helper at +0x6c. Inn slot 5 (`L2.02652`) calls
`L2.02366(member, -1)` (unread) for each member of the list at +0xa8 whose [+0x14]
byte +0x43 is 0, adds 1 to +0xd8, and when +0xd8 is above 0x78 (unsigned: `ja`) and
`L2.02502(+0xa8)` is 0 calls `L2.02653` for each entry of +0x6c and clears
+0xd8. `L2.02502`, `L2.02653` and `L2.02366` are unread, and the unit of
the +0xd8 count is unknown. The Building slot 5 (`L2.02654`), used by Pointer, does its work when dword
[[`L2.01317`]] modulo 60 is 0 (`L2.02655`..`L2.02656`, a fact of that body;
the Shop and Inn bodies carry no such test): when byte +0x40 is 15 or 16 and signed word
+0x42 is at or above 0 and below word +0x44, it adds 1 to +0x42 and calls
`L2.02657(object, 0, 0)` on `L2.02608`.

None of these bodies reads Shop +0x70..+0xbc (the 11b fields) or Inn
+0xc4..+0xd4 (the 11a fields). No type-4 record of the Shop or Inn kinds
occurs in the 46 campaign maps per root (R2-ASSET-123), so the campaign
builds no object of either class from its maps.

**Confidence.** High for the bodies listed, read in RU. No call site of
virtual slot 5 (`call [reg+0x14]`) and no caller of these bodies was read,
so nothing here says when slot 5 runs. Unknown for the readers of the 11b
and 11a fields and for their effect; EN was not read for these classes.

A navigation listing past Shop slot 5 shows further short Shop methods
that pass +0x6c to helper methods; they carry no confidence here.

**Unknown.** The helper methods `L2.02651`, `L2.02366`, `L2.02653` and
`L2.02502`, the receivers of packets 0x83 and 0x84, and the other methods
of both classes. A displacement scan of `.text` for +0x70..+0xbc and
+0xc4..+0xd4 with the receivers classified by class, and the helper
methods in both roots, would settle them. The event that runs slot 5: a
call-site scan of `call [reg+0x14]` over `.text` and the callers of the
Building slot-5 body. The root `.alm` maps (R2-ASSET-084), where the
multiplayer shops and inns would be placed, are not censused; the census
generator of R2-ASSET-123 over them would settle which kinds they build.

**Amended.** R2-ENGINE-536 reads a reader of Inn +0xc4..+0xd4 (the offer generator, called from one Inn method whose receiver is inferred from addresses, Medium) and R2-ENGINE-539 a reader of Shop +0x70..+0xbf (the fill, through helper +0x94). Other readers are Unknown (R2-ENGINE-512). The root `.alm` maps hold Shops and Inns (R2-ASSET-130). The slot-5 caller stays unread.

### R2-ENGINE-523

The 0x468 case (EN `L2.00827`, RU `L2.02658`; the case named by
R2-ENGINE-076 and R2-ENGINE-411) calls the Scenario current-location
pointer, then the record getter (EN `L2.02659`, RU `L2.02660`), which
returns DWORD +0 of the record. When it is 1 the case reads GetVar(512+i)
and GetVar(532+i) for i=0..19, appends i+1 when both are nonzero, calls the
creator (EN `L2.00175`, RU `L2.00177`) with GetVar(0x300) and the list when
the list is nonempty, calls `L2.00466` with 0 on app +0xd0, then calls
mission entry with 0 in either case. Any other value calls `L2.02197` with
two zeros on app +0xd0 and the town entry `L2.00266`. The DLL record setter
`D2.00086` stores its first argument at +0 and its second at +4;
ScenarioGetCurrentLocation returns the current pointer `D2.00007`;
ScenarioIsMissionAvailable accepts records whose getter `D2.00010` returns 1
and ScenarioIsTownAvailable those that return 2. ScenarioLeaveLocation
sends type 2 to `D2.00013` and every other type to the ordinary departure
`D2.00012`.

A call-target pass over each `.text` found one direct call of the creator
per root, at EN `L2.02661` and RU `L2.02662`, and a dword pass over each
`.rdata` found no entry address. The pass sees `E8` calls and `.rdata`
words only. The load entry and the 0x42f and 0x457 routes into mission
entry (R2-ENGINE-411) therefore create no hire among the routes the pass
can see.

**Confidence.** High for the predicate, the loop, the order of the calls
and the DLL bodies, read in both roots (entry case equal after masking
addresses and frame slots, except one exception-state byte). Medium that
type 1 means a mission: the getter `D2.00010` was not read and the meaning
rests on the export names. Medium for the single route: the call-target
pass is a navigation receipt and sees no register call or pointer outside
`.rdata`.

**Unknown.** Which senders post 0x468 and whether the 0x42f and 0x457
routes can follow a hire selection. The caller pass does not see `E9`
jumps, `.data` words, immediate operands, register calls, or the RU
section `.st1073`; an `E9`, `.data` and immediate-operand scan of both
roots plus the RU `.st1073` section would settle the single route. The
senders of 0x468 are settled by a scan of the calls that post the literal
0x468.

**Amended.** R2-ENGINE-533 lists the senders of 0x468 (map travel end and
the victory arm) and adds `E9`, `.data` and RU `.st1073` passes that find no
other reference to the creator; the single route stays Medium because
register calls are not excluded.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2066](../experiments/EXP-2066-rom2-hire-entry/)

### R2-ENGINE-524

The creator's object `L2.00811` (RU `L2.02561`) holds the Humans collection
at +0xa0 (`L2.00148`) and the Units collection at +0x8c (`L2.00146`). Lookup
`L2.02663` (RU `L2.02560`) walks Humans from the last index down to index 1
and returns the first index whose row passes `L2.02664` and whose parameter
0x18 (24) equals the key; `L2.02665` (RU `L2.02666`) does the same on Units
with parameter 0x37 (55). Index 0 is never returned. For each input word
masked to 16 bits the creator looks up 10000+10*ID in Humans, then in Units,
and remembers which answered. In that table it probes 10000+10*ID+k for
k=1..9 and stops at the first positive index. When one answered it looks
up 9998+10*ID+trunc(stage/10), with the stage signed and divided by 10, and
a nonzero index replaces the base index. A Humans index builds a 0x254-byte
Human from the row's name (`L2.00214`, RU `L2.00130`); a Units index builds
a 0x208-byte Unit (`L2.01063`, RU `L2.00129`).

Applied to the installed rows (R2-ASSET-125), hires 1..7 take the rows of
`hire-template-join.tsv`: at stages 30..110 the row whose name carries the
stage when the family has one (XBowman30, Knight30, Druid60, Troll70, Orc60,
Mage60, MercenaryCatapult at 110), the Base row below it, and at stage 10
or 120 a row of the neighbouring family when its serverID equals the stage
key (hire 2 at stage 10 takes XBowman110, hire 1 at stage 120 KnightBase).
Hires 8..20 have no row in either table, so both lookups return 0 and a Unit
is built from Units index 0.

**Confidence.** High for the lookup bodies and the key arithmetic, read in
both roots and equal after masking. Medium for the join: `L2.02664` and the
parameter accessor `L2.02667` were not read (R2-ENGINE-072 reads the
accessor as base plus 4*index), and the join assumes the native collections
hold the `world.res` rows in census order.

**Unknown.** Whether a hire enters a mission at stage 10 or 120 (the
stage-range reach of R2-SESSION-112 or a named-stage save settles it);
whether a hire ID above 7 is ever selected (the writers of selection and
availability 8..20, the unread part of R2-ENGINE-380); the native join
(a read of `L2.02664`, `L2.02667` and the collection filler).

**Amended.** R2-SESSION-199 narrows the Unknown on hire IDs above 7: no
immediate DLL store makes hires 8..20 available, and after NewGame they stay
unavailable at Medium.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2066](../experiments/EXP-2066-rom2-hire-entry/)

### R2-ENGINE-525

The Human constructor passes the row name with two zero arguments to the
Humans template load (`R2.0088`, RU `R2.0089`). The load stores +0xe = 0,
takes the hero class rule (+0xe = 0x21 or 0x23 plus gender) only when its
second argument is nonzero or the name starts at `Hero`, and otherwise ORs
gender into +0x4b. Its parameter routine (`L2.00219`, RU `L2.00220`) moves
the row's word into +0xe through `L2.02668` after the school skills and
before +0x4b, +0x134, +0x135, +0x49 and +0x4a: the typeID position
(R2-ENGINE-319). The Unit constructor calls the Unit initializer (`L2.01793`,
RU `L2.01794`), which stores +0xe = 0 and calls the Units name parser
(`R2.0086`, RU `R2.0087`); that parser selects the row by name, writes
+0x14c from parameter 55 and calls the Units parameter routine (`L2.02669`,
RU `L2.02341`), whose +0xe reader precedes +0x4b, +0x49 and +0x4a, the
titles typeID, face, tokenSize and movementType at parameters 29..32. The
installed typeIDs are 15 (XBowman), 5 (Knight), 23 (Mage), 100 (Druid), 102
(Troll), 101 (Orc) and 26 (both Catapult rows) (R2-ASSET-125).

The creator then writes WORD +0x14c = ID, +4 = the low word of `L2.02670`,
+0x14 = the owner from `L2.00310` on `L2.00292` (RU `L2.00311` on its
counterpart), appends the actor to owner +0x24, builds a 0x50-byte Group,
appends it to the collection at owner +0x28 and the actor to the Group,
registers both with the map at `L2.01066`, and calls the unit-state sender
(R2-ENGINE-527). The map build's owner builder (`R2.0081`, RU `R2.0024`)
reuses the owner from the same getter for its first row when Session +0x74
is 0 and `L2.00223` returns 1. The Humans template load stores the
parameter-24 word at +0x14c and, for a word above 10000, replaces it with
(word/10)%1000 (`L2.02671..L2.02672`), which equals the hire ID for the
Humans hire rows (hires 1, 2, 6). The Units name parser stores the low word
of parameter 55 unchanged (`L2.02673..L2.02674`), so a Units hire row
(hires 3, 4, 5, 7) leaves the serverID word (10030, 10040, 10050, 10070 ...)
until the creator overwrites it with the ID.

Hires are treated apart from other party members in three read bodies: the
victory transition by class (R2-ENGINE-526); the client availability store
for +0x1dc 1..20 (R2-SESSION-195); and the EN sender. The sender splits on
a virtual call `[obj+0x30]` at `L2.02675`. When it returns zero, a key +4
below 0x6000 with +0x14c above 20 reduces the mask by `&= 0x800000fb` and
`&= ~0x20` (a test hires, 1..20, do not meet and the hero, 21, does), and a
key at or above 0x6000 with Session +0x74 nonzero clears field bit 0x80
(`and al, 0x7f`, `L2.02676..L2.02677`). When it returns nonzero, an actor
whose owner equals the recipient reaches `L2.02678`, where Session +0x74
nonzero clears the same bit. Bit 0x80 is the bit that sends +0x14c
(R2-ENGINE-527). The creator passes the actor's own owner as recipient.

**Confidence.** High for the stores, the reader order and the branch, from
bodies read in both roots (the Humans load and Units parser differ only in
item allocation sizes). Medium for the class values: the parameter index
each sequential reader takes rests on the title order, as in R2-ENGINE-319.
Medium that the owner is the hero's: the getter `L2.00310` returns zero for
an empty collection and otherwise the head element of the Players
collection (`L2.02679..L2.02680`); its callees `L2.02681` and `L2.02682`
and `L2.00223` were not read, so "the hero's" holds only where the map
build's first row reuses it. The sender's mask tests are EN only; the
virtual body behind `[obj+0x30]` and the key `L2.02670` (navigation only)
were not read.

**Unknown.** Other writers of +0xe between creation and the mission end (a
scan of word stores to +0xe and of calls to `L2.02668` would settle it);
the RU sender (its counterpart of `L2.01056`, found by a caller pass over
the RU creator); the owner (a read of `L2.02681`, `L2.02682`, `L2.00223`).

**Evidence.** [EXP-2066](../experiments/EXP-2066-rom2-hire-entry/)

### R2-ENGINE-526

The victory transition (EN `L2.01664`, RU `L2.01833`; R2-ENGINE-412) ends
with a loop over the owners of `L2.00292`. An owner with +0x2c nonzero or a
matching name is removed. For every other owner it walks the +0x24 actor
list: an actor whose zero-extended class +0xe is at least 0x21 and below
0x40 gets HP and mana set to their maxima, +0x13c = 0, the reset `L2.01668`
and five cleared fields; every other actor is passed to `L2.01669` (RU
`L2.01841`), which calls `L2.01670` with it and then the actor's virtual
slot +4 with argument 1. The hire classes 5, 15, 23, 26, 100, 101 and 102
(R2-ENGINE-525) are all outside 33..63, so every installed hire row takes
the detach branch. R2-ENGINE-412 states classes 33..63 only; how Start_
heroes are built, and so their class, is Unknown here.

**Confidence.** High for the loop, the predicate and the detach body, read
in both roots (the RU transition pushes one more argument before a late
call). Medium that each hire is removed from the party: it composes the
class values, which no census of +0xe writers backs, and rests on steps
not read here: `L2.01670` (R2-ENGINE-382 read it at Medium), virtual slot
+4, the world clear (EN `L2.01837`), the map deletion and the first owner
loop that calls ten unread functions (R2-ENGINE-412). Medium that slot +4
with 1 destroys the actor: that body was not read. Defeat reaches the
transition only under R2-ENGINE-412's gate.

**Unknown.** What `L2.01670` removes beyond R2-ENGINE-382's reading (a read
of `L2.01670` and the slot +4 body settles it); the fate of a hire actor
that died earlier in the mission (a read of the death path and of the
first owner loop's ten callees); the class of a Start_ hero (a read of
the hero build path).

**Evidence.** [EXP-2066](../experiments/EXP-2066-rom2-hire-entry/)

### R2-ENGINE-527

The creator's last call per hire passes actor, owner +0x14, -1, 0xffb, 0
and 0 to `L2.01056` on `L2.00994`. In the EN body, a null owner argument
repeats the call for every owner; otherwise the third argument is a field
mask: bit 1 sends +0x94, bit 0x80 sends +0x14c, and the mask is reduced for
some actors: two reductions on the path where the virtual call `[obj+0x30]`
at `L2.02675` returns zero, and a clear of bit 0x80 when Session +0x74 is
nonzero (R2-ENGINE-525). Under bit 0x400000 the fourth argument goes to
`L2.02683`; under bit 0x200000, and only when the actor's owner equals the
recipient, the fifth and sixth go to `L2.00497`. The creator writes no
coordinate, and neither does the sender's body. The hire's cell at mission
start is set elsewhere.

**Confidence.** High for the EN sender's use of its arguments, from its
complete body. The RU sender was not read. The packet writer `L2.02684`
behind "sends" and the virtual body behind `[obj+0x30]` were not read.
Unknown for the cell.

**Unknown.** The cell where a hire stands. Reading the map registration
callees `L2.02685` and `L2.02686`, mission entry `R2.0026` and the map
build's per-actor calls (`L2.00201`, `L2.02687`, `L2.02688`) would settle
it.

**Amended.** R2-ENGINE-529 to R2-ENGINE-532 read the placement bodies: the
join's party placement puts each actor of the owner's list near the party's
start point through the positioning search. That a campaign hire reaches
those bodies is Unknown (R2-ENGINE-530, R2-ENGINE-532).

**Evidence.** [EXP-2066](../experiments/EXP-2066-rom2-hire-entry/)

### R2-ENGINE-529

The party placement routine (EN `L2.01851`, RU `L2.02696`) takes an owner.
It first makes sure the owner's group collection at +0x28 has a first group:
with none it logs `Oops - player has no groups`, builds a 0x50-byte group and
adds it; while the first group is empty and the collection holds more than
one, it removes that group. Then it fixes one start point (x, y) for the whole
party:

- when the receiver's +0x74 is nonzero and owner WORD +0xa6c is nonzero, x is
  its low byte and y its high byte;
- otherwise, when the word list at the receiver's +0xc0 is not empty, it draws
  i = rand(count-1) (`L2.00939`) and takes x and y from the low and high byte
  of word i;
- when x*y is 0 after that, x = rand(70)+30 and y = rand(70)+30, drawn x
  first, and it logs `Warning - no drop location in .alm - random used`.

The receiver is the object whose method this is: assumed the Session object;
its identity with `[L2.00805]` is not read (R2-ENGINE-532). In the EN `rand`
body, rand(n) is 0 for n = 0 and otherwise (rand()*(n+1))>>15, so 0..n; the
RU `rand` (`R2.0021`) is not read. The radius is r = trunc(max(5.0,
sqrt(n)+4.0)) for n = the count of the owner's +0x24 actor list, with the
constants 4.0 and 5.0 read in EN (`L2.02697`, `L2.02698`): 5 for 1..3
actors, 6 for 4..8, 7 for 9..15, if the two unread helpers are the square
root and the truncation. The join (R2-ENGINE-532) clears owner +0xa6c
before it calls this routine.

Three call sites per root reach the routine: the join (EN `L2.02699`, RU
`L2.02700`), the victory transition's first owner loop (EN `L2.02701`, RU
`L2.02702`) and a respawn routine (EN `L2.02703`, RU `L2.02704`). In the EN
bodies read, the last two run only when the +0x74 they test is nonzero.

**Confidence.** High for the control flow, the draw order and the two log
strings (EN `L2.02705`, RU `L2.02706`), read in both roots and equal after
masking addresses and frame slots except the block of R2-ENGINE-530. Medium
for the radius formula: the square root `L2.02707` and the conversion
`L2.02708` were not read in either root and are taken from their use, and
its constants were read in EN only. The `rand` body, and so each draw's
range, is read in EN only. Medium for the caller set: it rests on call-target passes, navigation receipts that see `E8`
calls only, and the +0x74 gates of the two other callers were read in EN
only, in navigation.

**Unknown.** The writer of the +0xc0 drop list and which map record fills it;
the log string names `.alm`. The EN victory transition clears the list
through `L2.02709`, whose callee `L2.02710` was not read. A census of calls
on +0xc0 by every encoding settles it. The RU radius constants (the `fadd`
and `fcomp` operands in `L2.02696` and the 8-byte table they name) and the
RU `rand` `R2.0021` are unread; a window on each settles the RU radius and
draw ranges. The identity of the receiver with the Session object is
unread; the source of `ecx` in the join arm's dispatching routine settles
it.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2067](../experiments/EXP-2067-rom2-hire-placement/)

### R2-ENGINE-530

After fixing the start point and radius (R2-ENGINE-529), the party placement
routine walks the owner's +0x24 actor list from its head. For each actor:

1. EN calls one wrapper (`L2.02711` on the ground grid `L2.01839`, callee
   `L2.02712`) and skips the actor when the returned pointer is that actor.
   RU calls two routines (`L2.01704`, `L2.01705`, on `L2.02538`) after a
   position getter (`L2.01521`). The behaviour of `L2.02712`, `L2.01704` and
   `L2.01705` is not read.
2. It sets the actor's position to (x, y) on the ground grid (`L2.02713`).
3. For the hero, owner +0x38, it calls positioning (R2-ENGINE-531) with
   radius 0; when that fails, and for every other actor, it calls positioning
   with the party radius.
4. On failure it logs `Error - can't place hero from previous mission o...`
   and continues.
5. In every case it appends the actor to the global list `L2.00325`, replaces
   the actor's +0x1c0 object with a new 0xb4-byte object and its +0x1c4
   object with a new 0xb8-byte object (keeping byte +0x78 of the old +0x1c4),
   and passes actor +0x70 to the map `L2.01066` through `L2.02714`.

The hire creator appends each hire to owner +0x24 (R2-ENGINE-525) and writes
no cell (R2-ENGINE-527). If the join runs this routine after the creator,
each hire is placed after the actors already in the list, around the same
start point as the hero; no read shows that order in a campaign.

**Confidence.** High for the loop, the order and the calls other than the
skip, read in both roots. Medium for the skip rule: what its returned
pointer means is not read. Unknown whether a campaign hire is placed here:
no read ties a hire to these bodies. The links are the packet that drives
the join arm, its sender, its dword +0xa in a campaign and the order of the
join and the creator (R2-ENGINE-532), and that no other routine places a
hire. A positioning call-target pass (navigation, `E8` only) found 12
callers per root; two EN callers (`L2.02715`, `L2.02716`) are not
classified and no RU caller is, so another placement of a hire is not
excluded. The creator's writing no cell (R2-ENGINE-527) excludes only one
alternative.

**Unknown.** What `L2.02712`, `L2.01704` and `L2.01705` return and test;
whether an actor whose placement failed is drawn or acts; the route of a
campaign hire to this routine. The arm's packet type and sender, the
dword +0xa and the join-creator order (reads of the dispatching routine and
of the creator's call chain), and the two EN callers, settle the route.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2067](../experiments/EXP-2067-rom2-hire-placement/)

### R2-ENGINE-531

Positioning (EN `L2.00312`, RU `L2.00313`) takes x, y and r as bytes.
With half = trunc(r/2) it sets the actor's position to (x, y), then for
k = 0..trunc(r*r/2)+1:

1. draws y' = y - half + rand(r), then x' = x - half + rand(r) (the range of
   each draw is the EN `rand` body's; RU `rand` `R2.0021` is not read);
2. sets the position through the clamp `L2.02717`, which keeps x in [8, W-9]
   and y in [8, H-9];
3. skips the test when the clamped y is below 12 and Session +0x74
   (read through `[L2.00805]`) is nonzero; otherwise a passing cell test ends the search.

When no random cell passed and r > 0, it scans x' from x-half to x+half
(outer) and y' from y-half to y+half (inner), skipping y' below 12 when
Session +0x74 is nonzero, clamping and testing each. A pass calls the ground
grid's place routine `L2.00314` and returns its result; a failure returns 0
and leaves the actor at the last candidate set, not placed on the grid. With
r = 0 the search tries (x, y) twice and does no scan.

The cell test `L2.02718` reads the actor's footprint size from its virtual
slot +0x1c and runs `L2.02719` for layer 0 and layer 1: each footprint cell
(x+i, y+j) of the layer is checked by `L2.02720`, and any nonzero result
fails the test.

**Confidence.** High for the positioning body's control flow and the order
of the two draws, read in both roots and equal through its `ret` after
masking. The range of each draw is read in EN only: the `rand` body is
unread in RU. High for the EN cell test, its layer loop,
the clamp and the position set; those helpers were read in EN only. Medium
for the meaning of a failed cell: `L2.02720` and the two layer accessors
(`L2.02721`, `L2.02722`) were not read.

**Unknown.** Whether a failed check means another actor, impassable terrain
or both. The RU draw ranges: a window on RU `R2.0021` settles them. Whether
party placement's receiver is the object at `[L2.00805]` (R2-ENGINE-532).

**Evidence.** [EXP-2067](../experiments/EXP-2067-rom2-hire-placement/)

### R2-ENGINE-532

The join routine (EN `L2.02723`, RU `L2.00132`) takes an owner and a flag.
Its receiver (assumed the Session object; its identity with `[L2.00805]` is
not read) supplies the +0x74 test and the +0xc0 list that party placement
reads through `ecx`. It clears owner WORD +0xa6c, and when owner +0x38 (the hero) is null it logs
and returns. After its Session +0x74 branch it calls party placement
(R2-ENGINE-529) when the flag is nonzero and owner byte +0x41 is 0, and then
sets +0x41 = 1 and +0x43 = 1. Its one call site per root (EN `L2.02724`, RU
`L2.02725`) lies in an arm that looks the owner up from WORD +5 in
`L2.00292` and passes flag = (dword +0xa == 0). The arm window begins
inside an instruction and holds no dispatch compare, packet type or class
identity; the arm is not shown to be a server arm.

Writers of byte +0x41 found by a byte-store pattern pass over the EN `.text`:
the victory transition's owner loop (EN `L2.02726`, RU `L2.02727`) stores 0
for every owner it keeps; the owner constructor (`L2.02728`) stores 0; the
join stores 1; two constructors of the class with vtable `L2.02693`
(`L2.02729`, `L2.02730`) store 1. So after a victory every kept owner's next
join with the flag set places its party again.

**Confidence.** High for the join body, the call site read in the arm window
and the transition store, in both roots (the join differs only in one
allocation size, 0x40f EN and 0x410 RU). Medium that the arm holds the
join's only caller: the call-target receipt (navigation 6) is an `E8`-only
pass; jumps, dword references and register calls were not searched. Medium
for the writer list: the pattern pass is an EN navigation receipt, and the
vtable `L2.02693` class is not identified. Unknown that a campaign mission
start reaches the join with the flag set after the hire creator: the packet
that drives the arm, its sender and its dword +0xa were not read. The
+0x74-dependent clauses hold if the receiver is the Session object.

**Unknown.** The packet type of the join arm, its class and when it is sent;
the dword +0xa in a campaign; the order of the join and the creator; the
`ecx` source of the call in the dispatching routine. The population
searched is the two arm windows (46 and 47 lines) and the `E8` call-target
receipt; a window on the dispatching routine's compare and the sender of
the packet settles the first three.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2067](../experiments/EXP-2067-rom2-hire-placement/)

### R2-ENGINE-533

A pattern pass for the bytes `68 04 00 00` over each `allods2.exe` `.text`
finds 3 EN and 41 RU hits. The three `push 0x468` sites per root are:

- map travel end (EN `L2.02731`, RU `L2.02732`), which posts 0x468 with two
  zero arguments and then calls EnterLocation (R2-ENGINE-432);
- the victory arm (EN `L2.02228`, RU `L2.02230`), which posts 0x468 after
  EnterLocation on the first available record when IsTownAvailable(0)
  returns 0 (R2-ENGINE-422);
- EN `L2.02733`, an allocation size passed to operator new, not a message;
  RU `L2.02734` has equal context bytes.

The other 38 RU hits are `add reg, 0x468` field offsets. Passes for the hire
creator's entry (EN `L2.00175`, RU `L2.00177`) as an `E9` target over `.text`
and as a dword over `.text` and `.data` in both roots, and as both over the
RU `.st1073` section, find no hit. With R2-ENGINE-523's single `E8` caller
and empty `.rdata` pass, the 0x468 case is the creator's only route among the
forms searched.

**Confidence.** High for the two sender bodies, read in both roots (map
travel end equal after masking; victory arm equal with frame slots masked).
Medium for the enumeration of three immediate sites per root: the 3 EN and
41 RU hits are navigation receipts, the third EN site is classified from a
navigation window, and the 38 RU `add reg, 0x468` hits are classified from
the bytes before the immediate. Medium that no other code posts 0x468: a
computed or table-held message number is outside the pattern. Medium for the single route: the creator
passes are navigation receipts, and register calls are not excluded. RU
`L2.02734` was not read.

**Unknown.** Register calls that could reach the creator, over `.text` of
both roots; a census of indirect calls whose target register is loaded from
a creator-address source settles them. RU `L2.02734` is unread; a window on
it settles its class.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2067](../experiments/EXP-2067-rom2-hire-placement/)

### R2-ENGINE-535

Readers of actor +0x1a0:

- Unit death (RU `L2.01807`, EN `L2.01806`; the body of R2-ENGINE-410):
  when +0x1a0 is not 0, or the name test `L2.01289` against the string at
  RU `L2.00408` matches, it replaces the bag at +0x7c with a new empty bag
  (`L2.01738`). Only for unit word +0xe at 0x40 or above with +0x1a0 = 0
  does it roll gold (chance parameter 0x26 against rand(100), amount
  parameter 0x27 plus rand(parameter 0x28)) and an item (chance parameter
  0x29, generator parameters 0x2a..0x2c). A nonempty bag or gold drops a
  sack through `L2.01811`. With +0x1a0 set nothing drops.
- The human attacker's experience award skips a victim with +0x1a0 set
  (R2-ENGINE-480; the site RU `L2.02739` lies in a navigation window here,
  Medium). A creature attacker's award (R2-ENGINE-480: its `+0x64`, RU
  `L2.02331`, adds X to its +0x130 and, below 0 health, adds 1 to its
  owner's +0xa48, with no +0x1a0 test in that card) was not read here for
  +0x1a0.
- The Unit save packs +0x1a0 into bits 24..31 of one dword (R2-ENGINE-209;
  RU `L2.02740`); the load sets +0x1a0 to 1 when those bits are not 0 (RU
  `L2.02741`).

Writers:

- Unit init (RU `L2.02742`, EN `L2.02743`) stores 0 in +0x194, +0x198,
  +0x19c and +0x1a0, with +0x138 and +0x148.
- The actor builder stores type-6 0x10 bit 8 (R2-ENGINE-513).
- Two unique-spell arms (R2-ENGINE-459) store 1: RU `L2.02744` (EN
  `L2.02745`) after `L2.01794` and before a placement with radius 6, and
  RU `L2.02746` (EN `L2.02747`) after a successful placement.
- The map build, after the actor builder (RU `L2.02748`..`L2.02749`, EN
  from `L2.02750`), makes the string "Self" (RU `L2.02751`, EN
  `L2.02752`) and passes it to `L2.02753` on the owner collection
  `L2.00293`. When that returns an owner S and Session+0x74 is not 0, then
  for every owner O whose +0x2c is not 0 and whose diplomacy byte
  [`L2.02609`]+0xa8c4+O.id*0x46+S.id has bits 0..2 clear, every unit in
  O's list +0x24 gets +0x1a0 = 1.

The tails of the two unit copy windows (RU `L2.02754`, EN `L2.02755`) are
equal up to register allocation: both free the old +0x200 object, test the
source +0x200, allocate a 0xc-byte object, store it, then copy +0x194,
+0x198, +0x19c and +0x204, and neither copies +0x1a0. Both windows start
inside the function; the head of the copy is unread. In the campaign maps 8
type-6 records per root carry bit 8 (R2-ASSET-132).

A displacement scan of `.text` for 0x1a0 finds 59 sites per root (44
displacements, 15 immediates). The sites above are inside windows read
here, and the actor builder store at RU `L2.02756` (`mov [eax+0x1a0], edx`;
R2-ENGINE-513). Windows at RU `L2.02757` and `L2.02758` show their sites on
Session fields, and `L2.02759` lies in a navigation window. The sites at RU
`0x42a..0x439`, `L2.02760`, `L2.02761` and `0x4d4..0x4da` stay
unclassified.

**Confidence.** High for the death body, the init, the two spell stores
and the map-build loop: committed listings in both roots, equal after
address masking (death body prefix 275 instructions, the window ending at
RU `L2.02762` without a `ret` and the rest of the body resting on
R2-ENGINE-410; init 13, spell stores 20 and 21, map-build window 70).
Medium that the copy omits +0x1a0 in both roots: only the tail windows were
read, the head is unread, and the supporting displacement scan (59 sites
per root, none in this function) is a navigation receipt that does not see
a block copy or register arithmetic. Medium for the award, save and load
sites: navigation windows and the cited claims; the award bounds only the
human attacker's. Medium that `L2.02753` looks up an owner by name (unread),
and for "no other reader or writer" (unclassified sites). The map-build
writer runs only with Session+0x74 set: 0 in a campaign at Medium
(R2-SESSION-198); set in the root maps if they are built by the routine of
R2-ENGINE-509 (Medium; R2-ASSET-130).

**Unknown.** What the name test at `L2.01289` matches: searched the death
window and the string at RU `L2.00408`; reading `L2.01289` in both roots
settles it. What diplomacy bits 0..2 and owner +0x2c mean, and whether the
owner named "Self" flags its own units (the loop does not exclude O = S and
the byte for S toward S is unread): searched the 70-instruction map-build
window in both roots; reading the writers of the table at
[`L2.02609`]+0xa8c4 settles it. The head of the unit copy (RU before
`L2.02754`, EN before `L2.02755`): not read; a window from the function's
first instruction in both roots settles whether it copies +0x1a0. Whether a
creature attacker's award tests +0x1a0: no site of the 59-site RU scan lies
in the code-region range and the body at RU `L2.02331` was not read; reading
it settles it.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2068](../experiments/EXP-2068-rom2-map-records/)

### R2-ENGINE-536

Entry: the Inn method starting at RU `L2.02763` (EN `L2.02764`; the
windows are equal, 60 instructions) takes a unit U and
works on its player P = U+0x14. It calls `L2.02765(P)` and `L2.02766(P)`.
When the second returns nonzero it calls `L2.00058(P)`, looks up P's id
in Inn+0x88 and, when found, sends message 9 through `L2.02767` on
`L2.02608`. Otherwise it calls the generator (RU `L2.02768`, EN
`L2.02769`) with P and then `L2.02770(Inn+0xe0, P, 1)` on `L2.02608`. A
call-target scan of `.text` finds this one call site of the generator per
root (RU `L2.02771`, EN `L2.02772`), and a dword scan of `.rdata` finds no
pointer to it.

The generator gets or creates P's 0x84 list in Inn+0x6c, keyed by P's
id, and leaves it at Inn+0xe0. It returns when `L2.02773(0x11, P id,
Inn+4)` on `L2.02774` or `L2.02775(P)` is nonzero. With H the hero
(P+0x38) and M the largest of 0 and H's words +0xaa..+0xb2, a candidate
unit passes the level window when 3M-50 < L < 3M+75 (both strict), L =
`L2.02776(unit)`. The distance bound B is 0x40 when
`L2.02777([L2.02538])` - 0x10 is below 0x80, else half that value; a
candidate needs the low byte of `L2.02426` (Inn+0x10 to unit +0x10) below
its block's bound.

The class gate on unit word +0xe admits 0x40..0x51 and 0x67..0x6a when
Inn+0xc8 is set, 0x52 up to 0x62 (block 1) or 0x63 (blocks 2 and 4) when
Inn+0xcc is set, and, in blocks 2 and 4 only, values below 0x40 when
Inn+0xc4 is set.

| Block | Ctor | Candidates | Value argument |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | `L2.02778` | units of owners with +0x2c set and unit +0x148 = 0; class gate, level window; counted per class and level byte +0x4b | count 1..9 times a template value |
| 2 | `L2.02779` | see R2-ENGINE-537; class gate, bound B, level window; at most 0x100 | 2 x unit +0x1c |
| 3 | `L2.02780` | see R2-ENGINE-537 | |

A block with candidates allocates one 0x30 offer, picks one candidate by a

being the Inn). Campaign maps build no Inn (R2-ASSET-123); the root maps carry

the template value and the ten constructors; and Medium that the one
direct call is the generator's only route, since a register-indirect

event calls the Inn method.

### R2-ENGINE-537

The actor builder stores type-6 0x10 bits 1, 2 and 4 in actor +0x194,
+0x19c and +0x198 (R2-ENGINE-513); the type-10 pass stores e2 bits 4 and
8 in group +0x48 and +0x4c (R2-ASSET-120), only when Session+0x74 is set
(R2-ENGINE-509). The Inn offer generator (R2-ENGINE-536) reads them as
block populations:

| Block | Population |
|---:|---|
| 2 | units with +0x194 set, of owners with +0x2c set other than the Inn's owner (Inn+0x14) |
| 3 | groups of owner +0x28 lists with +0x48 set; members need the level window, the distance bound and `L2.02773(0xd, group +0x1c)` = 0 |
| 4 | units with +0x19c set, of owners whose diplomacy byte toward P has bit 1; `L2.02773(0xc, unit id)` = 0 |
| 5 | groups with +0x4c set, under the same diplomacy rule |
| 6 | units of the Inn's owner with +0x198 set, +0x13c = 0 and `L2.02773(0xc, id)` = 0 |

EN and RU differ in block 3 only. RU compares the group's owner with the
Inn's owner (RU `L2.02795`, `cmp` with Inn+0x14) and skips the Inn
owner's groups before the +0x48 test at RU `L2.02796`; EN tests +0x48 at
`L2.02797` with no owner test, so EN also offers the Inn owner's groups.
The masked comparison counts 14 differing instructions, all in this
block.

Unit init clears the three actor flags and the unit copy keeps them
(R2-ENGINE-535). In the root maps (R2-ASSET-132) bit 1 is set in 316 EN
and 786 RU type-6 records, bit 2 in 30 and 131, bit 4 in 27 and 57; e2 bit
4 in 358 EN and 937 RU type-10 entries, bit 8 in 67 and 109. The campaign
maps set none of these.

**Confidence.** High for the reads and the EN/RU difference: the
generator was read in both roots. Medium that its receiver is the Inn of
R2-ENGINE-512 (R2-ENGINE-536), so the block populations are the Inn's by
that inference. Medium that the generator is the only reader: the displacement scans for +0x194, +0x198 and +0x19c (22, 15 and
19 RU displacement sites) were classified only inside windows read here,
and group +0x48 and +0x4c were not scanned.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2068](../experiments/EXP-2068-rom2-map-records/)

### R2-ENGINE-538

`L2.02502` (EN `L2.02798`) calls `L2.02799` (EN `L2.02800`) on the same
receiver, which returns its dword +0xc; both bodies are 9 instructions,
equal in the two roots. In the type-10 group function (R2-ENGINE-510) a
group whose value is 0 gets no object; in the object's slot 5 the
re-creation proceeds only when the value is 0 or below (signed; Medium,
from R2-ENGINE-510, whose slot-5 behaviour is Medium: no slot-5 body was

5 calls it on its member list +0xa8 (R2-ENGINE-521).

Slot 5 passes object +0xbc as the third argument of `L2.00313`, the

group's member spread there and EN keeps 0 (R2-ENGINE-511). So RU places

square around the object position; with r = 0 EN tests the centre cell
twice and has no square to scan.

**Confidence.** High for `L2.02502`: both bodies read in both roots.
Medium for the slot-5 re-creation clause (R2-ENGINE-510). Medium that
dword +0xc is a member count: its writers were not read.
Medium for the placement effect: it rests on R2-ENGINE-531 (its rand
ranges were read in EN only) and on slot 5, whose caller is unread.

**Unknown.** Which code calls slot 5 and how often: searched the `.text`
dword scans for the Shop and Inn class records (navigation receipts), whose

### R2-ENGINE-541

Population read: RU `ru-order-setters-a` (L2.02806..L2.02809), `ru-order-setters-b` (L2.02809..L2.00506), `ru-session-methods` (L2.02810..L2.02811) and `ru-message-handler`; EN `en-order-setters-b`. The RU setter windows hold 22 stores of an immediate into `[reg+0x50]` (3 and 19); two are the command-object stores of the helpers L2.01576 and L2.01584. The others write the order code on unit +0x50: 1 (L2.02806, L2.02807), 3 (L2.02812), 0xf and 4 (L2.02809 window), 0xd (L2.02813), 0xe (L2.02814), 0xb (L2.02815), 0xc (L2.02637), 0x17 (L2.02816), 8 (L2.02817), 0x11 (L2.02818), 0xa (L2.02819, L2.02820, L2.02821), 0x16 (L2.01579), 2 (L2.01580), 0x1a (L2.01581), 0x18 (L2.01582), 0x19 (L2.01583).

Each setter calls reset L2.01584 first. Reset calls L2.01585, which copies block byte 0 to byte 1, calls L2.02822 when block word +0x80 is nonzero and differs from the cell, recomputes range byte +0x14, clears support flag +0x60 and block +0x7c, and writes unit state +0x54 = 0; L2.01584 then writes command +0x50 = 0. The setter then writes its parameters (cell word +0xa for orders 2 and 4; target +0x28, spell +0x30 and range +0x14 for order 0xd; point word +0x3c, spell +0x30 and range for order 0xe; a target pointer for the others) and prepared byte +8: 0 at the ends of all setters read except the two order-1 setters (L2.02806, L2.02807), which store 1 at RU L2.02823 and L2.02824 (17 stores of 0 in the b window, L2.02825 to L2.02826, and one at L2.02827). The order code is on unit +0x50; parameters and prepared byte +8 are on the command object at unit+0x1c4. A setter replaces those stored values at once; the setter windows hold no write to a pending-order field.

Primary byte +9 stores in all RU windows read: 4 (L2.01721); 0 (L2.02828, L2.02829, L2.02830, L2.01723, L2.02831; L2.02832 and L2.02833 clear it only from 0xff); 0xff (L2.02834); 3 (L2.02835, L2.02836); 1 (L2.02837); 2 (L2.02838, L2.02839). None is in a setter.

Input chain: the message handler (RU L2.02840, jump table L2.02841, 21 entries indexed by message byte +9 minus 0x12, 17 of them not the default) calls session methods that apply L2.02842 to the selected list (reset L2.01584 and command +0x38 = 0 per unit) and then a setter: type 0x12 reaches L2.02816 (0x17), 0x13 reaches L2.01581 (0x1a), 0x14 reaches L2.01579 (0x16), 0x17 reaches L2.02815 (0xb), 0x18 reaches L2.02637 (0xc), 0x1d reaches L2.02819 (0xa), 0x1f (cast) reaches L2.02814 (0xe), 0x21 reaches L2.01580 (2), 0x24 reaches L2.02809. Types 0x16, 0x19, 0x1a and 0x1c reach L2.02843, L2.02844 or L2.02845, which call L2.02806 or L2.02812 (orders 1 and 3); their inner arms were read as call lists only. No window read calls L2.02813 (order 0xd).

**Confidence.** High for the setter bodies and the reset in RU; the EN setters of the b window (`en-order-setters-b`) are equal after masking (R2-ENGINE-548); the EN setters of orders 1 and 3 were not read. Medium that no pending-order field exists outside the setter windows (command word +0xb0, below) and that these are all the input routines: the callers rest on RU handler arms and one call-target receipt of navigation run 1; a call through a pointer is outside them.

**Unknown.** The inner arms of L2.02843, L2.02844, L2.02845; the callers of L2.02813; the EN jump table. Command word +0xb0: the executor, with +9 zero and `L2.00490` returning nonzero (RU L2.02846..L2.02847), passes the word's two bytes to L2.00093 and clears it; L2.02848 calls L2.00093 too. No setter, session or message-handler window writes +0xb0; its writer and L2.00093 are unread, so it may hold a queued target the setters do not touch. Reading the writer and L2.00093 settles it.

**Amended.** The command word +0xb0 is a destination cell copied from a cell record of kind 0x17 and consumed by the executor at +9 = 0; it is not a queued order (R2-ENGINE-557, Medium for completeness of its writers). The planner side includes the direct +9 clears and setter calls in R2-ENGINE-554 and R2-ENGINE-555. Unit +0x50 is the selector order code; command-object +0x50 is a separate field. The inherited RU setter listing shows L2.01576 -> L2.02636 -> L2.02637, which stores unit +0x50 = 0xc at L2.02881; L2.02882 then stores command-object +0x50 = 1. The latter is not unit order 1. No new setter acquisition was made. The ownership correction is recorded in `claims/retracted.md`.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2069](../experiments/EXP-2069-rom2-order-machine/RESULTS.md)

### R2-ENGINE-542

RU `ru-executor` (L2.00506..L2.02849, 467 instructions, 1719/1719 bytes decoded) and EN `en-executor` (467) are equal after masking. The actor step calls it at RU L2.01569 when `L2.01570` returns 0 (R2-ENGINE-399). It sets unit state +0x54 = 0 unless the state is 2 or 15, installs primary 4 when effect mask +0x144 & 0x40000 and +9 is 0 (R2-ENGINE-399), then indexes jump table L2.02849 (6 arms) through byte table L2.02850 by +9 minus 1, guarding only values above 0xfe (L2.02851): 1 reaches the strike arm L2.02852 (state 3), 2 the cast arm L2.02853 (state 13 when command +0x5c is nonzero, else 14), 3 the step arm L2.02854 (call L2.02848, state 1), 4 the hold arm L2.01722 (state 27, clears +9 when the mask bit is gone). The 16 cells read (L2.02850..L2.02855) hold 0, 1, 2, 3 and twelve 5s, which select the clear arm L2.02856 for +9 from 5 to 16. The sixth arm L2.02857 (state 27, +9 kept) is reached by no cell read. The strike and cast arms increment phase byte +0x15 and clear +9 and state when the phase is above 2 and completion byte +0x136 is nonzero. With +9 zero it indexes the 15-entry table L2.01571 by prepared byte +8 minus 1; prepared 3, 13 and 14 do nothing. After a handler it clears block +0x98 when set and replans: order 1 calls L2.02858, order 0xa re-aims, order 0x18 writes +9 = 0xff, otherwise +8 = 0 and L2.02425 runs.

**Confidence.** High for the control flow of the executor and the arms for +9 of 1 to 4 (complete local listing; cells read in both roots, EN equal RU minus 0xa039). Medium that any other +9 value clears: 239 of the 255 byte-table cells (L2.02855..L2.01571) were not read, and the executor itself stores +9 = 0xff at L2.02834 (order 0x18). Medium for the meaning of L2.02848 and L2.00490 (R2-ENGINE-546).

**Unknown.** The 239 unread byte-table cells (L2.02855..L2.01571) in both roots, which fix the arm for +9 from 17 to 255, including 0xff and the sixth arm L2.02857. The planner call schedule (R2-ENGINE-549).

**Amended.** All 255 byte-table cells are read in both roots (R2-ENGINE-553): +9 of 5 to 254 reaches the clear arm L2.02856, which also sets state 27, and +9 = 255 reaches the sixth arm L2.02857 (state 27, +9 kept). The statement that every other +9 value clears is narrowed accordingly (`claims/retracted.md`). The tail at L2.02883 runs after every arm, not only after the prepared handlers.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2069](../experiments/EXP-2069-rom2-order-machine/RESULTS.md)

### R2-ENGINE-543

Prepared byte 8 (handler L2.01552) and 9 (L2.02859) call the cast initializer L2.01575 or L2.02860 when the range helper (L2.01574, L2.02567) admits, else an approach step (L2.01577, L2.02634). The initializers write +9 = 2, phase +0x15 = 0, state 13 (target) or 14 (point), unit +0x5c (target) or +0x60/+0x61 (point), +0x64 (spell), and, when the support flag +0x60 is zero, call L2.01576 (state 0, command +0x50 = 1). Each later executor step sets state 13 or 14 and increments the phase. At phase 3 the arm posts a 21-dword record through L2.01727 (type 2 with a target, type 3 with a point); that callee was not read.

The actor step (RU L2.00028), substate +0x58: substate 0 calls the cast routine L2.00027 (target: L2.00029; point: L2.00030); a nonzero return sets +0x136 = 0, substate 5 and counter +0x6c = byte +0x134; a zero return leaves substate 0 and the call repeats at the next step. Substate 5 decrements +0x6c; at 0 it calls L2.00035 (target) or L2.00034 (point), clears unit +0x64 and +0x68, sets substate 7 and a count from byte +0x135, weapon and speed terms and the result of R2.0021(3); substate 7 decrements and at 0 sets substate 0 and +0x136 = 1. The executor then ends the cast. State 3 (strike) shares the substate machine; a mage with a staff in state 3 enters state 13 with the staff spell.

**Confidence.** High for the local control flow in RU (actor step, executor and cast routine complete; EN executor and cast routine equal after masking; EN actor step differs in two item-field offsets and two allocation sizes). Medium for the stage meaning: L2.01727, L2.00035 and L2.00034 were not read.

**Unknown.** What L2.01727 does at phase 3 and what the apply routines do.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2069](../experiments/EXP-2069-rom2-order-machine/RESULTS.md)

### R2-ENGINE-544

The cast routine L2.00027(spell, caster, target, x, y) (RU `ru-cast-routine`, 329 instructions; EN equal after masking): when the caster is a mage (L2.00044) and has no item (+0x68 zero), it returns 0 if spell cost word +0xc is above signed mana +0x9a, else subtracts the cost at RU L2.02808..L2.02861. It then builds the delivery, L2.02155 for a target spell and L2.02156 for a point spell, with a delay from distance and speed (R2-ENGINE-017), or the Prismatic path for kind 11. The subtraction precedes the wind-up and is made once per call that reaches the delivery. One path returns 0 after the subtraction: at RU L2.02862..L2.02863 the routine returns 0 when the spell object's +4 (the row pointer of R2-ENGINE-017) is 0. After a zero return the actor step calls the routine again at its next step, so on that path the subtraction would repeat; whether +4 can be 0 for a spell the book holds is unread. The executor, actor step and cast routine windows hold no instruction that adds to +0x9a.

### R2-ENGINE-559

The ROM2 EN executor, its 255-cell byte table, six-entry jump table and 15-entry prepared jump table equal the RU ones after masking or a constant shift; the +0xb0 and +9 store shapes agree.

**Population read.** `evidence/en-ru-compare.tsv` (`ru-executor` and `en-executor`: 467 of 467 instructions equal, masked as in `compare_en_ru.py`), `evidence/en-ru-tables.tsv` (255 of 255 byte cells; 6 of 6 and 15 of 15 jump cells equal after 0xa039), `evidence/derived/plusb0-stores.tsv` (4 byte, 4 word and 34 dword stores per root) and the EN +9 immediates at L2.02899..L2.02900, equal in sequence to the RU executor and handlers.

**Confidence.** High for the bodies and tables listed. Medium for behaviour of the masked branch distances. Bodies read in RU only (planners, the L2.00093 consumer, the L2.02922 writer, the movement helpers): EN Unknown, settled by the same ranges in EN.

**Unknown.** The EN counterparts of the RU ranges in R2-ENGINE-555 and R2-ENGINE-557.

**Format surface.** None.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2070](../experiments/EXP-2070-rom2-order-cells/RESULTS.md)

### R2-ENGINE-560

The read RU setters store the order at once without directly writing primary +9. While the executor handles a nonzero primary arm, it does not dispatch prepared +8 there. This local fact does not settle whether the action or stored order survives the common tail and callees.

**Population read.** Composed from R2-ENGINE-541, 542, 546 and 553 through 558. Strike (1), cast (2), step (3), hold (4) and 255 reach their acquired primary arms; the arms converge at L2.02883. The 5..254 arm directly clears +9 and sets state 27 (High local write, R2-ENGINE-553), but the common tail can write +9 = 0xff for unit order 0x18 with block +0x98 set. Other tail paths clear +8, call reset or call L2.02425 and its unread callee L2.02406. The flag-writer receipt is navigation only and does not establish when the flag coexists with an arriving order.

Prepared dispatch requires an admitting executor entry (no L2.02460 return), no hold reinstall at L2.01721, +9 still zero and a valid nonzero +8. A zero +8 bypasses dispatch at L2.02918..L2.02919. Order-1 setters prepare 1; the others store 0 and require a planner pass. Conditional +0xb0 consumption precedes this test, but its call does not guarantee relocation or handler success. Clearing +9 during a primary arm does not dispatch +8 in that same arm.

**Confidence.** Medium for the order-by-state composition, including new-order retention and eventual execution. High remains only on the direct local writes cited above. Planner closure, inherited actor/reset effects and unread callees prevent a stronger guarantee.

**Unknown.** Planner cadence; actor-step substates and reset effects for a new order; common-tail/flag coexistence; effects of L2.02406 and movement callees L2.02876/L2.02410/relocation helpers; structure state 15; L2.01727. Joining those paths and the admitting +8 preparation would settle the remaining cells.

**Amended.** The universal non-interruption and next-call execution clauses are narrowed in `claims/retracted.md`; the local primary-arm observations remain.

**Format surface.** Command object bytes +8, +9; `formats/rom2-autocast/format.md`.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2070](../experiments/EXP-2070-rom2-order-cells/RESULTS.md)

### R2-ENGINE-561

Cells of the ROM2 order machine that EXP-2070 leaves Unknown: the return of 0 after the mana subtraction (L2.02948), the per-order choice among the +8 constants of each planner, the planner cadence, the structure cell, and the EN counterparts of the planner and +0xb0 ranges.

**Confidence.** Unknown.

**Unknown.** (1) Whether the spell object's +4 is 0 for a player's cast (R2-ENGINE-544): not read, the construction of the spell object is the window that settles it. (2) The branch conditions inside L2.01530, L2.02907, L2.02873, L2.02874, L2.02439, L2.01731: listings exist, conditions unread. (3) The caller of L2.01724 and the callers of L2.02908 and L2.02885 (R2-ENGINE-558). (4) The structure order at state 15 (L2.02632). (5) The 139 unclassified RU byte-immediate +9 stores and the 34 dword +0xb0 stores per root. (6) The EN counterparts of the RU planner, consumer and writer ranges. (7) The apply bodies, L2.01727 and the effects of unread L2.02876, L2.02410 and relocation helpers (R2-ENGINE-549 items 2 to 4). RU L2.02848 through L2.02884 and L2.01578 are acquired local movement flow, not unread bodies. (8) Common-tail +0x98 coexistence with a new order, reset effects and unread L2.02406; the acquired local clears do not settle interruption. Read those callees and join flag and preparation paths to settle the composition.

**Amended.** The clause correction is recorded in `claims/retracted.md`; the remaining local facts stand.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2070](../experiments/EXP-2070-rom2-order-cells/RESULTS.md)

raw x86 listings committed under the experiment's `out/` and `out-ru/` and
reproduced against their Git blobs. Addresses are EN unless marked RU.

and `text/unitname.txt` (R2-ASSET-010, R2-ASSET-145) and the Humans
parameter order of R2-ENGINE-319, read under the existing grammar; no
stored layout changes. Card values attributed to "the shots" are
observations read from the published EXP-2071 catalogue shots s3.21, s3.33
and s3.34 (crossbowman, peasant, mage; R2-SESSION-203) and from no
committed output.

### R2-ENGINE-577

Left painter `L2.00745` (RU `L2.02951`) draws the card only when the
application word +0x5d8 (RU +0x63c) is 2 and the selected actor is not
null. When actor flags +0x1b8 bit 0x40 is clear it calls the shared sheet
`L2.01119` (RU `L2.02952`) with the actor as `this`; the painter's head
pushes 0xa0 and 0xee, and the rectangle passed comes from `L2.01491` and
`L2.02953`. The fallback actor of `R2.0069` sets bit 0x40 (flags 0x56),
so a fallback actor shows no sheet.

The sheet prints, by the main.txt label key it pushes before each value:

| Label (main.txt) | Value | Format |
|---|---|---|
| 15 Body | byte +0x144 | `%d` |
| 16 Agility | byte +0x147 | `%d` |
| 17 Mind | byte +0x145 | `%d` |
| 18 Spirit | byte +0x146 | `%d` |
| 19 Health | words +0x104, +0x108 | `%d/%d` |
| 20 Mana | words +0x148, +0x14a | `%d/%d` |

The grade is 7 when the actor's owner word (+0x14)+4 is 0, when helper
`L2.02954` returns its bit 8 set, or when global `L2.00989` is nonzero;
otherwise it is the byte at world(+0xe8)+0x3f70+NPC word, halved, for NPC
words 1..0x9ff, else 0. `L2.02954` and `L2.02955` both call `L2.02956`,
whose body was not read; "relation" names their use, not a read table.
The four attributes need grade 5 or more; HEALTH and MANA grade 1 or more,
with no class test, so the code prints MANA from +0x148/+0x14a for a
fighter as well; the damage block grade 3 or more; the closing lines grade
7 (R2-ENGINE-580).

Relation to existing claims. It settles R2-ENGINE-246's Unknown stat
drawing for the generic inn and R2-ENGINE-388's display record for this
caller: the record is the client actor itself.

**Confidence.** High for the painter, the fields, the keys and the grade
compares: complete EN left painter and sheet listings, pushed operands and
branch conditions. Medium for what the grade inputs mean, which rests on
the unread `L2.02956`.

**Unknown.** The callee `L2.01492` that places the rectangle, the body of
`L2.02956` and the grade byte table's writer.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2073](../experiments/EXP-2073-rom2-town-persons/)

### R2-ENGINE-578

The inn resolves each talk entry's NPC word through `R2.0071`, which
returns the first unit of the controlled collection whose word +0x1dc
equals it (R2-ENGINE-247, R2-ENGINE-051). A client unit's +0x1dc comes
from the server unit's +0x14c (R2-ENGINE-069), which a Humans template
load sets from serverID (parameter 24) or, above 10000, from
(serverID/10)%1000 (R2-ENGINE-072, R2-ENGINE-319).

The census read the installed client `world.res` `data/data.bin` of each
root: every Humans row by parameter 24 with that transform, and every Units
row by parameter 55, low word. It prints matching rows only:

| NPC word | Humans row (ordinal) | Body, Agility, Mind, Spirit | School skills 1..5 | typeID | face | ManaMax |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 207 | NPC07_2 (49) | 32, 32, 28, 22 | 12, 23, 4, 9, 48 | 15 | 4 | -1 |
| 2108 | 2U_PeasantMale (217) | 25, 20, 25, 20 | 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 | 1 | 46 | -1 |
| 517 | M141_MageTooth (170) | 35, 40, 45, 50 | 0, 99, 99, 0, 0 | 24 | 4 | 447 |

The selection for 97 printed no row in either root. The EN and RU census
rows are equal. The four attributes and the five skills equal the values
on the three shots, and typeID gives the heading's type line
(R2-ENGINE-581).

**Confidence.** High for the three printed rows in the two installed
client payloads. Medium for the absences (no other row for 207, 2108 or
517, no row for 97): the committed output prints no row counts and no
empty selection. Medium that the live patrons are units built from these
rows: the server routine that creates them in town was not read, and a
packet's optional key word can also set +0x1dc (R2-ENGINE-069).

**Unknown.** The creator of the town NPC units and its call. Reading the
callers of the serverID lookup `L2.02663` (`L2.02957`, `L2.02958`) would
settle it.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2073](../experiments/EXP-2073-rom2-town-persons/)

### R2-ENGINE-579

Evaluated on R2-ENGINE-578's rows with R2-ENGINE-290's arithmetic:
HPmax = trunc(trunc(Body*k + log1.1(E/5000+1)*k) * (1.1^Body/100+1)),
k 2 for a fighter and 1 for a mage; mana with Spirit and k 1/2, only when
the mana field is nonzero; E the sum of T(s) = trunc((1.1^s-1)*1000)
over the five school skills (R2-ENGINE-485). A row with ManaMax above 0
is a mage (R2-ENGINE-319).

| Patron | E | HEALTH | MANA | On the shots |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| crossbowman | 107930 | 156 | 0 | 156/156, 0/0 |
| peasant | 0 | 55 | 0 | 55/55, 0/0 |
| mage | 25053658 | 158 | 604 | 158/158, 604/604 |

Template load sets HP and mana to their maxima (R2-ENGINE-319), shown as
current/maximum. Including Skill.General in E would give the mage 163 and
623, which the shot does not show. The "On the shots" column is an
observation read from the published shots (rows of the record that crop
them; no committed output); the MANA 0/0 rows of the crossbowman and the
peasant are not in R2-SESSION-203's value column.

**Confidence.** Medium: every value matches, but the comparison values
are observations not reproducible from the committed record, and the
server recompute for these units, the experience sum's population and the
packet copy into the client fields +0x104..+0x14a were not read here.

**Unknown.** The client writer of +0x104, +0x108, +0x148 and +0x14a.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2073](../experiments/EXP-2073-rom2-town-persons/)

### R2-ENGINE-580

At the end of the sheet two lines are tested in order:

| main.txt line | EN / RU text | Position | Predicate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 190 | spellcaster / использует магию | (L+0x4a, T+0xae) | flags +0x1b8 bit 1 clear, dword +0x1c nonzero, grade 7 |
| 191 | Armor piercing / игнорирует броню | (L+0x4a, T+0xba) | flags bits 0x11 clear, byte +0x156 nonzero, grade 7 |

### R2-ENGINE-581

The sheet calls `L2.02949` on the actor's string +0xec (`L2.02959..L2.02960`);
when the result is nonzero it draws +0xec at (R-0x58, T+0x12) and string
+0xf8 at (R-0x58, T+0x1c). The body of `L2.02949` was not read; that a
nonzero result means "+0xec not empty" is inferred from the shots
(two-line mercenary headings, one-line peasant heading). Otherwise, when
flags +0x1b8 & 0x11 is nonzero, the first line is main.txt 84
(Mercenary / Наемный) if `L2.02955` returns bit 0 clear, or main.txt 83
(Enemy / Вражеский) if it is set and +0x24 is below 0x40; `L2.02955`
calls the unread `L2.02956`. The second line, at T+0x1c (`L2.02961`),
follows both arms of the flags test and is the type name. The type name
`L2.01929` returns pool line base+type, where `L2.02962` set the base of
`main\text\unitname.txt` to the pool count at its load and appended one
entry per CRLF line; the startup sequence loads main.txt first. Type names
are therefore unitname.txt lines.

Patrons. On the shots, the crossbowman's and the mage's cards draw
MERCENARY on the first line and CROSSBOWMAN or MAGE on the second:
unitname.txt lines 15 and 24, their rows' typeIDs. PEASANT is drawn on the
first line only (glyph rows 19..26 of s3.33; the other cards' second line
is rows 29..37), read as the +0xec branch. These are observations read
from the published shots by crops recorded in the consultation record,
with no committed output.

RU by the same rule, reading the RU text lines: НАЕМНЫЙ АРБАЛЕТЧИК and
НАЕМНЫЙ МАГ (Наемный, Арбалетчик, Маг), with the letter case the RU
font draws.

**Confidence.** High for the call order, the label keys and the type line
source in EN. Medium for the polarity of `L2.02949` and the relation bit
(unread helpers), for the patron headings (observations from published
shots), and for the RU headings (the RU sheet is equal after masking; the
RU text loader was not read). Unknown for the peasant's +0xec string and
its RU text.

**Unknown.** The bodies of `L2.02949` and `L2.02956`; the writer of +0xec
and +0xf8 for a non-hero unit.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2073](../experiments/EXP-2073-rom2-town-persons/)

### R2-ENGINE-582

The dialogue page method `R2.0046` (RU `R2.0045`) parses the part
header; when the dialogue has a portrait (+0x7c) it calls the face builder
`L2.02950` (RU `L2.02963`) at `L2.02964`, the only direct call of the
builder in the EN `.text` call-target scan. The argument is `[ebp-0x24]`,
an out-parameter of the part parser `R2.0048`, whose body was not read;
that it is the header's npc= number is R2-ENGINE-051's statement. The
builder resolves the actor through `R2.0071` (with the fallback of
`R2.0069` when no unit matches) and draws into an 88x108 surface:

- flags +0x1b8 & 0x11 nonzero: the actor's slot +0x88 (`L2.02965`), the
  paperdoll. The read part of that window builds `graphics\equipment\`
  plus `mfighter\`, `mmage\`, `ffighter\` or `fmage\` by flags & 6 (0, 2,
  4, 6), the item sprite names, and the body name `%s%d.256` with +0x28
  (`L2.02966..L2.02967`), then calls methods +0x18 and +0x40 of the loaded
  sprite objects. The committed window (0x1000 bytes) ends at `L2.02968`
  with no return, and its listing lines 521 to 1082 were not read; what is
  drawn, in which order and where is not determined.
- otherwise `graphics\infowindow\%s%d` with the type registry
  (`L2.02969`) name +0xf8 and +0x28, the digit dropped when +0x28 is 1,
  plus `.bmp`.

Types 0x40..0x66 take a crop rectangle from table `L2.02970`. A fallback
actor (flags bit 0x40) is deleted after the build. The inn's left painter
uses the same infowindow name for a non-paperdoll portrait.

Speakers of the read town-1 sections: `npc207talk9` NPC 207,
`npc2108talk8` NPC 2108, `npc517talk10` NPC 517 and the hero 21,
`plagatguard` NPC 97, equal in EN and RU.

**Confidence.** High for the page-to-builder call, the lookup-then-fallback
code, the flags split and the sprite and bitmap names built (EN; RU builder
and page equal after masking, R2-ENGINE-584). Medium that the argument is
the header's npc= number (unread parser). Unknown for the drawn frame and
crop, and for the RU slot +0x88 body (its window started inside another
routine).

**Unknown.** The rest of `L2.02965`; the parser `R2.0048`; other town-1
dialogue keys' headers; the copy geometry of the surface methods
+0x34/+0x38.

**Evidence.** [EXP-2073](../experiments/EXP-2073-rom2-town-persons/)

### R2-ENGINE-583

The gate click with flag 0x301 false calls the dialogue builder
`R2.0038` with key `plagatguard` (R2-ENGINE-241). Its one part header is
`npc=97, part=1` in EN and RU `text/town.txt`. The census printed no
installed Humans or Units row for 97 (R2-ENGINE-578). When the live lookup
`R2.0071` finds no unit with +0x1dc = 97, it builds the fallback actor of
`R2.0069`: flags 0x56, +0x24 = 1, +0x28 = 97-0x50 = 17. Flags & 0x11 =
0x10 selects the paperdoll; flags & 6 = 6 selects `fmage\`; a new actor
has no items, so the body name built is `graphics\equipment\fmage\17.256`.
In graphics.res that key is 11517 bytes, SHA-256
