| R2-ENGINE-603 | Selected ROM2 world programmes frame Building78, Pointer82, terrain escaped-count DWORD keys and escaped-count u16/raw60 entries; five mission documents fit these extents with empty Sack/extra lists. | High / Medium / Unknown | ✔ promoted (branch candidate) | [EXP-2076](../experiments/EXP-2076-rom2-save-load/) |
| R2-ENGINE-604 | Selected RU ROM2 base LOAD copies12 position bytes and registers saved addresses; the read key-map helpers insert and resolve exact DWORD keys, distinct from archive object indices. | High / Medium / Unknown | ✔ promoted (branch candidate) | [EXP-2076](../experiments/EXP-2076-rom2-save-load/) |

### R2-ENGINE-601

The exact message-table entry selectsL2.02035. After old-session clearing
through L2.02971 the arm calls L2.00826 at L2.02972. The entry sets mode 2,
creates the server and calls L2.00289. That reader consumes the Bsg& envelope,
discards blobEnd, decodes through L2.02973 and calls L2.00243.

The document consumes head, Players with all nested Group/actor programmes,
dead actors and worldPresent. Zero skips the world half. Nonzero reaches
Buildings, SpellEffects, map construction from the saved scenario name,
terrain, session, Sacks and the extra Token list. Session reading is itself
guarded by a null session-global pointer. Both sentinel words and raw400
trailer are read afterward; the sentinel values are not compared.

L2.01830 reopens the file at blobEnd+256, loads inline REG and requests
CurrentState/InBattle. Nonzero calls R2.0026(1). Zero takes town preparation,
L2.02974 and post0x42e; its measured table entry reaches the town-display
routine L2.00266. Selected mission/town tail readers consume REG,
pairsL2.00383, scenario-loader pointer
L2.00393 and nineL2.00388 buffer calls in that order. The label is sought past.
The existing Ok contract is R2-ENGINE-439. The town display reaches view
slots+0x80/+0x34; their dispatch and paint scheduling remain open.

**Confidence.** High for selected local instruction/table/call order.
Medium for composition across unread construction, transport and callback
contracts. Unknown for ordinary LOAD completion and the first visible frame.
The instrument follows direct CFG branches, records indirect jumps and
does not close exception handlers, all callers or arbitrary virtual targets.

**Unknown.** Failure/short-read behavior, global-pointer invariants, indirect
DLL/view dispatch and later overwrites. The InBattle value in each save's
registry was not read, so the branch taken per file is Unknown. The listing
also contains a 0x421 arm and a zero-worldPresent field-reset loop whose
effects are unexamined. A cold-LOAD trace from Ok through the first frame,
with document/tail boundaries and field witnesses, would settle it.

**Amended.** R2-SESSION-244 reads CurrentState/InBattle = 1 in the five
mission-like saves, so they take the mission branch; R2-ENGINE-613 gives
that branch's order through the REG restore and the tick-period store.
The four town-like values remain unread, and the first frame remains
Unknown.

### R2-ENGINE-602

Selected class descriptor/factory/constructor/vtable chains bind Spell to
EN L2.02975/RU L2.02976 and Spellbook toENL2.02977/RU L2.01167. The book is
behind Unit+0x140's gate; its header is two DWORDs. The array element getter
RU L2.01172 returns backing_pointer+4*index; size getterL2.02978 reads+8.
The selected resize body and loop leave index 0 outside serialization.

Spell stores u8+8 ID, u8+9 range, u8+0xa defensive, u16+0xc cost and u32
self address. LOAD registers that key and rebuilds+4 from the ID's row lookup.
The nine-byte payload has no damage/duration field; later derivation remains
separate. Null/earlier-object references carry no new payload. IDs and slot
indices are distinct fields; the measured nonnull book entries agree.

**Confidence.** High for selected local widths, order, index arithmetic and
both programme bindings. Medium for composed native SAV delivery, inheriting
conditional Group framing and successful-transfer assumptions. Unknown for
final cached values, failed allocations and original acceptance.

**Unknown.** Book+0x18, later refill/derive precedence and malformed counts.
An original cold LOAD with distinct saved/cached fields and book observations
would settle final values; no runtime process was started.

### R2-ENGINE-603

Building serializes the 38-byte base, raw22 and scalar widths1, 2, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 4, 4:
78 payload bytes. Pointer calls it then adds DWORD+0x6c:82. Selected EN/RU
descriptor chains and instruction programmes agree on these widths.

RU R2.0171 transfers terrain keys through R2.0174: the escaped count of
R2-ENGINE-200, then 4 bytes per key. Its selected constructor binds embedded
+0x54084's vtable+8 to L2.02979: escaped count, per entryu16 key and raw60
through L2.02980; a saved terrain key follows. Contents of raw60 remain Unknown.
The selected constructor binding does not prove every runtime vptr invariant.

The five mission buffers have 15 Building and one Pointer each; all complete
terrain extents lead to the 10374-byte session programme and exact following
list/trailer boundaries. Only game0006 has nonempty world effects, as
R2-SESSION-235 records. Selected Sack is base38, DWORD+0x3c and the bag
programme; the observed Sack and extra lists contain no bodies.

**Confidence.** High for local widths and the five hashed buffers' exact
extents. Medium for selected embedded binding and native composition.
Unknown for raw60 semantics, nonempty Sack/extra acceptance and live effects.

**Unknown.** A nonempty identified Sack/extra save and a cold LOAD would settle
those unexercised kinds. Layer-entry and effect/target observations would
settle semantic and continuation questions; no image-wide absence is claimed.

### R2-ENGINE-604

RU L2.02981 requests 12 raw bytes in both directions. Under R2-ENGINE-055,
bytes 0/1 are tile X/Y and 4/5 fractions; other position bytes remain unassigned.
The baseL2.01164 also reads a saved self key and owner key. The acquired
L2.01168 calls L2.02982 then stores the object in the returned value cell.
L2.02982 usesL2.02983's bucket search, inserts a node with the incoming key
on a miss, and returns node+8.L2.02983 hashes(key>>4), traverses the bucket
and compares full DWORD keys.L2.01323 returns that node's value on a match.
These bodies close the local insert/lookup semantics left open in
R2-ENGINE-323; allocation internals and failure remain unexamined.

The selected Group insertionL2.00361 writes member+0x70=Group and
Group+0x44=member owner after a list helper. The nine measured Player-1
saved-key equalities are R2-SESSION-236. Archive shared indices and saved
address keys are separate namespaces; their numeric equality is not required.

**Confidence.** High for selected RU operations, exact key comparison and
position-transfer width. Medium for the complete successful native mapping
path and EN parity beyond inherited contracts. Unknown for post-load roster,
repositioning and subsequent writes. No whole-image writer/caller census is made.

**Unknown.** Observe identity maps, owner/member lists and positions after
deserialization and at the first frame to settle delivered state and later
placement. Allocation failure and short transfer need controlled original
observations; this experiment ran none.

## Signpost click, structure order and event box

Static reads of the owned EN and RU `allods2.exe`: raw x86
listings decoded with Capstone, one generation reproduced byte for byte.
EN addresses first where both are given; "equal after masking" means equal
once every number at or above 0x400000 is masked.

| ID | Claim | Confidence | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R2-ENGINE-605 | The ROM2 hover routine (EN L2.02985, RU L2.02986) names the object of the last-registered rectangle meeting a 3x3 box at the cursor; a CStructure gets flag 0x800 only if kind-record +0x8c is set, else +0x64 set skips it. | High / Medium / Unknown | ✔ promoted (branch candidate) | [EXP-2077](../experiments/EXP-2077-rom2-signpost/EXP-2077.md) |
| R2-ENGINE-606 | A ROM2 map click whose box is at most screen width x 10/640 and whose cursor is [L2.02987] sends message type 0x24 with the hovered ID and the IDs of objects that L2.02988 accepts; EN picks that cursor only on hover flag 0x800. | High / Medium / Unknown | ✔ promoted (branch candidate) | [EXP-2077](../experiments/EXP-2077-rom2-signpost/EXP-2077.md) |
| R2-ENGINE-607 | ROM2 message 0x24 finds the structure by ID and sets order 0xf: target its position word, range 1 for building byte +0x60 of 1 or 2, 2 (cell +0x101) for 3 or 4, else 3 (+0x202); prepared 0xf reaches the state-15 handler. | High / Medium / Unknown | ✔ promoted (branch candidate) | [EXP-2077](../experiments/EXP-2077-rom2-signpost/EXP-2077.md) |
| R2-ENGINE-608 | The ROM2 event box starts as a 580x240 rect at (30,120); placement rounds it to 8+96k by 104+64k and centres it on the screen (488x232 at 268,268 at 1024x768); Enter and Esc post 0x470 as Ok does. | High / Medium / Unknown | ✔ promoted (branch candidate) | [EXP-2077](../experiments/EXP-2077-rom2-signpost/EXP-2077.md) |
| R2-ENGINE-609 | A ROM2 modal box sets UI bit 8 (EN +0x404, RU +0x41c), darkens the screen and sets cursor [L2.02989]; in EN bit 8 stops the edge routine and six panel redraws per pass and defers events; no read body stops the simulation. | High / Medium / Unknown | ✔ promoted (branch candidate) | [EXP-2077](../experiments/EXP-2077-rom2-signpost/EXP-2077.md) |

### R2-ENGINE-605

The routine (585 instructions per root) clears the hovered object +0x994,
the hovered ID word +0x9a8 and +0x998..+0x9a4, and returns 0 when the
cursor point (getters `L2.02990`, `L2.02991` on `L2.02992`) lies outside
the view rectangle. It forms the box (x-1, y-1, x+1, y+1) from the globals
`L2.02993`, `L2.02994` and walks index i from [view+0x134]-1 down to 0:

1. The 16-byte rectangle i of list view+0x10c (`L2.02995`) is normalised
   (`L2.02996`) and intersected with the box (`L2.02997`); no overlap
   continues the walk.
2. The ID word i of list view+0x120 (`L2.02956`) is looked up in the
   object collection view+0x9d0 (`L2.02998`); a miss ends the walk.
3. The name of the object's runtime class record (vtable slot 0) is
   compared with "CUnit" (flag 1), "CAirUnit" (flag 2) and "CStructure"
   (EN `L2.02999`, `L2.03000`, `L2.03001`; RU `L2.03002`, `L2.03003`,
   `L2.03004`). For "CStructure" it takes record [`L2.03005`]([obj+0x24])
   through `L2.03006`, which calls `L2.03007`: +0x8c nonzero adds flag
   0x800; otherwise +0x64 nonzero skips the object and the walk continues.
   Both kept paths add 0x20. `L2.02955`(word +4 of [obj+0x14]) on
   view+0x9cc adds flag 4.
4. The object is stored at +0x994. Outside campaign mode (app +0x5d8 = 2
   in EN, +0x63c in RU) a walk over view+0x4970 fills
   +0x998..+0x9a4 first. Then the ID word i goes to +0x9a8 and the walk ends,
   so the highest index that overlaps wins.

After the walk, a cursor inside view child 2 or 3 (RU 3 or 4) clears +0x994
and +0x9a8. The routine stores the cell under the cursor at +0x9ac, +0x9b0,
adds flag 0x40 or 0x400 from bits 0xc000 of four map words and, when the
hovered object changed, posts 0x408 to app members +0xe0 and +0xe4 and sets
+0x114 = 1 on the new and the old object. It returns the flags.

EN `L2.03008` passes its 16-byte rectangle argument with index +0x134 to
`L2.03009` on list +0x10c and its ID word with the same index to `L2.03010`
on list +0x120, then adds 1 to +0x134; both store-at-index calls are unread,
so that they append is Medium. A
call-target scan of EN `.text` finds four direct callers, `L2.03011`,
`L2.03012`, `L2.03013` and `L2.03014`, not read.

**Confidence.** High for the control flow and stores of the routine and of
`L2.03008`: the descending index, the three name compares, the flag
`or`s, the skip and the stores to +0x994 and +0x9a8; the routine is equal
in EN and RU after masking except the campaign field offset and the two
child IDs; `L2.03008` is EN only. Medium that index i addresses the i-th
registered rectangle and ID, that `L2.02997` tests overlap, that
`L2.02996` normalises, that `L2.01497` forms the box and that `L2.02998`
finds by ID: the list, rectangle and collection helpers `L2.02995`,
`L2.02956`, `L2.02998`, `L2.02997`, `L2.02996`, `L2.01497`, `L2.03009` and
`L2.03010` are unread. Medium for the other meanings: the cursor getters, `L2.02955`, `L2.03007` and the record layout
of `L2.03005` are unread, and that the registration order is the draw order
rests on the unread callers. Unknown which rectangle an object registers
(sprite frame, foot cell or other).

**Unknown.** The rectangle a Pointer registers: the four callers of
`L2.03008` would settle it, or a run hovering the top of the signpost
sprite and its foot cell. Whether the Pointer's client object is a
CStructure (its runtime class was not read) and whether its kind record
has +0x8c set, that is, whether a Pointer gets flag 0x800 at all:
`L2.03007`, the table writer and the Pointer's client class.

### R2-ENGINE-606

The click routine (EN `L2.03015`, RU `L2.03016`; 190 instructions, equal
after masking) builds a rectangle from a cursor point (`L2.03017` on
`L2.02992`) and its argument point, normalises it, grows an empty one by
(1, 1), and goes to `L2.03018` (unread) when its width or height is above
[`L2.00628`] x 10 / 640. With view +0x140 = 0 it calls `L2.03019`.
Otherwise it compares the current cursor (`L2.03020`) with the handles in
`L2.03021`, `L2.03022`, `L2.03023`, `L2.03024`, `L2.03025`, `L2.01940`,
`L2.03026`, `L2.02987` and `L2.03027` in that order (through `L2.03028`).
On [`L2.02987`] it calls `L2.03029` (RU `L2.03030`) with word view+0x9a8,
the hovered ID of R2-ENGINE-605. A call-target scan of `.text` finds that
call as the only direct caller in each root (EN `L2.03031`, RU `L2.03032`).

`L2.03029` (60 instructions, equal after masking) fills the message
buffer `L2.03033` (RU `L2.03034`): byte +9 = 0x24, word +5 = word +4 of
the player object view+0x9cc, word +7 = 0, byte +0x12 = 0. For each object
of collection view+0x9d0 (head `L2.03035`, next `L2.03036`) that `L2.02988`
accepts, it stores word +0xe = the hovered ID and appends the object's
word +4 (`L2.03037`, RU `L2.03038`). It sends the buffer through
`L2.00871` on `L2.00872` (RU `L2.00459` on `L2.03039`, the packet bus of
R2-ENGINE-047) and calls slot 0x6c of `L2.03040`'s result. A `.text`

### R2-ENGINE-607

The message handler's 21-entry jump table (R2-ENGINE-541) holds at index
18 (type 0x24) EN `L2.03051`, RU `L2.03052`. The arm (46 instructions,
equal after masking except frame offsets) runs when [`L2.01066`] (RU
[`L2.02609`]) is nonzero and calls EN `L2.03053`, RU `L2.02792` with word
+0xe on [[ctx+0x7c]]: from EN `L2.03054` through `L2.03055` (RU
`L2.03056`, `L2.03057`) it returns the
first object whose dword +4 equals the sign-extended word, else 0. On 0 the
arm formats string RU `L2.03058` (EN `L2.03059`) with the ID and stops;
otherwise it calls the setter EN `L2.03060`, RU `L2.02809` with the unit
[ebp-0x18] and the object (R2-ENGINE-541 reads the unit selection).

The setter (86 instructions, equal after masking) calls reset EN
`L2.03061` (RU `L2.01584`), stores unit +0x50 = 0xf and, on the command
object, +0x68 = the object, +0x14 = 1, +8 = 0 and word +0xa = word +2 of
[object+0x10] (EN `L2.03062`, RU `L2.01521`). It then indexes the 4-entry
table EN `L2.03063`, RU `L2.03064` by byte +0x60 of the object (EN
`L2.03065`, RU `L2.03066`) minus 1:

| +0x60 | +0x14 | +0xa |
|---|---|---|
| 1, 2 | 1 | unchanged |
| 3, 4 | 2 | + 0x101 |
| 0, 5..255 | 3 | + 0x202 |

The order-0xf planner (EN `L2.03067`, RU `L2.02875`; R2-ENGINE-555)
stores command +8 = 0xf and +0x68 = its second argument. Index 14 of the
15-entry prepared table (R2-ENGINE-542; EN `L2.02887`, RU `L2.01571`,
prepared byte minus 1) holds EN `L2.02984`, RU `L2.02638`, which calls the handler of R2-ENGINE-519 (EN
`L2.02633`, RU `L2.02632`) with the unit and command +0x68. So a structure
click gives order 0xf. The handler tests +0xa and +0x14 with RU
`L2.02567` (R2-ENGINE-519): on a zero test it calls RU `L2.02634` (an
approach step, R2-ENGINE-543; unread here) and sets state 1 (Medium that
the unit walks toward +0xa); on a nonzero test it sets state 15, where the
arm of R2-ENGINE-518 runs a Pointer's action.

**Confidence.** High for the arm, the lookup, the setter, the planner, the
prepared arm and the table cells, read in both roots. Medium that the unit
walks toward +0xa in state 1: `L2.02634` was not read here (R2-ENGINE-543
names it an approach step; R2-ENGINE-546 reads state 1 as a cell step).
Medium that byte +0x60 is the Buildings sizeX (R2-ASSET-124 gives Pointer
1..6 sizeX 1; no body read stores +0x60), so a Pointer's range of 1 is
Medium; Medium that
EN `L2.03054` and `L2.03055` (RU `L2.03056`, `L2.03057`) walk every
building and that +0xa packs x in the low byte and y in the high byte.
Unknown what a unit that cannot walk does.

**Unknown.** The writer of building byte +0x60 (the Building constructor
and its record read). A unit that cannot reach the cell: the state-1 arm
of the handler, or a run clicking the signpost with the hero blocked.

### R2-ENGINE-608

The event dialogue builder (EN `R2.0038`, RU `R2.0037`; R2-ENGINE-050;
167 instructions, equal after masking except the IDs) allocates 0x88 bytes
and calls the dialogue constructor (EN `R2.0040`, RU `R2.0039`) with
(base ID 9 or RU 0xa, 0x1e, 0x78, 0x262, 0x168, key). Its child IDs are
those of R2-ENGINE-051. The base constructor (EN `L2.01470`, RU
`L2.03068`) passes the values to `L2.00634`, stores vtable `L2.03069` and
calls the placement EN `L2.03070`, RU `L2.03071`. The rectangle constructor
EN `L2.00635` stores the ID at +4 and passes the four values to
`L2.00636`.

The placement reads width = dword +0x10 - dword +8 and height = +0x14 -
+0xc (EN `L2.03072`, `L2.03073` on +8), sets w = (w - 8) / 96 x 96 + 8 and
h = (h - 0x68) / 64 x 64 + 0x68 with truncating division, x = ([`L2.00628`]
- w) >> 1 and y = ([`L2.00629`] - h) >> 1, and stores (x, y, x + w, y + h)
at +8. With (0x1e, 0x78, 0x262, 0x168) as left, top, right, bottom, w = 580
gives 488 and h = 240 gives 232; at 1024x768, x = 268 and y = 268.

The dialogue key handler (EN `L2.03074`, RU `L2.03075`) posts 0x470
through slot 0x48 for 0xd and 0x1b and returns 1; other keys go to the base
handler EN `L2.03076`, RU `L2.03077`, whose byte table sends 9 to a focus
step (`L2.03078`) and 0x25..0x28 to the neighbour fields +0x50, +0x54,
+0x48, +0x4c of [+0x38]. 0x470 is the Ok message of R2-ENGINE-051; its
close goes through EN `L2.00782`, which for 0x445 and 0x446 calls slot 0x84
and posts 0x44c with the dialogue to the application. The builder ends
with the modal push of R2-ENGINE-609. A call-target scan of EN `.text`
finds 21 direct callers of the builder; `L2.03079` is the UI 0x433 branch
and the other 20 are not read.

**Confidence.** High for the arithmetic, the constructor arguments and the
Enter and Esc arm in both roots. Medium for the numbers on screen: they
rest on `L2.00634` and `L2.00636` storing the four values in order at +8
(read in navigation only) and on [`L2.00628`] and [`L2.00629`] holding the
screen size. Medium for the Tab and arrow cells, read from table bytes that
the listing decodes as code. Unknown which of the 20 other callers open a
box in play.

**Unknown.** The box frame and its drawn size: a run opening the signpost
box at 1024x768 and measuring its rectangle, with the hero at two screen
places to test R2-SESSION-230's "to his right".

### R2-ENGINE-613

With argument 1 (the LOAD tail of R2-ENGINE-601) the entry runs, in order:

1. client +0x80 = 0; `L2.01133` on cursor `[L2.03110]`; music stop
   `L2.01408` when `[L2.00878]` is set.
2. The name copy from app +0x5d0; the map caller `L2.00222` is skipped
   (it needs argument 0 and app +0x5d4).
3. `L2.03111` rebuilds the room stack: app +0xd4 gets children app +0xd8,
   +0xdc, +0xe0, +0xe4; app +0xcc gets app +0xd0 and +0xd4; app +0x404 = 1.
4. Client loaders `L2.03112(0,0)`, `L2.03113(0,0)` and `L2.03114`.
5. app +0x3f0 = 1; `L2.03115(1)` sends packet type 4 (byte +9) with the
   word +4 of the client Player `[client+0x9cc]` at +5, 0 at +7 and the
   argument at +0xa through `L2.00872`; `L2.03116(client+0xab4)` and
   `L2.03117` send type 0x46 subtypes 1 and 3 (the latter with
   `[L2.01503]`); `L2.03118(client+0xab0)` is unread.
6. Only when app +0x5d4 is set (test at `L2.03119`), one call of the
   session tick `L2.03120`.
7. A wait loop: one window message (PM_REMOVE; WM_QUIT returns 0), a
   network wait (`L2.03121`) with timeout error 0x1005, then the client
   pump `L2.00466(0x64)`. The pump takes messages (`L2.03122`) and
   dispatches type t through byte table `L2.00467` (index t-3) and jump
   table `L2.00468`; it returns 1 only after a message of type 0x64 and,
   with a nonzero argument, keeps polling while none is queued. Type 0x64
   reaches arm `L2.03123`, which stores message +0xa in app +0x408; type 6
   reaches arm `L2.03124`, which creates the client map (R2-ENGINE-615).
   The loop tests client +0x80 at its top and after a pump return, so it
   ends at the first type-0x64 pump return after +0x80 is nonzero, not when
   type 6 finishes: a type 0x64 message before the first type 6 makes the
   loop run again, and every message dispatched before that 0x64 runs
   first. A zero pump return returns 0.
8. app +0x3f0 = 0; in campaign mode (app +0x5d8 = 2) the REG restore of
   R2-ENGINE-614 after reopening the file at blobEnd+256.
9. app +0xd4 slot +0x48(0x408, 0, 0) (`L2.03125`) and app +0xcc slot +0x34
   (`L2.03126`). The receiver of the first is the room object `L2.03111`
   fills with children +0xd8..+0xe4; whether slot +0x48 forwards 0x408 to
   those children, and that they are panels, is not read.
10. Outside mode 3: the music body `L2.01375` (R2-ENGINE-336); app +0x43c =
    -1, +0x3e4 = 0, +0x3e8 = 0.
11. Mode 2: `L2.03127(app+0x41c)` (R2-ENGINE-620; it stores the tick
    period and time stamps and does not show that the clock runs), then
    `main\text\mission%d.txt` and `main\text\quest.txt` through `R2.0056`
    and the briefing `R2.0027`.
12. Argument 1 skips the 0x442 autosave; `L2.01133` on `[L2.02989]`;
    return 1.

RU `R2.0023` has 1002 instructions, as EN. After masking, 24 instructions
differ, each only in an app field offset; the 13 EN/RU pairs are 0x3bc/0x3d4,
0x3e4/0x3fc, 0x3e8/0x400, 0x3f0/0x408, 0x41c/0x434, 0x43c/0x454,
0x460/0x478, 0x47f/0x497, 0x4dc/0x4f4, 0x598/0x5f8, 0x5d0/0x630,
0x5d4/0x638 and 0x5d8/0x63c. The 59 strings pushed (48 distinct) are equal in order.
RU callees were not compared.

**Confidence.** High for the EN order, branch conditions, packet bytes and
stores of the entry, the pump tables and the two arms, and for the RU body
equality after masking. Medium for callee meanings: the loaders, the tick
body beyond its phase dispatch, the senders' receivers and `L2.03118` are
not read to their effects. Unknown which server messages reach the client
before type 0x64 and in what order, which of them create client objects
(the hero among them) before the REG restore, whether the clock runs
(app +0x418 is only stored) and what receives 0x408.

**Unknown.** A cold LOAD of game0001 with a trace of the type byte at each
`L2.00466` dispatch until type 0x64 would give the message order, the
arrival of type 6 and the stores made before the REG restore. The first-frame
run of R2-ENGINE-621 settles whether the clock runs and what reacts to 0x408.

type 3, the low byte of +4 as one element for type 1 and nothing for type 0

| GameOptions Speed, ShowTimeFlow | app +0x41c, global `L2.03133` |

### R2-ENGINE-615

The pump arm `L2.03124` tests client +0x80. When zero it calls
`L2.03145(message+0xf)`; if +0x80 is still zero it sets `[L2.03146]` =
0x1004 and returns 0.

`L2.03145` releases an existing map (slot +4 with 1), forms the name from
its argument, prefixed with `scenario\` (`L2.03147`) when app +0x5d8 is 2,
creates a 0x30 object through `L2.01385(name)`, stores it in client +0x80,
sets client +0xdc = 1, calls `L2.03148(map)`, posts 0x403 with the client
to app +0xd4 (slot +0x48), then `L2.03149(1)`, `L2.03150(map+0x28)` and
client +0x4970 `L2.03151(0)`.

`L2.01385` (1046 instructions) creates a 0x3b8 object with the ALM reader
`L2.02484(name)` of R2-ENGINE-616. It stores width and height (`L2.03152`,
`L2.03153`) at +4/+8, a double of map +0x18 at +0x20, map +0x1c at +0x2c,
map bytes +0x20/+0x24 at +0x1c/+0x1d and 0x1fff at +0x28. It allocates
+0xc (2wh bytes, the tile words of `L2.03154`), +0x10 (wh bytes copied from
map +0x14), +0x14 (zeroed, then rows 8..h-5 columns 8..w-9 copied from map
+0x10) and +0x18 (zeroed). For each entry of map list +0x390 it creates by
entry word +4: 0x21 a 0x14c object (`L2.03155`), 0x25 a 0x14c object
(`L2.03156`), any other a 0x144 object (`L2.03157`); the object gets word
+4 = entry +0x10 + 0x6000, +0x24 = the kind, +8 = entry word 0 * 256 +
0x80 and the next coordinate from entry word 2, and goes into client
+0x9d0 under that key. A second loop (`L2.03158`..`L2.03159`) runs over
map list +0x3a4. For each entry it builds an object of 0x254 bytes
(`L2.00233`) when entry flag +0x48 has bit 0x10, else of 0x208 bytes
(`L2.03160`); then a 0x1e4-byte object (`L2.03161` or `R2.0067`) whose
word +4 is entry word +0x3c + 0x6000 (`L2.03162..L2.03163`) and which goes
into client +0x9d0 (`L2.00142` at `L2.03164`). Between them the loop calls
`L2.02708` when app +0x5d8 is 2 (`L2.03165..L2.03166`). The constructor
beyond these two loops was not read beyond its call list; the asset object
is freed at `L2.03167` (`L2.03168`).

**Confidence.** High for the arm, the creator and the read part of the
constructor, both creation loops included. Medium that message +0xf carries
the saved scenario name: the server sender of type 6 was not read. Medium for
the meaning of the copied grids, for what the second-loop objects are (the
roles of the 0x254, 0x208 and 0x1e4 objects and of `L2.02708` are unread;
that they are units rests on the key range of R2-SESSION-245) and for the
constructor instructions after the two loops.

When worldPresent is nonzero the document reader `L2.00243` takes the name
from session +0x90 and prefixes `Scenario\` (`L2.03169`) when session
+0xd4 is nonzero. In order:

1. Units of each Player list +0x24 whose byte +0x4c lacks bit 8 are added
   to `[L2.00325]` through `L2.00202`; Buildings (`L2.03170`) and
   SpellEffects (`L2.03171`) are read from the document.
2. The map: a 0x3b8 object through `L2.02484(name)`, signature "M7R"
   (`L2.03172`), error codes 1..6 at +0x8c, version at most 0x640 and a
   13-entry record table `L2.02737`.
3. Terrain: a 0xa4570 object `L2.03173(map, [L2.00325])` takes width and
   height into +0x50000/+0x50004 and per-cell tiles (`L2.03174`,
   `L2.03175`), is stored in `L2.01839` and then reads the document
   terrain through `L2.03176` (R2-ENGINE-603).
4. When `L2.01066` is null, a 0xeb20 object `L2.03177(terrain, Players)`
   is stored there and reads the document through `L2.01736`.
5. Sacks and the extra list are read from the document; the script is
   compiled by `L2.00201(session+0x98, map, 0)`.
6. `L2.03168(map, 1)` frees the map; session +0x94 = 1.
7. Post-load: `[L2.00325]` slot +4 (R2-ENGINE-617), the dead list slot +4,
   terrain `L2.03178`, `L2.03179` on `L2.01066`, SpellEffects slot 0.

When worldPresent is zero each unit gets +0x40, +0x44 and +0x5c = 0.

**Confidence.** High for the name source, the order, the sizes and the free,
for the terrain size and tiles taken through `L2.03173`, and for the calls
that hand the document reader to the Unit, Building, SpellEffects and Sack
readers. Medium for the script and the terrain layers: the script compiler
`L2.00201` receives the asset as an argument, and the bodies of `L2.03176`,
`L2.01736` and the compiler were not read, so which fields they take from
the asset and which from the document is Unknown. The server's map lists
+0x390 and +0x3a4 are touched in no read listing; that does not exclude
their use in the unread bodies.

## Mission failure reasons and the failure text

Static reads of the owned EN and RU `allods2.exe` (raw x86 listings decoded
with Capstone from the plan of one generation reproduced byte for byte) and
measurements of both roots' `scenario.res` and `main.res`. EN addresses
unless RU is named. "Session" is the object at `[L2.01066]` that holds
+0xbe14 (R2-ENGINE-060). "Owner" is the player object whose byte +0x40 the
result tick and the death routine write. A reason is the value sent with
packet 0xb4. "Equal after masking" means equal once every hex number of five
or more digits is masked.

from 1 to 10 bytes back: 11 hits per root, all in `.text`.

| EN site | RU site | Instruction use |
|---|---|---|
| `L2.03211` | `L2.03212` | Session init stores 0; EN stores 0 at +0xbe08, +0xbe0c and +0xbe10 beside it |
| `L2.03213` | `L2.03214` | instant 5 stores IR scalar 0 (+8); action table `L2.00509` index 4 is `L2.03215`, which calls `L2.00521` |
| `L2.03216`, `L2.03217` | `L2.03218`, `L2.03219` | check 18 adds 1 (R2-ENGINE-627) |
| `L2.03220`, `L2.03221` | `L2.03222`, `L2.03223` | detector adds 1 (R2-ENGINE-628) |
| `L2.03224` | `L2.03225` | value passed to `L2.03226` (RU `L2.00354`) |
| `L2.03227` | `L2.03228` | address passed to `L2.03229` (RU `L2.02583`) |
| `L2.03230`, `L2.03231`, `L2.03232` | `L2.03233`, `L2.03234`, `L2.03235` | result tick reads (R2-ENGINE-624) |

The instant-5, check-18, detector and result-tick bodies are equal after

**Confidence.** High for the 11 hits per root and their instructions.
Medium that no other routine writes the register: an access through a
smaller displacement from an embedded base, a bulk copy, or a write through
the address that `L2.03229` receives lies outside a displacement scan.
Medium that `L2.03226` and `L2.03229` save and load the value: both are
unread and named from the value-then-address pairing. Medium that the
check-18 arm, the detector and the init address the `[L2.01066]` object the
tick reads: R2-ENGINE-060 places instant 5 there and the field layout is
shared, but each routine's `this` was not traced to that global.

**Unknown.** Whether a LOAD restores a pending reason: reading `L2.03229`,
or saving a mission between an instant 5 and the failure screen and loading
it in the original, would settle it.

### R2-ENGINE-624

Result tick EN `L2.00524`, RU `L2.00127`: 269 instructions each, equal after
masking. With owner byte +0x41 nonzero and DWORD +0x2c zero
(R2-ENGINE-060), in order:

1. Owner +0x40 of 2 or more skips steps 2 to 4. When the tick object's
   +0x74 is nonzero, a branch through `L2.03236`, actor word +0x94 at most
   −40 and owner +0xa64 later stores owner +0x40 = 0 (`L2.03237`).
2. Owner +0x38 null, or the +0x38 actor's byte +0x13c above 0: owner
   +0x40 = 2 and 0xb4 with 2 (`L2.03238`); then, if owner byte +0x42 is
   nonzero and the tick object's +0x74 is zero, 0xb4 with 0 (`L2.03239`).
3. Otherwise Session +0xbe14 above 0 and owner +0x40 below 2: 0xb4 with
   +0xbe14 (`L2.03240`) and owner +0x40 = its low byte (`L2.03241`).
4. Otherwise Session +0xbe0c nonzero and owner +0x40 not 1: 0xb5 and owner
   +0x40 = 1 (`L2.03242`).

Each send calls `L2.01047` with ecx `L2.00994` (RU `L2.02566`). In the EN
receiver opcode 0xb4 has selector byte 0x29 (`L2.03243`), whose table entry
`L2.03244` is `L2.03245`: it posts UI 0x433 with ID 0xff and packet DWORD
+0xa. UI 0x433 (`L2.00133`) stores the ID at +0x43c, and ID 0xff posts 0x431
with the second argument (R2-ENGINE-050). A reason of 1 stores owner +0x40
= 1, the value step 4 stores, and leaves +0x40 below 2.

**Confidence.** High for the branch order, stores and sends in both roots.
Medium for the EN receiver route (narrowed by the review): the selector
byte, the table entry and the arm are committed; the dispatch at
`L2.03246..L2.03247` that indexes them is not. Unknown for the meanings of
actor +0x13c
(the victory transition clears it, R2-ENGINE-526), owner +0x42 and the tick
object's +0x74, and for how often the tick runs relative to the script tick.

**Unknown.** In the original, a mission in which the hero dies, with the
screen recorded, shows which text reason 2 brings; a memory read of hero
+0x13c across a death and a victory would name the byte.

### R2-ENGINE-628

EN `L2.03210` (130 instructions; RU `L2.03286` equal after masking) walks
the list at `[this+0xa50]` +0xa456c. For each unit, class word +0xe = 0x18
sets a flag; a unit whose owner (+0x14) has +0x2c = 0 adds 1 to a count
and, while no class-0x18 unit has been seen, is tested by
`L2.03287(x, y, 0x3f, 0x1a)`; a result below 4 stores +0xbe08 = 1. After
the loop: no class-0x18 unit and +0xbe08 set add 1 to +0xbe0c; a count of 0
with +0xbe10 set adds 1 to +0xbe14; a nonzero count with +0xbe10 clear
stores +0xbe10 = 1 and calls `L2.03288`. Scans of the EN image: no
E8/E9/0F8x rel32 or EB/7x rel8 branch targets `L2.03210`, and no raw DWORD
holds it.

**Confidence.** High for the body and the EN negative over those
encodings. Medium that it never runs: a computed or table call through a
non-literal address lies outside the scans, and the RU image was not
scanned. The meanings of class 0x18 and `L2.03287` are unread.

### R2-ENGINE-629

The 0x431 arm (EN `L2.03289`): app +0x3e8 = 0 and +0x5d8 = 2 (campaign
mode, R2-ENGINE-049); it stores +0x3e8 = 1, calls `L2.03290(reason − 2)` on
the cache `L2.03291` and passes the result to the report `R2.0033` (its
one caller, `L2.03292`), whose title is slot 0x8d of text table `L2.02397`
(RU `R2.0032`, `L2.03293`). `L2.03290` calls `L2.03294`, which returns
`[this+4] + 4 * index` with no compare. The cache loop (EN `L2.03295`, RU
`L2.03296`, equal after masking) empties `L2.03291`, then for n = 2, 3, ...
calls the filler `R2.0029(n)` (one caller, `L2.03297`; key `#failure%d`,
the rule of R2-ENGINE-049); an empty result (`L2.01986`: length +4 = 0)
with n below 5 takes `L2.02396(0x118 + n)` of `L2.02397`; an empty result
with n of 5 or more stops; each entry is appended by `L2.03298`.

A mission whose cache holds E entries covers reasons 2..1+E. For such a
reason the entry is the `#failure<reason>` section of the mission text, or
slot 0x118 + reason for an empty 2..4 (Medium, see Confidence). A reason below 2 or above 1+E
indexes past the filled entries; reason 0 (R2-ENGINE-624 step 2) is index
−2.

**Confidence.** High (narrowed by the review) for the control flow of the
EN arm (gate, +0x3e8 = 1, argument reason - 2, call to `R2.0033`), for the
unbounded accessor `L2.03294` and for the loop's start at 2, its compare
with 5 and the `0x118 + n` argument. Medium that entry i holds the i-th
filler result (`L2.03299`, `L2.03300` and the insert `L2.03301` that
`L2.03298` calls are unread), that the report displays it with slot 0x8d as
its title (`L2.02030` is unread) and that UI 0x431 reaches `L2.03289`
(R2-ENGINE-049). High for the RU loop, filler and report equal after
masking. Medium for the RU 0x431 arm, which was not read. Medium that slot
0x118 + n is `main.txt` row 0x118 + n: rows 282..284 are measured, the
table load and the lookup `L2.02396` are unread. Unknown what a reason
outside the cache shows: the array's capacity and the bytes after its last
entry were not read. The arm sets +0x3e8 = 1 and runs only while it is 0;
where +0x3e8 is cleared is unread, so a report per mission is not
established.

**Unknown.** In the original, mission 96 with the trigger that runs its
instant 5 (reason 5, three cache entries), recording the failure screen.

### R2-ENGINE-633

The selector's campaign segment (EN `L2.00437..L2.00432`, RU
`L2.00438..L2.00433`):

1. tests app +0x5d8 == 2 (RU +0x63c) and skips the segment otherwise;
2. calls EnterInn through cell `L2.00409` (RU `L2.00551`) with an option
   array at ebp-0x94 and a count at ebp-0x14;
3. appends each of the `count` words to a list through `L2.03306`;
4. calls the producer at `L2.03302` (RU `L2.03304`) with GetVar(0x300) (cell
   `L2.00451`, RU `L2.00449`) and the list, receiver `[L2.00805]`;
5. calls `L2.00466(0)`.

The words are EnterInn's packed options: low word NPC or hire ID, bits
16..27 topic, bits 28..30 kind (R2-ENGINE-219). At stage 30 one is NPC 22,
topic 30, kind 3, `0x301e0016`, with no bank gate (R2-ENGINE-216). The
other constants with low word 21..30 are NPC 22 topic 40 (stage 40), NPC 22
topic 62 (the continuation, stage 60 or more; R2-ENGINE-498) and NPC 23
topic 49 (stage 50). The tail hire IDs are 1..20 (R2-ENGINE-221). The two
segments have 40 instructions each. After masking they differ in one line,
the app offset.

**Confidence.** High for the segment, its gate, the order of calls and the
arguments, read in both roots. Medium for "before the inn page is shown": the
inn page is opened after the segment (EXP-2031's selector listing), and no
inn-page path back to the segment was traced. The meaning of app +0x5d8 == 2
is not read here.

**Narrowed by the review.** The headline said "before any inn action"; it now
says "before the inn page is shown (Medium)".

### R2-ENGINE-634

Over every executable byte of each client, the E8, E9, 0F8x, EB and 7x
branch-target scan finds two sites per root that target the producer:

- EN: `L2.03302` (R2-ENGINE-633) and `L2.03303`;
- RU: `L2.03304` and `L2.03305`.

A raw DWORD scan of all sections for the producer's address finds none in
either root. `L2.03303` lies in the 0x41d leave arm. In that arm the order is:

1. the transition `L2.01664`;
2. `L2.01854`;
3. GetCurrentLocation (`L2.00270`);
4. LeaveLocation (`L2.02297`);
5. `L2.00173`, which returns GetVar(0x305), slot 773;
6. when that value is nonzero, the producer with GetVar(0x300) and a list
   holding it, then `L2.00466(0)`.

The RU arm (`L2.03307..L2.03308`) has the same 41 instructions. After
masking, 11 frame offsets and the exception-state byte differ. Its getter
`L2.03309` equals EN's.

**Confidence.** High for the scan results and both callers' bodies. Medium
that no other route reaches the producer: a register call through a
computed address escapes both scans.

### R2-ENGINE-635

The producer (380 instructions per root, no open edge, equal after masking)
treats each list word's low word as an ID. ID 21..30 (0x15..0x1e) is the
controlled test. Keys 10000+10*ID go to the Humans lookup (`L2.02663`), then
the Units lookup (`L2.02665`). Keys 9998+10*ID+stage/10 replace the base when
a suffix probe hits (R2-ENGINE-381, R2-ENGINE-524). For ID 22 the base key is
10220. The only Humans row with that raw value is `Fighter_Hero`, and no row
holds 10221..10229 (R2-ASSET-160), so no suffix probe hits.

The controlled branch walks owner +0x24 comparing each actor's WORD +0x14c
with the ID. A match ends the branch. Otherwise it:

1. allocates 0x254 bytes and calls the Human constructor `L2.00214`;
2. passes the constructor (name from `L2.03310` on `L2.00148`, 1, 0);
3. stores WORD +0x14c = ID at `L2.03311`;
4. stores +4 = key from `L2.02670` and +0x14 = owner;
5. appends the actor to owner +0x24 (`L2.00202`) and a 0x50-byte Group to
   owner +0x28;
6. calls `L2.03312` and `L2.02714` on `[L2.01066]`;
7. calls the sender `L2.01056` with 0xffb.

The constructor passes its arguments 2 and 3 to the Humans template load
`R2.0088`. With argument 2 nonzero, that load takes the hero class rule,
+0xe = 0x21 or 0x23 plus gender (R2-ENGINE-525). The constructor is 34
instructions per root and equal after masking.

The non-controlled branch does not touch the owner list. It builds a Unit
(`L2.01063`) or a Human with (name, 0, 0), stores +0x14c at `L2.03313`, sets
+0x14 and keeps the actor in a local list. Each local actor's key then goes
to `L2.03314`, which clears its bit in `L2.00339` when the key is below
0x6000.

**Confidence.** High for the producer's branches and stores, read in both
roots. Medium that the row built is `Fighter_Hero` and that the class is
the hero class: the lookup filter `L2.02664`, the name helper `L2.03310` and
the +0xe writers after the load are unread. Medium for the owner's identity
(R2-ENGINE-525).

**Unknown.** Whether `[L2.01066]` is null in a town, and what `L2.03312` and
`L2.02714` do then, so whether the build completes in a town. In the
original, entering the stage-30 inn and recording whether identity 22
appears in the party settles both.

**Narrowed by the review.** The headline named the row `Fighter_Hero` and the
hero class without their grade (Medium) and omitted the town registration
(Unknown); both are now in the headline.

### R2-ENGINE-636

A raw DWORD scan of every section of the EN client for 0x149..0x14d finds
193 hits. A hit is a store candidate when some decode 1 to 10 bytes back is
a write-class mnemonic whose memory operand at displacement 0x149..0x14d
overlaps +0x14c..+0x14d: 59 candidates. 19 of them have a `mov word`
decode, 15 at +0x14c:

| Site | Source of the word |
|---|---|
| `L2.03311`, `L2.03313` | the producer's ID (R2-ENGINE-635) |
| `L2.03315`, `L2.02672` | Humans load: parameter 24, (w/10)%1000 above 10000 (R2-ENGINE-525) |
| `L2.00166` | literal 0x15 |
| `L2.03316` | literal 0 |
| `L2.03317` | the hire creator's ID, 1..20 (R2-ENGINE-381) |
| `L2.02674` | Units parameter 55, low word (R2-ENGINE-525) |
| `L2.03318` | a Humans row word, parameter 0x18, untransformed |
| `L2.03319` | a Units parameter 0x37 word |
| `L2.03320`, `L2.03321` | a copy from another object |
| `L2.03322` | a stream word |
| `L2.03323` | the word at `[L2.03324]` |
| `L2.03325` | not read |

No Humans row holds raw 22 and no Units row holds 22 in parameter 55
(R2-ASSET-160). A raw row word therefore never gives 22.

**Confidence.** High for the 193 hits, the 59 candidates and the 15 word
moves. Medium for the sources: some rest on windows ending 0x10 bytes past
the site. Unknown for the 44 dword-only candidates, `L2.03325`, `L2.03323`
and the copies, any of which can carry 22.

**Unknown.** A window at each unclassified site settles it.

**Narrowed by the review.** The headline said "53 sites are not classified";
the table gives a source for eight of the nine unclassified word moves, so it
now says the 53 sites "carry values that are not shown". The sources are
known, the values they can carry are not.

### R2-ENGINE-637

Composed from R2-ENGINE-633, R2-ENGINE-635, R2-ENGINE-219, R2-ENGINE-526,
R2-ENGINE-625 and R2-SESSION-254.

1. At stage 30 an inn entry passes `0x301e0016` to the producer, which adds
   identity 22 when the owner lacks him.
2. TALK 22/30 adds mission 30 and sets 533 = 1, 553 = 2 (hire 2). It builds
   no actor.
3. The leave arm adds a controlled actor only from slot 773, which the
   literal stores set to 0 or 23 (R2-SESSION-254).
4. The last owner loop of the victory transition resets actors of class
   0x21..0x3f and detaches the rest (R2-ENGINE-526). Identity 22 has the hero
   class rule at Medium (R2-ENGINE-635), so that loop does not detach him.
   Whether he stays in the party is Unknown: R2-ENGINE-526 leaves the first
   owner loop's ten callees, `L2.01670`, slot +4, the world clear and the map
   deletion unread.
5. His death sends reason 3 when the guards of R2-ENGINE-625 hold: Session
   +0x74 zero (Medium), owner +0x2c zero, and a death that reaches the block
   (the callers are not censused). 44 of 46 mission texts per root carry
   `#failure3`.
6. A later inn entry with NPC 22 topic 40 (stage 40) or topic 62 (the
   continuation) adds him again only if he is absent.

**Confidence.** Medium: the weakest links are the town registration and
the class (R2-ENGINE-635) and the unclassified +0x14c stores
(R2-ENGINE-636). Unknown whether a dead actor leaves owner +0x24, and
whether any unread routine removes him.

**Unknown.** Whether the identity-22 actor is the companion the talk
presents: the talk text `npc22talk30` was not read. The same talk stores hire
2's availability 533 = 1 and town 553 = 2, and R2-SESSION-255 step 5 builds
hire 2 at mission entry when its selection 513 is set. Whether hire 2 is a
second character, the same character or excluded (the preregistered
alternative A3) is not shown.

**Unknown.** In the original: from a stage-30 town-2 save, enter the inn
and record the party before entry, after the page opens and after TALK
22/30, with hire 2 and the name shown for the talk. Then let identity 22 die
in mission 30, record the failure screen, and after a LOAD record the party.

No producer read removes him. The victory transition's last owner loop does not
detach a class 0x21..0x3f actor, and whether he stays is Unknown
(R2-ENGINE-526). His death sends reason 3 when the guards of R2-ENGINE-625
hold (Medium). Inn stage 40 or topic 62 adds him again when he is absent.

**Narrowed by the review.** The headline said "the stage-30 inn companion is
identity 22 ... victory keeps him, his death sends reason 3". The evidence
shows that the inn selector builds an actor with +0x14c = 22 (Medium for the
composed join), not that this actor is the character the talk presents. It
reads one predicate of the victory transition, not retention, and the death
guards are listed in item 5.

## The client fog stamp

Static reads of the owned EN and RU `allods2.exe` (raw x86 listings decoded
with Capstone from the plan of one generation reproduced byte for byte) and
measurements of both roots' `scenario.res:10.alm`. EN addresses unless RU
is named. "Client" is the object whose +0x80 holds the client map
(R2-ENGINE-615); "fog words" are the W x H words at client map +0xc
(R2-ENGINE-614). "Budget" is the accumulator of 41 x 41 DWORDs at client
+0x17e4, row stride 0xa4, indexed [i][j] with i the x offset and j the y
offset plus 20. "Equal after masking" means equal once every hex number of
five or more digits is masked.

### R2-ENGINE-643

Stamp `L2.03326`: one bounded CFG of 140 instructions. It returns unless
the owner gate (R2-ENGINE-648) passes and word +0x10a is nonzero, sets
client +0xdc = 1, runs the walk `L2.03329` (R2-ENGINE-645) and writes the
figure (R2-ENGINE-646).

Census over the EN image:

| Reference | Population | Result |
|---|---|---|
| E8/E9 rel32 to `L2.03326` | every byte offset of executable sections | one, `L2.03330` in `L2.03327` |
| raw DWORD `L2.03326` | every byte offset of every section | seven `.rdata` slots: `L2.03331`, `L2.03332`, `L2.03333`, `L2.03334`, `L2.03335`, `L2.03336`, `L2.03337` |
| raw DWORD `L2.03327` | every section | `L2.03338`, `L2.03339` |

Tables read at 24 DWORDs: slot +0x48 (index 18) is `L2.03327` in
`L2.03340` and `L2.03341`, whose +0x20/+0x24 slots read unit collection
`L2.02969`, and `L2.03326` in `L2.03342` (statics, collection `L2.03005`),
`L2.03343` and `L2.03344` (size slots `L2.03345`/`L2.03346`, unread). The
other four stamp slots sit in tables whose starts (`L2.03347`, `L2.03348`,
`L2.03349`, `L2.03350`) are inferred from the slot position, not read, so
the class of those four is unknown. Narrowed by the review: the claim
"units and statics" rests on `L2.03342` read as statics and, through the
wrapper `L2.03327`, `L2.03340` and `L2.03341` read as units.

Second route, narrowed in by the review. Slot +0x44 of the same tables
holds `L2.03328` in `L2.03342`, `L2.03343` and `L2.03344`
(`code/en-vt-*.txt`, words `L2.03351`, `L2.03352`, `L2.03353`), and the
wrapper `L2.03354` in `L2.03340` and `L2.03341` (`L2.03355`, `L2.03356`).
The review's raw DWORD scan of `L2.03328` finds seven slots, one word
below each stamp slot outside the unit tables; its single E8 caller is the
wrapper `L2.03357`, which tests byte +0x184 below 3. The body of
`L2.03328` ends at `L2.03358`, just before the stamp. It applies the same
two gates as the stamp (owner gate `L2.02954`, word +0x10a nonzero) and
calls virtual slot +0x48 at `L2.03359` when (obj+0x54 & 0x1f) and
(obj+0x58 & 0x1f) both equal 0x10 and obj +8/+0xc differ from +0xc8/+0xcc,
the two words the stamp stores (R2-ENGINE-646). The unit update slot +0x3c
(`L2.03360`) calls slot +0x44 at `L2.03361` on its idle path ([obj+0xa8] is
0, byte +0x184 below 5), and the tick calls slot +0x3c of every client
object on every client tick (`L2.03362`, `code/en-tick-L2.01389.txt`). A unit
whose cell word differs from its last stamped one can therefore be stamped
on any tick, not only on every 32nd. In the base constructor window the
review read (`L2.03363..L2.03364`) +8 and +0xc are stored as 0 and no store
to +0x54, +0x58, +0xc8 or +0xcc appears, so whether a fresh hero differs
from its last stamped cell on its first update is unread.

Cadence: the client handler `L2.03365` (raw DWORD at `L2.03366`) first
calls `L2.00913` and takes the message switch only when it returns 0
(`L2.03367..L2.03368`, read by the review), and maps message 0x401 through
byte table `L2.03369` (entry 0 is 0) and jump table
`L2.03370` to `L2.03371`, which calls the tick `L2.01389`, whose only E8
caller is `L2.03372`. The tick adds 1 to client +0xa88 and then calls
`L2.01068` when `[L2.00989]` is 0 and +0xa88 & 0x1f is 0. +0xa88 has two
stores (raw DWORD 0xa88, every section): 0 in the client constructor
(`L2.03373`) and the tick's add. `L2.01068` has one E8 caller (`L2.03374`)
and no raw DWORD reference. It sets client +0xdc and +0xe0 to 1, ANDs
0xbfff into all W x H fog words and calls slot +0x48 of each object of
client +0x9d0 through `L2.03035`/`L2.03036`. Nine `push 0x401` patterns
exist; `L2.03375` and `L2.03376` follow the server tick `L2.03120` and the
pump `L2.00466(0x64)`, `L2.03377` follows the pump; each is sent through
[app+0xcc] slot +0x48. The other six are not classified.

**Confidence.** High for the bodies and the census rows as stated, and for
the vtable words and the tick's call of slot +0x3c in the listings. Medium
for the second route: the bodies of `L2.03328`, `L2.03354` and `L2.03360`
and the scan of `L2.03328` were read by the review and are not in the
evidence directory. Medium that no other path stamps: a call through a
register to slot +0x48 of an object has no fixed target to scan, and four
of the seven vtable starts (`L2.03347`, `L2.03348`, `L2.03349`, `L2.03350`)
are inferred from the slot position, not read. Medium that the posted 0x401
reaches `L2.03365`: the dispatcher between [app+0xcc] and the client
handler is unread. What the evidence excludes is an earlier stamp by the
refresh `L2.01068`; it does not exclude `L2.03328`.

**Unknown.** Real time per client tick. The initial values of +0x54, +0x58,
+0xc8 and +0xcc of a client object, and so whether `L2.03328` stamps a
fresh hero before the 32nd tick; whether a unit's creation or move calls

### R2-ENGINE-644

Walk `L2.03329` stores (movsx word obj+0x10a >> (8 - s)) + (1 << (s - 1))
at client +0x2504, the centre [20][20], after zeroing 0x1a44 bytes of the
budget. s is client +0x3f50 and K = 1 << s is client +0x3f4c; the client
constructor stores s = 7 at `L2.03378` and K at `L2.03379`, the only
stores in raw DWORD scans of 0x3f50 and 0x3f4c. With s = 7 the seed is
(sight >> 1) + 64.

Of the 26 hits of the raw DWORD 0x10a scan (disp32 forms of +0x10a only),
the word stores are: `L2.03380`
stores 0 (base constructor); `L2.03381` copies it from the argument
(`L2.03382`); `L2.03383` stores argument word +0xa4 (`R2.0075`, E8 callers
`L2.03384`, `L2.03385`, `L2.03386` in the client pump, `L2.03387`,
`L2.03388` and `L2.03389` in the map builder); `L2.03390` stores the next
message word when message flags +0x14 have 0x40000; `L2.03391` stores the
Buildings collection `L2.03202` lookup (key, 2) shifted left by 8, and
`L2.03392` a lookup shifted left by 8; `L2.03393` and `L2.03394` are in
unread functions.

R2-ENGINE-290 gives sight word +0xa4 = trunc(((Mind + Reaction)/25 + 4) ·
256): 1648 for the unmodified Start_MF template row 40/36/25/17
(R2-ASSET-076; the delivered hero differs by its attribute choice and
items, R2-SESSION-144) and 1617 for the saved heroes, 41/34/24/17 in 0000/0001 and 19/15/43/25 in the other seven EN
saves (R2-SESSION-236), both with Mind + Reaction 58. The seeds are 888 and
872; ScanRange 6 as 6 · 256 would give 832.

**Confidence.** High for the walk's arithmetic, s and K. The list of +0x10a
writers is the raw DWORD list: a block copy or a store through a computed
address would not appear, and two writers (`L2.03393`, `L2.03394`) are in
unread functions (narrowed by the review). Medium that the hero's client object gets +0x10a from argument +0xa4 or a
message word equal to its sight word: the copy's argument and the message
sender are unread, and item modifiers may change the word.

### R2-ENGINE-645

Walk `L2.03329` (197 instructions) with cell test `L2.03395` (78), bounds
`L2.03396` and tables `L2.03397`:

1. Origin ox = obj+0x38 - 20, oy = obj+0x3c - 20; h0 = movsx byte
   plane[(obj+0x3c) · W + obj+0x38], plane = client map +0x10 (`L2.03398`),
   W = client +0x84.
2. For r = 1..19, for k = -r..r, the cells (20+k, 20-r), (20+k, 20+r),
   (20-r, 20+k), (20+r, 20-k) are tested only when `L2.03396(ox+i, oy+j)`
   accepts them: 7 <= x < W - 7 and 7 <= y < H - 7. After a ring in which
   no tested cell stays positive, the walk ends.
3. Cell (i, j): (dx, dy) = the byte pair at client +0xac0 [i·0x52 + j·2];
   budget[i][j] = budget[i+dx][j+dy] - (cost[i][j] + movsx
   plane[oy·W + ox + j·W + i] - h0); cost is the word at client +0x3228
   [i·0x52 + j·2].
4. Tables, for a, b = 0..20 and each quadrant: (dx, dy) points one step
   back along x when b < a >> 1, along y when b > 2a, else diagonally;
   cost = ftol(sqrt(a² + b²) · K / max(a, b)) through `L2.02707` and
   `L2.02708`: 128 on the axes, 181 on the diagonal. The tail sets [21][20]
   to (-1, 0) and [19][20] to (1, 0).

A height above h0 costs its difference; one below gives budget back. The
plane is signed bytes, one per fog cell, at the same index. The map builder
`L2.01385` copies W x H bytes from ALM asset +0x14 to client map +0x10;
the ALM reader `L2.02484` fills asset +0x14 in switch entry 2 of table
`L2.02737` (13 entries) and +0x10 in entry 3, switching on the record
header dword at [ebp-0x34] with the payload size at [ebp-0x38].

**Confidence.** High for the arithmetic and the copy. Medium that the
switch value is the record's typeId and so that the plane is ALM type 2:
the header reader `L2.02735` is unread; the 20-byte header copy at
[ebp-0x40] puts typeId at [ebp-0x34]. The three EN saves' 154 cells match
type 2 heights, not type 3 (R2-ENGINE-647). Medium for truncation in
`L2.02708` (unread); rounding gives the same figure at 11/41 for seeds
888 and 872.

### R2-ENGINE-646

After the walk the stamp sets cx = obj+0x38 + slot+0x20()/2 and cy =
obj+0x3c + slot+0x24()/2 (cdq, sub, sar 1: division toward zero). For i, j
= 0..40 with budget[i][j] > 0 it ORs 0xc000 into the fog words idx, idx+1,
idx+1+W and idx+W, idx = (cy - 20 + j) · W + (cx - 20 + i), with no bounds
test. It then stores obj+8 at +0xc8 and obj+0xc at +0xcc.

The walk runs from (+0x38, +0x3c) without the size term, so the figure
lies on the walk centre for sizes 0 and 1 and one cell to +x and +y for
sizes 2 and 3. Unit size slots `L2.03399` and `L2.03400` both return
record +0xf0 of collection `L2.02969`, a square body; static slots
`L2.03401`/`L2.03402` return record +0x10/+0x14 of `L2.03005`. The refresh
clears 0x4000 only; 0x8000 stays set. The draw routines `L2.03403` and
`L2.03404` AND each of the four words of an object's 2 x 2 block at
(x >> 8, y >> 8) with 0xc000, OR the four results and draw the object only
when that union equals 0xc000 (`cmp ecx, 0xc000`; `L2.03405..L2.03406`):
one word with bit 0x8000 and another with bit 0x4000 pass. The unit
routine also tests byte +0x184, +0x1b8 and the owner gate. The same union
sets [obj+0x7c] at `L2.03407..L2.03408`. For a block the stamp wrote, the
union and "all four words hold 0xc000" agree; they differ at the border of
an area uncovered earlier (0x8000 only) next to a lit cell (narrowed by the
review).

**Confidence.** High for the writes, the centre arithmetic and the size
slots. Medium that +0x38/+0x3c is the cell of the object's position: no
writer of either was found (a disp8 store escapes the raw DWORD scan); the
client pump stores +8/+0xc as cell << 8 + 0x80. Medium for the hero's
size: record +0xf0 for its class was not read.

### R2-ENGINE-647

Derived by `fogdata` from R2-ENGINE-644..646 and `10.alm` (R2-ASSET-162)
for hero cell 11/41 (the four EN saves, R2-SESSION-236) with a one-cell
body, type 2 heights and truncating costs. The walk stops after ring 7.

| Seed | Sight | Lit budget cells | Uncovered | Row-major runs | Rows |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 888 | 1648 | 130 | 155 | 29 | 14 |
| 872 | 1617 | 129 | 154 | 29 | 14 |
| 832 | ScanRange 6 | 120 | 145 | 29 | 14 |

Every seed, rounding and height source gives runs of 4 cells in -x (to
x = 7, the walk's bound), 7 in +x, 6 in -y and 7 in +y from the hero cell;
the figure spans x 7..18 and y 35..48. The three EN saves at 11/41 hold
154 set cells in 29 runs of 6400 (R2-SESSION-244), the cells 0x8000 marks
(R2-ENGINE-614); compared by count and runs, of 18 variants only seed 872
with type 2 heights and seed 832 with no heights give that pair. The tick
adds 1 before its test, so a counter at 0 makes the first refresh
`L2.01068` the 32nd tick. That holds for the refresh only: the second
route `L2.03328` (R2-ENGINE-643) can stamp a unit on any tick, and the
first frame is Unknown. game9999, at 11/41 with 0 set cells, fits a save
before the first stamp.

**Confidence.** Medium: the hero's anchor and size (R2-ENGINE-646), its
delivered seed (R2-ENGINE-644) and that its owner passes the gate
(R2-ENGINE-648); whether the client constructor runs per mission is
unread. Medium for the figure once stamped, 155 or 154 cells. Unknown for
the time of the first stamp: the evidence excludes an earlier stamp by the
refresh only (narrowed by the review).

**Unknown.** The time of the first stamp, and whether `L2.03328` stamps
before the 32nd tick (R2-ENGINE-643). A run of the original: a new hero
left at the unmodified Start_MF template, mission 1, saved at once, again a
few ticks later and again after 32 or more ticks without moving. If only
the refresh stamps, the Fog data would hold 0 cells, then 155 cells in 29
runs over x 7..18, y 35..48; a nonzero first save names the other route.
